On 20 held-out prompts, hand-scored for accuracy, topicality and specificity (maximum 120), the base model, continuation adapter, instruction adapter and instruction adapter with retrieval scored 42, 56, 84 and 81. The retrieval score reflects a corrected index-leakage issue. A paired test supports the instruction-tuning gain but finds no retrieval benefit on this set. Accuracy remained low: 14/40 without retrieval and 16/40 with it. A second evaluation used prompts from passages excluded from both instruction-data splits, addressing selection leakage in round one. It confirmed the instruction-tuning gain (p=0.0001 and p=0.0002) and found that retrieval significantly helped the base model, but not the instruction adapter.

papers.title: Weak and Strong Moments of Log-Concave Measures
papers.abstract: Let $X\in\mathbb{R}^d$ be a log-concave random vector, and let $N$ be a seminorm on $\mathbb{R}^d$. For $p\ge 1$, we show that $\|N(X)\|_p$ is at most $\mathbb{E} N(X)+C s_p$, where $s_p$ is the supremum of $\|u(X)\|_p$ over all linear functionals $u$ satisfying $|u(x)|\le N(x)$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. A choice for $C$ is $2+2e$. This bound implies Latała's conjecture on weak and strong moments.

papers.title: AscendGYM: A Cost-Aware Kernel Optimization Benchmark for Real-World Workloads on Ascend NPUs
papers.abstract: Kernel optimization is essential for efficient large language model (LLM) training and inference on Ascend NPUs. Existing Ascend kernel benchmarks primarily focus on kernel generation, with less emphasis on the ability of agents to optimize existing implementations under input configurations drawn from real workloads. To address this requirement, we introduce AscendGYM, a benchmark whose initial suite comprises 48 kernels across three difficulty levels. Each kernel is paired with test cases whose data types and tensor shapes are collected from real-world training and inference tasks. Consequently, performance improvements on AscendGYM map directly to the corresponding workloads. In terms of usability, two evaluation modes are supported in AscendGYM: model evaluation and model-harness evaluation. The kernel optimization capabilities of both trained models and custom agents are allowed to be measured. It provides a complete execution environment that closely reproduces how Ascend kernels are invoked in practical pipelines. For model evaluation, it additionally includes a built-in harness equipped with search orchestration and experience accumulation. Finally, we propose a new metric, the Speedup-Token Score (STS), which quantifies performance gains relative to token cost. By jointly considering speedup and cost, STS enables the assessment of practical kernel optimization capability of a model or harness under an acceptable budget. AscendGYM is available at https://github.com/SLAI-AITP/AscendGYM.

papers.title: Solutions of the set-theoretic quantum Yang-Baxter equation arising from posets
papers.abstract: Victoria Lebed observed that the map $(x, \, y) \mapsto (\min\{x, \, y\}, \, \max\{x, \, y\})$ on a totally ordered set is an idempotent solution of the braid equation. We extend this example in several directions, by constructing four families of solutions of the braid equation associated to posets. First, for a given poset $P$, the map $R_P$ which sorts the comparable pairs and fixes the incomparable ones is an idempotent solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is the automorphism group of the poset $P$. Combined with the classical theorem of Birkhoff, this shows that every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of an idempotent solution of the braid equation of the form $(P, \, R_P)$, for some poset $P$. Moreover, $R_P \cong R_Q$ if and only if $P \cong Q$, and the solutions of the form $R_P$ are exactly the idempotent solutions of the braid equation which permute the components of each pair. Secondly, we classify all the solutions $R$ of the braid equation on an arbitrary set $X$ such that $R(x, \, y) \in \{(x, \, y), \, (y, \, x)\}$ for all $x$, $y\in X$: they are exactly the solutions $R_{\mathcal{P}}$ associated to the decompositions $\mathcal{P}$ of $X$ into posets. Finally, we associate to any finite poset $P$ two involutive solutions $D_P$ and $E_P$ of the braid equation, whose automorphism groups are $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^P \rtimes {\rm Aut} (P)$ and, if $P$ is connected and has at least two elements, the group of automorphisms and anti-automorphisms of $P$.

papers.title: Mobility-Aware Task Offloading in Mobile Edge Computing-Empowered Space-Air-Ground Integrated Internet-of-Things Networks
papers.abstract: Mobile edge computing (MEC)-empowered spaceair-ground integrated Internet-of-Things (IoT) networks (SAGIINs) provide a promising solution for computation-intensive tasks generated by mobile IoT devices (IDs). However, task offloading in SAGIINs is challenging due to time-varying IDto-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) channels, intermittent LEO satellite service availability, and the coupling among UAV trajectory, communication, computation, and energy decisions. This paper investigates an energy-efficient task offloading and UAV trajectory planning problem in an MEC-empowered SAGIIN, where one UAV acts as both an aerial relay and an MEC server, and multiple LEO satellites provide supplementary computing resources. The UAV trajectory planning, task splitting, and computing resource allocation are jointly optimized to minimize the total system energy consumption under task completion, communication, computation, flight region, and satellite service window constraints. The resulting non-convex problem is decomposed into a UAV trajectory planning subproblem and a task splitting and computing resource allocation subproblem. To solve the former, a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-assisted large language model (LLM)-enhanced deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm, termed RLD, is proposed. The latter is shown to be convex and can be solved by using CVXPY for a given UAV trajectory. A weighted retrieval score is further designed to balance ID mobility-pattern similarity and historical UAV trajectory energy performance. Simulation results show that RLD completes all computational tasks in previously unseen test scenarios while consuming less total energy than the benchmark algorithms.

papers.title: TS-GEAR: Taobao Shangou GEnerative Ad Retrieval
papers.abstract: On-demand delivery platforms such as DoorDash and Uber Eats impose a constraint absent in traditional e-commerce: merchants beyond the user's delivery range are invalid candidates rather than merely low-ranked. Generative retrieval has recently shown strong potential in large-scale retrieval systems. Adapting it to this setting, however, poses three challenges. First, existing semantic IDs encode geography only as a soft signal, so reachability can only rely on a non-differentiable post-generation hard truncation. Second, user preferences vary substantially across both regions and queries, so aggregating historical behaviors without conditioning on geography and the current query yields biased interest estimates. Third, the retrieved candidate set is evaluated by its collective value, yet autoregressive training scores each sequence independently, with no set-level signal to discourage redundant near-duplicates. To address the challenges, we propose TS-GEAR, a unified generative retrieval framework for on-demand delivery: (1) Geo-Semantic ID splits merchant identifiers into geographic prefixes and semantic suffixes, making reachability a prediction target rather than a post-hoc filter; (2) Query-Geo Target Attention aggregates historical behaviors using the real-time query and location as dual targets, while encoding each behavior's own location into its attention key; (3) GMPO (Group Marginal Policy Optimization) rewrites advantages using a deduplicated group reward and marginal advantage within GRPO, avoiding auxiliary diversity objectives. Deployed online with a lightweight 0.1B backbone, TS-GEAR serves over 150 million queries per day in the search advertising pipeline of Taobao Shangou, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art generative retrieval methods on both HitRate and geographic validity, and achieving 3.8% gains in ad impressions and 4.2% in ad revenue.

papers.title: FreeOcc: Decoupling Ego-Motion for Efficient 4D Occupancy Forecasting via Continuous Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Current 4D occupancy world models use heavy cross-attention or deep recurrence to disentangle ego-motion from scene dynamics. This requires significant computational capacity. However, this effort is largely redundant since the ego-vehicle's intended future motion is provided by the downstream motion planner. We present FreeOcc, a lightweight continuous-time world model that introduces explicit $SE(2)$ geometric decoupling into a conditional flow-matching framework. By mathematically factoring out self-motion, we create a purely dynamic feature space. This space supports attention-free temporal fusion and allows physics-constrained ODEs to operate strictly on residual agent kinematics. To maximize deployment efficiency, FreeOcc introduces an uncertainty-aware blending mechanism. This routes well-observed voxels to a single-pass decoder, reserving the ODE solver exclusively for ambiguous, high-uncertainty regions. Requiring only 28.3M parameters-roughly 40% of comparable models-our optimal ensemble mode (FreeOcc-E) runs at 27 FPS. On nuScenes, FreeOcc achieves state-of-the-art forecasting performance with a 0.47 m Near Field Chamfer Distance (NFCD) and 32.1% mIoU. Furthermore, the model transfers zero-shot to SemanticKITTI. It also proves highly robust, retaining 92.8% of its ideal mIoU under significant sensor packet loss and timestamp jitter.

papers.title: Liouville systems I: Blow-up analysis and orthogonal decomposition
papers.abstract: We study blow-up solutions of generalized Liouville systems on a closed surface at and near critical parameter hypersurfaces. Under a Morse assumption on the reduced functional, we establish the following results. First, we introduce amplitude variables in the approximate manifold and prove that every sequence of blow-up solutions at a fixed critical parameter, or along an admissible sequence from the lower side, admits a unique minimizing decomposition up to permutation. The remainder converges to zero and is orthogonal to the center, scale, and amplitude directions. The concentration scales are comparable, the limiting configuration satisfies the scale balance conditions, and the amplitudes vanish after multiplication by the logarithmic scale. Second, we determine the leading parameter defect in both critical decay regimes and prove that, along each fixed admissible path, all sufficiently large solutions lie in finitely many disjoint bubbling neighborhoods. Finally, assuming the leading coefficient is nonzero at every balanced critical configuration, the solution set at the fixed critical parameter is compact. These results provide the analytic foundation for studying the resonant degree via critical points at infinity.

papers.title: Equivariant Deep Learning in Direct-Product Space for Electronic-Structure Hamiltonian Prediction
papers.abstract: Most existing equivariant architectures for Hamiltonian prediction propagate features in direct-sum spaces of irreducible spherical tensors, whereas the target Hamiltonian is naturally an operator block in a direct-product representation over local orbital and spin bases. This representation mismatch fragments contiguous Hamiltonian blocks, obscures direct manipulation of orbital couplings, and organizes features into irregular angular-momentum components that require numerous transformations and are poorly aligned with efficient hardware execution and memory management. To address both the representation mismatch and computational bottleneck, we propose DP-Learner, an equivariant learning framework that performs message passing directly on Hamiltonian-like operator blocks in the direct-product space. Theoretically, we propose Lie-generator-based directional embedding and invariantly weighted left--right products and contractions that preserve equivariance to SO(3), SU(2), and spatial inversions, without explicit Clebsch--Gordan decomposition or inverse reconstruction. Methodologically, we instantiate this principle as a Transformer architecture, in which Hamiltonian-like feature matrices or tensors evolve through equivariant operators in the direct-product space, while non-linear invariant scalar routing controls structured gating over matrix units, directional propagation, attention, and environment-embedded context interactions. We further construct MP-HAM-110K, a large-scale Hamiltonian dataset comprising more than 110,000 material structures covering 68 elements with both Hamiltonian and wavefunction data. Experiments on MP-HAM-110K and Materials-HAM-SOC demonstrate that DP-Learner dramatically improves Hamiltonian prediction accuracy and inference efficiency over the state-of-the-art method.

papers.title: When Scores Conflict with Preferences: Pre-Alignment Diagnosis and Adaptive Correction of Constraint Drift in DPO
papers.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is increasingly used in settings where pairwise preferences coexist with pointwise criteria such as response length, answer correctness, or safety scores. When the two disagree, standard DPO treats pairs whose preferred output scores worse on the pointwise criterion (conflict pairs) in the same way as the remaining (matching) pairs. We characterize a systematic failure mode, constraint drift: for sufficiently small updates, conflict pairs tend to increase constraint cost while matching pairs tend to repair it, and the net change depends on their balance. This balance yields a closed-form pre-alignment diagnostic, $ρ^{*}_{\mathrm{eq}}$, computable from dataset statistics, that indicates whether a dataset is self-correcting or requires intervention. Building on this diagnostic, we propose Conflict-aware DPO (CoDPO), which down-weights conflict pairs with a strength set from $ρ^{*}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ rather than tuned, and adds an adaptive margin shift that addresses residual drift during training. Empirically, drift grows monotonically with conflict exposure on the conflict-dominated domains, and the intervention decision given by $ρ^{*}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ matches the observed drift on every domain, including one that it identifies as self-correcting. On all four domains of the main comparison, CoDPO reduces drift while largely preserving the preference learning of vanilla DPO. Compared with hard filtering and recent constrained and multi-objective baselines, CoDPO also achieves a more favorable drift-preference trade-off.

papers.title: The Maximum Second Zagreb Spectral Radius of Trees, Unicyclic Graphs and Bicyclic Graphs
papers.abstract: The second Zagreb matrix of a graph $G$ is $Z(G)=D(G)A(G)D(G)$, where $D(G)$ and $A(G)$ are the degree matrix and the adjacency matrix of $G$. For many degree-based weighted adjacency matrices, the trees, unicyclic graphs and bicyclic graphs with the largest spectral radius have a vertex adjacent to all others, and Mei et al. conjectured this for every such matrix on unicyclic graphs. Jiang et al. showed that $Z(G)$ is a counterexample. We prove that, for $q\in\{0,1,2\}$ and every $n\ge4$, the connected graph of order $n$ and cyclomatic number $q$ maximizing the spectral radius of $Z(G)$ is unique, and is obtained from two adjacent vertices with $q$ common neighbours by attaching $n-q-2$ pendent vertices to them as evenly as possible. The only exceptions are the star for $q=0$ and $n\le7$, and the triangle with one pendent vertex at each vertex for $q=1$ and $n=6$. This confirms a conjecture of Jiang et al.\ and all three parts of a conjecture of Shen and Shan for this matrix, with best possible thresholds on $n$. For $n\ge8$, the maximum value is $\lfloor (n+q)^2/4\rfloor+(n+q)/2+7q-2+O(1/n)$, whereas the star gives only $(n-1)^{3/2}$. A key tool is a determinant criterion that reduces spectral comparisons to sign conditions on explicit polynomials.

papers.title: EP-LVMQA: Evidence-Preserving Coarse-to-Fine Localization for Low-Quality Long Video Moment Question Answering
papers.abstract: Long instructional videos are increasingly used in medical education, industrial training, and procedural knowledge transfer, yet their evidence is often incomplete or unreliable: subtitles may be missing, ASR noisy, OCR sparse, and decisive actions briefly shown without narration. Existing VideoQA systems typically return labels or free-form text, making answer support difficult to inspect. We study Long Video Moment Question Answering (LVMQA), where a system returns timestamped answer-supporting evidence. We propose EP-LVMQA, an evidence-preserving coarse-to-fine framework comprising an Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Evidence Timeline, a Coarse Evidence Planner, and an Evidence-Conditioned Fine Localizer. An evidence card transfers planner scores, matched cues, source-confidence proxies, modality-specific evidence, neighboring context, and a temporal prior between the latter two modules. On MedVidQA, EP-LVMQA achieves 26.1 R1@0.5 and 31.8 mIoU, improving the strongest non-ours results by 6.3 and 5.1 points. It raises Suff.@2 and Ver.@2 to 25.4 and 22.6, gains of 9.5 and 8.8 points. Under matched low-quality perturbations, average relative degradation is reduced from the strongest non-ours value of 14.6% to 11.1%. On Ego4D-NLQ and QVHighlights, EP-LVMQA remains broadly comparable to established task-specific localization methods.

papers.title: Galois-modular obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings
papers.abstract: In this article we establish new obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings by combining the values of irreducible characters of the Grothendieck ring with the Galois symmetry of the induced unit object $I(1)$ in the Drinfeld center. As a result, we show that a near-group ring of type $G+m$, where $G$ is an abelian group and both $|G|$ and $m$ are odd, can only categorify if $m=|G|$.

papers.title: Quadratic Hubbard trees, automata, and ray connections
papers.abstract: We describe an algorithm that, given a postcritically finite quadratic polynomial, outputs a finite state machine whose regular language is the set of angles whose dynamical rays land on the Hubbard tree, generalizing an example of Milnor. We do this by extracting orbit portraits from angled internal addresses, and constructing a suitable Markov partition of angle intervals. A main application is computing direct ray connections between Hubbard trees in matings of quadratic polynomials, and understanding when ray connections between the trees first appear when moving along veins of the Mandelbrot set. If one of the mating parameters is fixed, we prove that first ray connections are picked up at parabolic parameters or tips of veins. We also prove that the locus of parameter pairs in two given veins for which there are no ray connections between the trees is open. Additionally, we show that there are no ray connections between small Julia sets in matings of locally connected rabbit tunings.

papers.title: Obstruction to local entropy laws on arbitrary black-hole cuts in five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity
papers.abstract: We study local entropy laws on arbitrary cuts of event horizons in five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity, treated as an exact theory. No covariant local entropy can both reproduce the stationary black-hole entropy and be nondecreasing between every ordered pair of cuts, provided its density is smooth on an invariant open set of off-shell metric and cut jets containing a flat planar cut and every cut used in the argument. No global bound on derivative order is assumed. The counterexamples to the second law are vacuum black holes perturbed by a gravitational wave, with a strongly hyperbolic formulation near the relevant horizon interval and its stationary future. Shear makes the intrinsic curvature of a cut depend on its bending. The stationary entropy fixes the coefficient of this curvature term, and local corrections cannot cancel its response to cut bending. The obstruction appears at second order in wave amplitude on a smooth horizon, without a merger or topology change.

papers.title: Unsatz: Evaluating Scientific Discovery Without a Given Ansatz
papers.abstract: Before a scientist fits any parameter, they must decide what the model contains: which quantities exist, which are hidden, how they interact, and how they are measured. Physicists call such a trial form an ansatz. Benchmarks for automated equation discovery mostly supply it, by fixing the variables, a library of candidate terms, or a law to be modified. We introduce Unsatz, a benchmark in which an LLM agent must construct the ansatz itself. Each task is a simulated system, generated from a private seed as a program in a small modeling language: ordinary, delay, or partial differential equations, discrete maps, static and causal models, or stochastic processes, possibly with latent states, distorted sensors, and uninformative measurement channels. The agent buys experiments within a budget, writes candidate programs in the same language, obtains their coefficients from the benchmark's fitter, and is scored only on how its final program predicts experiments it never saw: conditions outside the ordinary ranges, interventions, and longer runs. Across 80 systems in 20 domains, nine language models solve between 21% and 60%. On the 64 deterministic systems, the two strongest agents solve 39 and 31, and classical and neural baselines together 14. The difficulty lies in finding the structure, not in the data: in 55% of the agents' failed investigations, the experiments they bought suffice once the true program is given with unknown coefficients. We also start agents on a related system from the program of a first system, either the one they discovered or the true one; agents holding a correct program solve the related system in 15 of 42 investigations, and agents without one in 5 of 64. Stronger agents make fewer unscientific errors; beyond these, agents that find a system's variables still miss how they act, and prefer revisions that lower the training error to ones that predict better.

papers.title: Convergence in law of the maximum of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
papers.abstract: Let $T \to \infty$, let $τ$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$, and let $σ= σ(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. We establish the convergence in law of the recentered maximum of $\log|ζ(σ+ \mathrm{i}τ+ \mathrm{i} h)|$ over $I_θ = \smash{[ - (\log T)^θ,(\log T)^θ]}$, for every fixed $θ> 0$. Under explicit conditions on the displacement $σ- 1/2$, the recentered maximum converges to a Gumbel distribution with scale parameter $1/(2\sqrt{1 + θ})$. The recentering is an exact upper quantile of the one-point law of the associated Haar field $F_{h}^{\mathrm{H}} = \Re\sum_{p^{j}\leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(jp^{j(σ+ \mathrm{i} h)})$, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. The positive constant in the limiting distribution is characterized by a Gaussian process describing the limiting microscopic increments of the Haar field around a high point. The result is established without the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: UA-Depth: Uncertainty-Aware Depth Restoration for Material-Agnostic Object Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation requires accurate metric depth, yet commodity RGB-D cameras often fail on non-Lambertian objects such as transparent, reflective, and translucent materials, producing holes, structured noise, and biased depth. Most restoration methods produce only a single depth map, treating noisy and reliable regions uniformly for downstream tasks while ignoring regional uncertainty. We present UA-Depth, an uncertainty-aware depth restoration framework that iteratively co-refines depth and pixel-wise uncertainty, and uses uncertainty-gated features to suppress unreliable cues for stable updates. To strengthen zero-shot behavior, UA-Depth leverages a frozen depth foundation model as a prior to initialize missing or unreliable depth, and applies two-stage MAD-weighted log-depth scale normalization to reduce outlier bias in relative-to-metric alignment. We introduce an eight-dataset zero-shot benchmark across diverse scenes, materials, and sensors. Across these benchmarks, UA-Depth achieves the best mean rank among representative baselines, with particularly strong gains on datasets dominated by transparent and reflective objects. Beyond depth metrics, we demonstrate downstream improvements in category-level 6D pose estimation and 6D grasp synthesis by exploiting the predicted uncertainty. \emph{Code, models, and data for training and evaluation will be released upon publication.}

papers.title: Mathematical modeling to study combination strategies for neural stem cell therapy in glioblastoma
papers.abstract: Neural stem cells (NSCs) are a promising treatment platform due to their ability to cross the restrictive blood-brain barrier and migrate toward damaged regions of the brain. These properties can be leveraged to target brain tumors, as NSCs can infiltrate tumor lesions and deliver therapeutic agents such as drugs, oncolytic viruses, and genetic materials. Despite the advantages of NSCs, translational challenges remain, including patient-specific chemotactic signaling and immune responses, variability in migration and localization at tumor sites, and optimization of delivery strategies. In this work, we focus on intranasal delivery of NSCs and combination strategies for the treatment of brain cancer. To investigate strategies for improving NSC arrival at the tumor site, we developed a hybrid mathematical model of NSC migration that couples an agent-based model with a partial differential equation, where cell motion is guided by the spatial dynamics of chemoattractants. Using data collected from a murine model and our mathematical model, we {investigate treatment-motivated downstream effects associated with three combination strategies:} (1) IL-10 pretreatment, (2) CXCL12 pretreatment, and (3) radiotherapy. We find that IL-10 pretreatment improves NSC arrival numbers at tumor only under the Gaussian chemoattractant profile, whereas CXCL12 pretreatment moderately improves arrival numbers when the tumor is located in the anterior brain. Radiotherapy significantly enhances the tumor arrival under uniform profiles. These simulation studies suggest that both treatment strategies and chemoattractant distribution influence intranasal NSC delivery, and the proposed model can be used to predict how targeted modulation of chemotactic signaling and tissue-guided migration may improve delivery outcomes.

papers.title: The spin-transfer inverse Faraday effect in Au/YIG thin film bilayers
papers.abstract: The inverse Faraday effect (IFE) (the generation of an effective magnetic field in a material upon irradiation with circularly polarized light) offers a pathway to ultrafast, non-thermal control of spin dynamics. In metallic/ferromagnetic-insulator (NM/FMI) bilayers, IFE-driven spin polarization in the metallic layer can be an alternative to generate magnon excitations in the magnetic insulator which otherwise would be inaccessible with photon energies below the insulator bandgap, but this avenue has remained mostly unexplored. In this work, we investigate the regime of spin-transfer via IFE in Au/YIG bilayers, by means of ultrafast time-resolved magneto-optical experiments. Understanding the mechanism of this spin-transfer IFE in these NM/FMI heterostructures is crucial for several reasons: it elucidates the fundamental coupling between light's angular momentum and collective spin modes at buried interfaces, it enables all-optical generation and manipulation of pure spin currents, and it paves the way toward THz-frequency spintronic devices leveraging the insulator's long magnon lifetimes.

papers.title: I$_4$ complex acting as near-infrared emitter with a quantum memory in silicon
papers.abstract: Silicon color centers emitting in the near infrared offer a route to spin--photon interfaces compatible with mature complementary metal--oxide--semiconductor fabrication. A key unresolved candidate is the X-line at 1039.7 meV in the photoluminescence (PL) spectrum, long attributed to a complex of four self-interstitials (I$_4$), yet whose microscopic structure and spin properties have remained controversial and uncharacterized at a predictive level. Using hybrid-functional (HSE06) density functional theory, we unambiguously establish the bare I$_4$ complex as the origin of the X-line: our calculations quantitatively reproduce the zero-phonon line, the complete phonon sideband structure---identifying the prominent secondary peaks as one- and two-phonon replicas of strongly coupled quasi-local modes---and the EPR hyperfine constants. The charge transition level is found at VBM$+$0.08~eV, conclusively ruling out the previously proposed association with the B3 EPR center and its correlated deep donor level. Most significantly, we identify a metastable spin-1 triplet excited state separated from the singlet by $\sim$1.6~meV, consistent with the NL51 EPR signal. The $D_{2d}$ symmetry of the defect suppresses intersystem crossing and phosphorescence by first-order spin--orbit coupling, implying an exceptionally long spin--lattice relaxation time. Combined with a spectrally resolvable zero-field splitting and near-infrared emission, the triplet state of the I$_4$ complex constitutes a viable spin quantum memory intrinsic to silicon.

papers.title: WorldFlow: Joint Video and 3D Motion Prediction via Large-Scale Pretraining
papers.abstract: Predicting future physical states stands as a central challenge in embodied intelligence. Existing video world models leave 3D dynamics implicit, action-based formulations remain tied to specific robot configurations, and 3D motion prediction models use flow-only supervision, providing a limited learning signal for physical dynamics. To circumvent these limitations, we introduce \method{}, a generative world model that jointly predicts future video and query-based 3D trajectories. By parameterizing 3D motion as continuous displacement tokens aligned with the video grid, a unified Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone jointly denoises both modalities under a rectified-flow objective. This formulation couples explicit geometric dynamics with visual evolution, effectively unlocking the physical commonsense embedded within pretrained video models. To empirically scale and validate this unified architecture, we train \method{} on a heterogeneous mixture of 1.44 million object-level samples spanning simulated and real-world domains. We further introduce WorldFlowBench, comprising 1,678 evaluation samples from 11 data sources across simulated and real-world interactions, including spatial reasoning tasks. Across all three evaluation sets, WorldFlow achieves the lowest average displacement error (ADE) and final displacement error (FDE) among the evaluated learning-based methods. Notably, on the challenging SpatialCog set, WorldFlow achieves an ADE of 0.060 m, a 54.2\% reduction compared with the strongest external baseline. It also reduces ADE and FDE by 55.9\% and 68.5\%, respectively, compared with its flow-only variant. Project page: https://roboscience-ai.github.io/worldflow-page/.

papers.title: Beyond Aggregate WER: In-domain Adaptation, Learner Speech, Code-Switching, and Speaker Attribution in Online Spanish Learning Classrooms
papers.abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) increasingly supplies transcripts for educational NLP, but aggregate word error rate (WER) can conceal errors concentrated in learner speech, multilingual turns, and speaker attribution. We compare platform-integrated, open-weight, adapted, and commercial ASR configurations on held-out sessions of online L2 Spanish interaction between L1 English learners and their instructors and tutors. Because English is the learner's shared first language, the interactions contain Spanish-only, English-only, and code-switched turns. Evaluation combines overall WER and character error rate (CER), WER disaggregated by speaker role and language context, and diarization error rate (DER). We also adapt Whisper large-v3 and MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize with LoRA using human-corrected in-domain classroom data. MOSS adaptation produced consistent improvements across speaker roles and language contexts, whereas Whisper showed smaller gains. Domain match proved more important than data volume: Larger out-of-domain bilingual and learner corpora did not outperform the smaller classroom corpus, where learner speech and code-switching are embedded in instructor--learner interaction. The open-weight MOSS adapter was competitive with commercial Muse Voice Transcribe on WER and CER and achieved lower system-provided DER on the recordings eligible for each system. Learner, English-only, and code-switched speech remained more difficult than instructor and Spanish-only speech. The findings demonstrate the value of condition-aware evaluation and interactionally matched data for bilingual educational ASR.

papers.title: Let the Gate Decide: Per-Lookup Precision for Quantized Conditional Memory in LLMs
papers.abstract: Conditional memory layers, such as DeepSeek's Engram, attach large hashed n-gram tables to a language model, and removing them from DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash costs 36.8 PopQA points. Low-bit quantization loses long-tail facts first, and the standard remedy, giving more bits to frequently accessed rows, backfires: refining lookups by access frequency is worse than refining them at random. We trace this to the gate that scales each retrieved row. A lookup's quantization error is weighted by its gate, which is small for frequent n-grams, large for the rare n-grams of long-tail entities, and computable from a 1-bit code. GateRQ therefore stores each row as a ladder of 1-bit residual codes, keeps level 1 in GPU memory to compute the gate, and reads deeper levels only for the lookups the gate ranks highest. Without retraining, GateRQ cuts GPU table memory by 7.8x on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, which raises vLLM throughput by 11%-31% over FP8 tables, while losing about 1 PopQA point at 1.50 bits read per lookup and 0.2 points at 2.10 bits across two models.

papers.title: Numerical reconstruction of polygonal obstacles by diffracted waves
papers.abstract: We present a numerical method for recovering rigid polygonal obstacles in two dimensions, based on the diffraction-based inverse scattering theory of Bao, Chen, Lu, and Xiong. A single pulse is emitted from a point source, and the resulting wave field is measured on a receiver curve. After isolating the diffracted signals, we recover the visible vertices from arrival times and the corner orientations and opening angles from amplitudes. The use of amplitude information permits local reconstruction in the reflection shadow, where reflected waves do not reach the receiver. The amplitudes also determine the direction of a shadowed edge adjacent to a visible vertex, enabling local non-line-of-sight imaging. Numerical experiments for a convex corner, a concave corner, a triangle, a pentagon, and a star-shaped obstacle confirm that the visible portion of the boundary can be recovered stably from diffracted signals. A further convex-corner test with additive noise at level $0.2\%$ on the single arc $L_{1}$ confirms that the tip and opening remain recoverable.

papers.title: LoRA Superposition across Pretrained Models
papers.abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is usually tied to the pretrained backbone on which it is learned. We ask whether LoRAs trained independently for the same task on different pretrained backbones can be summed and applied unchanged to all contributing backbones. We call this construction LoRA superposition. Across seven ViT-B/16 CLIP backbones and eight image-classification tasks, the exact sum improves all 56 backbone-task pairs and achieves a mean accuracy gain of 30.21 percentage points over the unadapted backbone. The exact sum achieves a mean accuracy only 0.28 percentage points below that of individually trained solo LoRAs. In contrast, a leave-one-model-out (LOMO) sum produces a mean gain of only 0.06 percentage points over the unadapted backbones. Backbone-specific solo LoRAs are nearly orthogonal in parameter space, while pairwise cross-backbone responses are strongly concentrated on the diagonal. These results support a component-wise non-interference hypothesis, under which the frozen backbone acts as an implicit selector of its own component without explicit routing or cross-model alignment.

papers.title: WildAIGC-Bench: Can AI Image Detectors Handle the Wild?
papers.abstract: An AI-generated scene or a subtle edit to a photograph can make a false claim about a public event appear credible. Existing benchmarks test detectors across generators and platforms, but offer limited insight into how well they recognize fabrications that circulate as evidence for such claims. We introduce WildAIGC-Bench, an event-driven benchmark designed for broad coverage, timely updates, and human-verified labels. A recurring search across news outlets, fact-checking sites, and social posts identifies emerging cases, and reviewers verify the evidence for each image. The benchmark contains 600 AI-generated or edited images and 638 genuine photographs of related subjects. It preserves posts alongside crops of the depicted images and links documented edits to their original photographs where available. All ten visual detectors achieve lower balanced accuracy on WildAIGC-Bench than their respective averages across eight external benchmarks with both classes. On 37\% of the AI images, at least three quarters of the evaluated detectors predict real. Cropping improves recall for most visual detectors but reduces it for most general-purpose multimodal models. Comparisons with editing originals further reveal local alterations that most detectors miss even when they correctly accept the original photograph.

papers.title: Elastic theory of ideal liquid crystal elastomers
papers.abstract: A liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) exhibits a two-way coupling between its mesogen order and network elasticity: the mesogen order sets the undeformed network conformation, and the network deformation reorients the mesogens. This coupling gives rise to large, reversible stimuli-responsive actuation, as well as to soft elasticity, a finite deformation at nearly zero stress. This article reviews the elastic theory of ideal LCEs, bridging single-chain statistics and continuum constitutive models. The "ideal" elastic behavior rests on the assumption of anisotropic Gaussian chains that retain no memory of the crosslinking state, such that the director can rotate at no cost of free energy when accompanied by a corresponding stress-free, ground-state deformation. The resulting neo-classical free energy of a monodomain LCE, when minimized over the director, is non-quasi-convex, with a continuous family of stress-free ground states, leading to thermally induced spontaneous deformation and soft elasticity accommodated by coexisting stripe domains. The quasi-convex relaxation of the free energy classifies the behavior of polydomain LCEs into three phases, each with a distinct macroscopic mechanical response depending on the stretch state. The ideal elastic theory can be further extended to incorporate additional behaviors and physical processes, including thermo- and photomechanical coupling, Frank elasticity from director distortion, semi-soft or non-soft behavior arising from network nonideality, and temperature- and rate-dependent viscoelasticity.

papers.title: A Bayesian Distance-Weighted Ising Model for Task-Related Regional Analysis of Neuroimaging Data
papers.abstract: Neuroimaging analysis commonly involves identifying task-relevant brain regions and examining functional connectivity. These objectives are typically addressed separately, without a model-based framework. We propose a Bayesian distance-weighted Ising model that jointly quantifies regional importance for task-label prediction and functional connectivity between brain regions. The Ising model favors agreement between interacting labels. We extend it with region-specific interaction parameters and weights based on distances between functional signals. The parameters quantify regional importance for distinguishing tasks, while the weights measure functional connectivity through signal similarity between regions. Inference for this model is challenging because the signals may be observed on unequal time grids and the likelihood function contains an intractable normalizing constant. To address this, we use a basis expansion and an auxiliary variable Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm. We apply the method to functional near-infrared spectroscopy data from younger and older adults, comparing resting-state and task-related activity. The model reveals age-dependent patterns of regional importance and connectivity. Among younger adults, the left orbitofrontal cortex contributes more strongly to task discrimination than the dorsolateral prefrontal and frontopolar cortices, whereas regional differences are less evident among older adults. Older adults also exhibit greater bilateral connectivity between corresponding regions, consistent with reduced hemispheric lateralization.

papers.title: CHSM8: A Chess Transformer that Follows Natural-Language Style Prompts
papers.abstract: We present CHSM8, a 210M-parameter chess transformer that plays moves conditioned on a free-text description of a playing style, e.g. "go for the Sicilian Defense", "solid, safe, risk-free chess" or "You are Magnus Carlsen in his prime". The model is pretrained without search on 1.07B filtered Lichess games, using a factorized move representation and legal-move masking. It reaches 1837 Elo against a strength-limited Stockfish and, in 1,000-game matches, beat every other public model we tested that was likewise trained without preference tuning, rewards or search, including one with 13 times as many parameters. We then fine-tune it to follow text on a synthetic dataset: Gemma-4-31B describes the playing style of 3M game sides, a 1B Gemma-3 model distilled from the 2.4M of those descriptions that contradict nothing on the board labels the rest, and every one of 30M selected game sides gets five descriptions. Supervised fine-tuning attaches a frozen text encoder through gated cross-attention, and direct preference optimization (DPO) uses the same moves under a mismatched description as the rejected sample. After DPO, style adherence rises on every prompt we test (for example, queens traded early 53% -> 67%, pawn moves 29% -> 32% of all moves, queenside castling 97.3% -> 99.7%), and strength without a prompt stays within noise of SFT (1792 vs. 1797 Elo). Design choices at every stage were made by fixed-budget automated search loops on top of standard architectures and training recipes. We document the full pipeline and the decisions behind it, report the ablations that failed, and evaluate the models across many style prompts and kinds of games, with 1,000 games per setting. The work is fully open source and reproducible: weights, datasets with all training labels, prompts, configurations, inference code and playable demos are public and free to build on.

papers.title: Multi-Method Machine Learning Classification of Astronomical Sources with Rubin Data Previews: a Spectroscopy-Free Approach with DP1 and DP2
papers.abstract: We present a multi-method machine-learning study for the binary photometric classification of point-like and extended sources in the Rubin Observatory Data Preview 1 (DP1) and Data Preview 2 (DP2). The workflow runs on the Rubin Science Platform using DP1 and DP2 ugrizy photometry, the DP1 ancillary photometric-redshift catalog, and the Monster astrometric and photometric reference catalog, without relying on external spectroscopy. Six methods (SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, k-Nearest Neighbors, an Artificial Neural Network, and a soft Voting ensemble) are benchmarked in the deepest DP1 field, the Extended Chandra Deep Field South. These methods reach 10-fold cross-validation macro-F1 scores of 0.95-0.97 on the balanced training subset and test macro-F1 scores of 0.87-0.92 on the imbalanced held-out set, with RF and the SV ensemble tied at the top (0.918); the differences among the leading methods are within the statistical uncertainty. Permutation importance identifies FWHM as the dominant feature, and the six methods agree on 79.5% of the full catalog. The same pipeline is then applied without retuning the settings to the two other DP1 fields with full ugrizy coverage and photometric-redshift support, Euclid Deep Field South and the Low Galactic Latitude Field. Together, the three fields span a factor of approximately 7 in E(B-V) and approximately 10 in stellar density, yet headline macro-F1 remains above 0.87 in every field. We then apply the same pipeline to four DP2 fields (ECDFS, COSMOS, EDFS, and ELAIS-S1). Using colors and morphology, the best method reaches a test macro-F1 of 0.83 to 0.88 across these fields, and the six methods agree on 77 to 86% of each catalog. Adding the per-band photometric uncertainties as features raises the best macro-F1 to about 0.95 in ECDFS DP1 and 0.97 in ECDFS DP2 (and to approximately 0.97-0.98 in the other fields).

papers.title: Martingale Transforms and Subsequence Estimates in Noncommutative \(L_p\)-Spaces
papers.abstract: We establish a transference principle from martingale transform inequalities to subsequence estimates for weakly null sequences. As applications, for every von Neumann algebra $\M$, (1) we show that, every bounded sequence in the Haagerup space $L_1(\M)=\M_*$ has either a norm-convergent subsequence or a $2$-co-lacunary subsequence, answering an open problem of Parcet and Randrianantoanina; (2) we prove that every UMD Banach space has the uniform USP, which in particular yields uniform USP for $L_p(\M)$, $1<p<\infty$, answering a question posed by Oikhberg and Spinu; (3) we answer an open problem of Haagerup, Rosenthal and Sukochev for the upper $\ell_p$ estimates for $L_p(\M)$, $1<p<2$, in the affirmative; (4) we also answer the problem of whether every $2$-strictly singular operator on a noncommutative $L_1$-space is automatically Dunford--Pettis.

papers.title: Softmax-Free Attention in Spiking Transformers as Zero-Temperature Two-Level Systems: Applications to XAI
papers.abstract: Spiking Transformer architectures usually drop the softmax, and some threshold each query--key score into a binary attention map. For such maps, the statistical mechanics of softmax attention does not carry over, because no temperature of the softmax gives a binary map. We show instead that each query--key link of threshold attention is a two-level system, as a spiking neuron is. Thus, a spiking Transformer with threshold attention is a zero-temperature network of two-level systems. In this picture, the attention map is a ground state, and the surrogate gradients used in training are susceptibilities at a finite temperature. Cooling trained networks from high temperature then shows that their predictions form gradually as their units freeze. Using this cooling picture, we adapt thermodynamic integration to explainable AI (XAI). Specifically, we heat the binary units of each patch, its neurons and the links into it, to random states at their deployed occupation, then cool them back patch by patch and credit each change of the output to the patch just cooled. This thermal integration (ThI) needs no gradients or input baseline, and its scores sum exactly to the output change. On CIFAR-10, pixel-level integrated gradients with surrogate gradients instead miss the output change by about a quarter. On six deletion and insertion tests in the spiking Transformer, ThI's mean rank is second only to Shapley value sampling with blurred patches. Yet ThI never ranks below fourth, whereas Shapley sampling, with any choice of removed patches, drops to sixth or seventh on some tests.

papers.title: NucleoNet: A Nuclear-Aware Determinant Ansatz for Multi-Geometry Neural Variational Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Neural-network variational Monte Carlo provides an accurate route to solving the electronic Schrödinger equation, but many neural wavefunctions are optimized for a single nuclear geometry, requiring separate calculations to map out a potential energy surface. We introduce NucleoNet, a nuclear-aware determinant ansatz that jointly evolves electronic and nuclear representations through a shared backbone, with antisymmetry enforced by electronic determinants. Across eight equilibrium small-molecule benchmarks, NucleoNet achieves energies comparable to established neural-wavefunction baselines with substantially fewer trainable parameters, totaling 0.10--0.13 million. For each molecular system, a single model optimized jointly across geometries describes the N$_2$ dissociation curve, Li displacement in LiCN, and the ethane and formamide minimum-energy paths for bond dissociation. Models trained on sparse geometry sets generalize to unseen configurations in N$_2$ and LiCN without further optimization. For N$_2$, training on six geometries yields a mean absolute error (MAE) of $1.13\ \mathrm{m}E_h$ on a 32-point evaluation grid, compared with $1.07\ \mathrm{m}E_h$ when optimized on all 32 geometries. Ablation studies on N$_2$ show that propagating nuclear representations improves geometric generalization under both shared and nucleus-specific envelope parameterizations.

papers.title: Fine-Grained Hardness of Approximating Dynamic Time Warping
papers.abstract: We prove conditional lower bounds for approximating dynamic time warping (DTW) over the uniform metric. Let $N,M$ be the lengths of the two strings and $n,m$ their numbers of runs. Under the Gap Block Disjointness Hypothesis, no deterministic algorithm $O(N^{\varepsilon})$-approximates DTW on two strings of length $N$ over three symbols in $\widetilde O(N^{2-δ})$ time for any constants $δ\in(0,1]$ and $\varepsilon\in[0,δ/3)$. In particular, no deterministic constant-factor approximation runs in strongly subquadratic time. For run-length encoded strings with $n=m$, the Orthogonal Vectors Hypothesis rules out every constant-factor approximation in $\widetilde O((nm)^{1-δ})$ time for every constant $δ>0$. It also rules out $(N+M)^{1-η}$-approximation in this time for every constant $η\in(0,1)$. The bounds extend to every fixed metric with at least three points, including absolute distance on $\{0,1,2\}$. Both reductions use long runs to force equal-symbol matches on low-cost paths. For explicit strings, Boolean gadgets encode the source predicate. A deterministic disperser-based density amplification then yields the polynomial gap. For run-length encoded strings, we encode regular-expression membership so that the gap grows without adding runs.

papers.title: Interval Inverse Inequalities for Multiscale Kernel Primitives with Positive Exponential Spectra
papers.abstract: Inverse inequalities are fundamental for controlling derivative growth and ensuring sampling stability in kernel-based approximation. Extending whole-space and single-scale estimates to multiscale analytic spaces on bounded intervals requires uniform control of boundary truncation and cross-scale cancellation. We establish unweighted $L^2(0,1)$ inverse inequalities of sharp scaling order $h_*^{-1}$ for trial spaces spanned by affine functions and multiscale primitives of kernels with positive exponential spectra, where $h_*$ denotes the finest scale. Under geometric scale separation and within-scale center separation, the inverse constant depends only on the kernel and separation parameters; it is independent of the number of scales and centers, allowing centers at the endpoints and arbitrary cross-scale center coincidences. To prove the bound, we combine an exterior Gram decomposition with endpoint-distance weights to establish configuration-uniform Riesz bounds for normalized high-order derivatives of order $q$, whose lower constant approaches the optimal limit $1/2$. A synthesis-operator perturbation argument and parameterized interval interpolation then yield the first-order estimate. Two-center constructions confirm sharpness in both the scaling order $h_*^{-1}$ and the $q^{-1/2}$ asymptotic deficit from $1/2$ as $q \to \infty$. An application to deterministic least-squares sampling is derived, and numerical experiments on boundary-layer asymptotics, multiscale Gram spectra, sharp inverse constants, and midpoint sampling illustrate the theory.

papers.title: Affine balancing of complex dilatations: affine invariants and optimal distortion of harmonic quasiconformal mappings
papers.abstract: Target real-affine postcomposition induces a disk automorphism on the complex dilatation of orientation-preserving planar harmonic mapping. Motivated by the lack of intrinsic distortion measures for real-affine orbits, we introduce the affine circumradius, affine diameter, and affine circumcenter from the hyperbolic geometry of the dilatation range. The affine circumradius is the logarithm of the minimal value of the maximal differential distortion over the real-affine orbit, and the affine circumcenter describes minimizers up to Euclidean similarity. For non-constant dilatation, at most two or three contact points determine the minimal enclosing hyperbolic disk. We prove sharp two-sided radius-diameter bounds, with equalities realized by globally univalent harmonic quasiconformal mappings. Each orbit admits a canonical balanced representative, for which we derive a sharp norm bound for the gap between the harmonic pre-Schwarzian derivative and that of its analytic part. This bound exhibits quadratic small-dilatation asymptotics, and the balanced representative achieves the minimal dilatation parameter over the real-affine orbit.

papers.title: Why Directly Learning Periodic Trajectories Can Fail
papers.abstract: Operator learning of periodic solutions requires deciding how simulation data should be recorded and represented. A natural choice is to integrate long enough for transients to decay and record a window wide enough to contain at least one full period of all trajectories. We find that these conservative choices can make the resulting trajectories difficult to learn, even when the underlying periodic orbits vary regularly with system parameters. Unaligned trajectories generalize poorly even within the training distribution. Phase alignment substantially improves in-distribution generalization, but models trained on a fixed physical-time window still have large errors on trajectories with periods outside the training range. We explain both failures through a common mechanism: frequency differences accumulate over time, so the target phase varies rapidly with the parameters. Predictors that cannot track this variation incur a population MSE floor in both settings; for fixed window prediction, we also derive a per-sample lower bound. We then study one of the simplest representations that escape these floors: learning an aligned, normalized waveform and its period separately. We establish regularity of the decoupled targets under ODE assumptions and show experimentally that this approach avoids both failures in ODE systems and a PDE case study.

papers.title: Adaptive Determinantal Client Scheduling in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Scheduling clients for model training is critical in federated learning due to both data and system heterogeneity. Most previous works focus on the quality of the scheduled clients to achieve faster convergence, shorter wall-clock convergence time, or better average model performance. They rarely consider the diversity of clients, which is important to counter heterogeneity and improve performance for the worst-off clients. In this work, we advocate the use of determinantal point processes (DPPs) to model and enhance the diversity in client scheduling. We first design the kernel matrices of DPPs using gradient information and quality scores, which inherently enables a flexible quality-diversity trade-off. Applying fast MAP inference over DPPs, we propose Adaptive Determinantal Client Scheduling (ADCS) in FL. We further quantify the gradient approximation error of ADCS and develop convergence analysis for general biased client selection in FL with non-convex loss functions. We conduct comparative numerical experiments showing that ADCS outperforms state-of-the-art client scheduling algorithms, including both quality-based and diversity-based ones.

papers.title: Polynomial Length Cycles In Tough Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that every $n$-vertex $15$-tough graph contains a cycle of length $Ω(n^{1/20})$.

papers.title: Protecting Private Values in Tool-Using LLM Agents via Recoverable Context Projection
papers.abstract: Memory-augmented and tool-using agents may expose exact private values when a remote LLM processes retrieved memory, tool actions, and observations. One-way masking limits initial exposure but removes values needed for trusted execution and may allow them to reappear in later observations. We propose Trustworthy Virtual Memory (TVM), a closed-loop runtime that exposes only projected context to the remote model, resolves exact values locally for trusted execution, and reprojects subsequent observations. We study whole-field and structure-preserving span-level projection, using a trusted local model to predict protected spans without access to the evaluation manifest. Experiments show that span-level projection preserves task-relevant structure, while recovery is necessary to turn protected reasoning into executable utility with low measured exposure.

papers.title: No-Box Vulnerability Analysis: Description-only Detection of Indirect Prompt Injection Vulnerabilities in MCP Servers
papers.abstract: When auditing remotely hosted services or commercially gated software for vulnerabilities, third-party analysts may lack both direct system access and the ability to interact with the running system. We call this a no-box setting, in which analysts have access only to functionality metadata that may describe the intended inputs, behaviors, and outputs of the system. Such descriptions constrain the possible implementations of a system, enabling analysts to hypothesize potential implementations and their underlying vulnerabilities. These hypotheses can subsequently guide validation when system access becomes available. To demonstrate the feasibility of conducting vulnerability analysis under no-box setting, we implemented MCPSEC, a prototype that audits Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities using only the tool metadata exposed at server registration time. Flagging vulnerable tools, MCPSEC produces hypothesized vulnerabilities and attack scenarios for later validation. We evaluated MCPSEC on 20 widely deployed MCP servers comprising 177 tools, among which human evaluators confirmed 95 as vulnerable. Using only tool metadata, MCPSEC successfully identified 94 of these confirmed vulnerable tools (98.9% recall), compared to 81 (85.3% recall) identified by an agentic baseline. Overall, we operationalize and evaluate no-box vulnerability analysis and demonstrate its practical feasibility in realistic systems.

papers.title: ELASTIC: Trajectory-Based Synchronization of Event and Tracking Data in Soccer
papers.abstract: Combining event and tracking data is fundamental to modern soccer analytics, yet the two sources are rarely well aligned: event timestamps recorded by human annotators often miss the true moment of the action, distorting the spatiotemporal context that downstream models rely on. Existing synchronization methods depend on noisy human-annotated event locations and fail to detect ball receptions, obscuring when each player gains ball possession. To address these limitations, we propose ELASTIC (Event-Location-AgnoSTIC synchronizer), a framework that infers the start and end timestamps of events solely from player and ball trajectories, without relying on annotated event locations. To recover ball receptions, ELASTIC enriches the event sequence by inserting virtual termination events between consecutive events, so that the end of each event is detected jointly with its start. It then extracts a sparse set of candidate frames where ball touches are physically plausible, and aligns the termination-inserted event sequence with the candidate-frame sequence using an extended Needleman-Wunsch algorithm. For reproducible evaluation, we construct a publicly available benchmark by annotating ground-truth timestamps on the Sportec Open DFL Dataset, on which ELASTIC substantially outperforms existing methods. Through downstream task evaluation, we further show that improved synchronization translates into measurable gains in soccer analytics. The source code and benchmark are available at https://github.com/hyunsungkim-ds/elastic.git.

papers.title: A General Framework for Metropolis-Adjusted Dikin Walks: Dimension-Square Mixing on Polytopes and Log-Det Walks on Spectrahedra
papers.abstract: Sampling from a log-concave density over a convex body is a fundamental problem. The Metropolis-adjusted Dikin walk draws Gaussian proposals shaped by a local barrier metric, and the main difficulty in its analysis is to control the proposal determinant and the reverse quadratic form at a random endpoint. In this paper, we analyze these walks with exact metrics by keeping the two terms together. In the complete logarithmic acceptance ratio, their leading uncentered terms cancel, and second-order tools control the remaining centered fluctuations. For a polytope given by $n$ inequalities and a convex $L$-Lipschitz potential, we show that the regularized Lee--Sidford walk mixes from a warm start in $\widetilde O((d^{2}+dL^{2}R^{2})\log(w/δ))$ steps. For a spectrahedron with $n\times n$ blocks, we show that the log-det walk scaled by $κ=\widetilde O(ψ^\star)$ mixes in $\widetilde O((ψ^\star nd+dL^{2}R^{2})\log(w/δ))$ steps, where $ψ^\star$ measures matrix leverage. Both analyses share an acceptance-to-mixing reduction. Moreover, we give exact-arithmetic implementations. For polytopes, a proposal-comparison argument transfers the bound to an appropriately padded $O(1/d)$-accurate metric computed from high-precision Lewis weights. For spectrahedra, given $\widehatψ\geψ^\star$, our implementation with the exact or a TensorSRHT-sketched log-det metric obtains the same bound with $ψ^\star$ replaced by $\widehatψ$.

papers.title: Direct linearization, Cauchy matrix and Sato Grassmannian
papers.abstract: Fu and Nijhoff's direct linearization scheme for the KP hierarchy employs a system of evolution equations of an infinite matrix U. Part of the matrix elements of U can be identified with affine coordinates of the top cell of the Sato Grassmannian. The evolution equations of these matrix elements are identical to the KP hierarchy realized as a dynamical system on the Sato Grassmannian. The system of evolution equations of U itself can be extended by the so called negative flows, and the extended system turns out to be equivalent to the two-component KP hierarchy. The Cauchy matrix approach to the KP hierarchy can be re-interpreted in this geometric perspective. This geometric interpretation of the direct linearization scheme persists to be useful for a multi-component generalization. The AKNS and anti-self-dual Yang-Mills hierarchies fall into this scheme. Multi-component Sato Grassmannians show up therein as the relevant geometric structure.

papers.title: ArmorOCR: Grounded Adversarial Visual Perception via Observation-Transferred Self-Distillation
papers.abstract: Large multimodal models (LMMs) have demonstrated strong OCR recognition capabilities, yet remain vulnerable to adversarial visual text that is readable to humans but challenging for models to localize and recognize. Existing OCR benchmarks mainly focus on natural or document-style text, while adversarial OCR evaluations remain limited in scale, task coverage, or region-aware evaluation. In this paper, we formulate adversarial OCR as a \textbf{grounded OCR perception} task and introduce \textbf{AdvSpot}, the first benchmark for grounded adversarial OCR evaluation. AdvSpot comprises 390 images with region-level annotations, spanning 5 primary categories and 13 fine-grained adversarial OCR types. To address this challenge, we propose \textbf{ArmorOCR}, a two-stage training framework for robust adversarial OCR perception. ArmorOCR first acquires missing adversarial OCR perception from privileged transformed observations through On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), and then refines grounded OCR perception through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with task-conditioned rewards for localization, recognition, full spotting, and visual question answering (VQA). Experiments on our AdvSpot, other adversarial OCR benchmarks, and general OCR benchmarks demonstrate that ArmorOCR consistently improves adversarial OCR perception while preserving competitive general OCR capability.

papers.title: Towards Understanding On-Policy Distillation through the Lens of Test-Time Scaling
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) has emerged as a promising post-training technique for enhancing LLM reasoning. Under the reverse KL objective, the idealized optimum of OPD aligns the student distribution with that of the teacher. When the teacher consistently outperforms the student, this naturally suggests that OPD should yield broad improvements over the pre-OPD student. However, do such improvements extend across the entire range of test-time sampling budgets? In this work, we revisit this expectation through the lens of test-time scaling by varying the sampling budget $K$ and evaluating performance with pass@$K$. Across multiple settings, we observe two distinct patterns: OPD can improve pass@$K$ at both small and large sampling budgets, but it can also improve small-budget performance while reducing large-budget pass@$K$. We show one condition that guarantees such a reversal and an idealized reverse KL counterexample where it occurs even when the teacher has higher accuracy on every problem. To choose between two candidate teachers at a target sampling budget, we propose the \textit{Teacher Advantage Score at $K$} (TAS@$K$), which can be computed before OPD training to predict which teacher will lead to a larger improvement in pass@$K$. Across three domains and thirteen benchmarks, the ordering predicted by TAS@$K$ agrees with the observed pass@$K$ improvements of the resulting OPD models in 83.6\% of experiments, providing a useful signal for teacher selection at the target pass@$K$.

papers.title: Locating the missing baryons in the warm-hot intergalactic medium with fast radio bursts and the Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect
papers.abstract: Traditional astronomical censuses in the late-time Universe can only account for a fraction of the baryonic matter budget. Hydrodynamical simulations predict that the missing baryons reside in the vast filamentary structures of the cosmic web as a highly diffuse, warm-hot intergalactic medium (WHIM). Observing the WHIM directly has remained a long-standing challenge due to its typical temperature. In this study, we measure the angular cross-power spectrum between the dispersion measures (DMs) of fast radio bursts (FRBs) from the second CHIME/FRB catalog and the thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) Compton-$y$ map from the Planck satellite. After masking cataloged galaxy clusters, we find a positive correlation between FRB DMs and the tSZ map at $>98\%$ confidence ($p_{\rm null}=0.0169$). With a temperature normalization of $2.4\times10^6\ {\rm K}$, we infer that a fraction $f_{\rm WHIM}=0.375^{+0.165}_{-0.161}$ of cosmic baryons resides in the hotter WHIM. These measurements constrain a substantial reservoir of hotter diffuse gas in the cosmic web and statistically close the cosmic baryon budget in the local Universe under the adopted density and pressure model.

papers.title: Flying over The Uncertain Nature (FORTUNE): Intelligent and Humanistic 3D Path Planning for Low-Altitude Collaboration
papers.abstract: Low-altitude intelligent agents are driving demand for timely, socially responsible collaborative sensing in dynamic urban environments. Yet jointly handling heterogeneous spatio-temporal sensing demands, real-time uncertainty, and human-centered constraints in a unified multi-uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) framework remains challenging. We study 3D multi-UAV path planning and joint task assignment under heterogeneous spatio-temporal uncertainty of ground points of interest (PoIs). Unlike studies assuming static, known PoIs, we formulate a unified model capturing persistent (Type-I), temporally predictable (Type-II), and emergent unpredictable (Type-III) demands. Following the low-altitude-for-good principle, we explicitly model altitude-dependent societal and environmental costs, including noise and public safety risks, jointly optimizing sensing effectiveness and socially compliant operations. To solve the resulting large-scale mixed-integer nonlinear problem, we propose FORTUNE, a hierarchical offline-online framework. Offline, a Transformer-based predictor forecasts Type-II activation windows, while an enhanced sparrow search algorithm (ES2A) with priority-aware decoding and danger-aware evolution generates globally coordinated flight plans. Online, lightweight trajectory refinement accommodates new Type-III PoIs while preserving global mission coherence. Experiments on real-world traffic and synthetic datasets show FORTUNE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art benchmarks, validating effectiveness, scalability, and practical applicability in dynamic low-altitude systems.

papers.title: Augmented Inverse Hybrid Weighting: Robust Inference under Deterministic and Random Distribution Shifts
papers.abstract: Reweighting source samples to match a target covariate distribution is a standard response to distribution shift when generalizing evidence across populations. It is well suited to deterministic, learnable covariate discrepancies, but can fail when source--target differences extend beyond covariate shift or when estimation of the density-ratio weights is unstable. We introduce a new model where the discrepancy between two population laws comprises a deterministic covariate shift and a non-systematic component, modeled as random perturbation of the probability space. This separates systematic shifts, treated as bias and corrected by reweighting, from random perturbations, treated as distributional uncertainty and reduced by dataset pooling. Under pure random perturbations, this principle yields Augmented Inverse Distance Weighting, which combines regression augmentation with variance-optimal dataset-level pooling and attains asymptotic variance no larger than exact covariate balancing. When both components are present, we develop Augmented Inverse Hybrid Weighting, which interpolates between AIDW and standard augmented importance weighting. Both estimators tradeoff sampling and distributional uncertainty via a distributional distance quantifying the strength of random perturbations. We establish asymptotic normality of both estimators and provide tuning and diagnostic tools. On three real-world multi-site datasets exhibiting diverse distribution shifts, the proposed methods consistently reduce mean-squared error compared with weighting baselines, and improve empirical coverage when covariate-shift adjustment alone undercovers.

papers.title: Agentic Coding in the Wild: Characterizing GitHub Copilot Traces at Production Scale
papers.abstract: AI coding agents (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Codex) interleave multi-step LLM inference with tool execution, creating a workload different from chatbots. We present the first production-scale characterization of coding agents using sampled GitHub Copilot traces from June-July 2026, comprising 7.4M users, 819M conversations, 5.7B LLM calls, and 946T tokens. Our analysis reveals distinctive workload properties with unique systems implications: e.g., sparse user-initiated turns unfold into autonomous agent loops with nearly 1:1 coupling between LLM calls and tool execution; parallel LLM calls are rare but exist in turns that trigger subagents; KV cache hit rates average 90% within a turn, but fall to 52% across turn boundaries and to 6% after model switches; workflows and user behaviors exhibit diverse, long-tailed resource footprints. We further distinguish short agentic turnaround times from minutes-long user idle periods between turns, and develop a lightweight idle-time predictor that captures 87-89% of total idle time. We demonstrate two use cases: (1) a harness-side LLM API keep-alive policy that preserves provider-side context KV cache, reducing token costs by 14.9% on turn boundaries; and (2) a serving-side KV cache residency policy that uses predicted idle time to guide DRAM offloading, reducing time to first token (TTFT) by 3-33% compared with LRU during a one-week evaluation with GitHub Copilot traces.

papers.title: An indefinite Coulomb interaction from the Steklov spectrum of perforated manifolds
papers.abstract: We establish optimal convergence rates for Steklov eigenvalues and harmonically extended eigenfunctions toward their weighted Laplace--Beltrami counterparts on a closed manifold perforated by many small geodesic balls. The holes have radii that scale critically with respect to their spacing in the sense that the boundary area of each hole balances with the weighted volume of its Voronoi cell. We then derive a higher-order expansion of the Steklov eigenvalues; in dimensions two and three, we identify two correction scales. The expansion is governed by an indefinite Coulomb-type energy of the discrepancy between the boundary and bulk measures, mediated by the reduced Green function of the limiting operator. The proof relies on sharp estimates for certain auxiliary functions that we introduce in order to quantify the discrepancy measure between the surface measure on the holes and their background density. Our paper serves to bridge an emerging literature in spectral geometry with one on systems of points interacting via Coulomb-type energies.

papers.title: Intercity EV Charging Readiness in Türkiye: A Countrywide Scheduling and Economic Assessment
papers.abstract: This paper assesses whether Türkiye's 9,641 public charging stations licensed by the Energy Market Regulatory Authority (EPDK) can support intercity electric vehicle (EV) travel, and at what cost relative to internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles. A charging scheduling framework based on a directed acyclic graph plans the charging stops of 3 million synthetic intercity trips on a 55,236-link highway network built from OpenStreetMap. Virtually all trips can be completed with the existing stations under both 10--100% and 20--80% state-of-charge windows; the 0.3% feasibility that a 20--80% window can produce arises only when trips must also start within the window, not from gaps in the network. Capacity, not coverage, is the binding constraint: with plug counts calibrated to EPDK socket statistics, uncoordinated charging builds long queues at the stations where trips converge, whereas coordinating charging times with reservations nearly eliminates waiting at today's adoption level of about 3%. In the 350 kW scenario at 3% adoption, the EV is 49.8% cheaper than the ICE vehicle in operating costs (energy, refueling, detour, and charging time) and 7.4% cheaper in total cost of ownership, an advantage that holds as long as the EV costs at most about 9% more than a comparable ICE vehicle. Adding the cost of charging infrastructure makes the EV more expensive at low adoption with high-power chargers and cheaper as adoption grows.

papers.title: Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in recommendation systems
papers.abstract: Large-scale recommendation systems face "Memory Wall" bottlenecks due to massive, dense embedding tables. While generative retrieval uses discrete tokens for IDs, high-dimensional context still relies on inefficient dense formats. Inspired by computer vision data compression, we propose Dual-purpose Semantic IDs to achieve LLM-level I/O efficiency. Our methodology uses hierarchical quantization to condense continuous embeddings into discrete Semantic IDs performing two concurrent roles: (1) Collaborative Identity: modeling user-item interactions via learnable embedding table; and (2) Content Reconstruction: using a lightweight Semantic Decoder for on-the-fly embedding approximation. This approach replaces massive vector storage with on-demand reconstruction, reducing system overhead and data footprints. We demonstrate the efficacy of our framework through offline evaluations and successful online deployment in production-scale ranking and retrieval systems at a major video sharing platform, showing that discrete tokens are indeed all you need for highly efficient, content-rich recommendation.

papers.title: Probabilistic "Copies" in Generative AI Models
papers.abstract: Recent work shows that it is possible to extract verbatim or near-verbatim text of some copyrighted works from some large language models (LLMs or models). That is evidence that the model weights encode the works in some form---that the model has "memorized" those works from its training data. But LLMs don't store information in the same format as familiar databases. Rather, their weights store statistical relationships that have been learned from the training data, and those relationships inform a generation process that in practice is often probabilistic rather than deterministic. In the case of memorization, those relationships are strong enough that, in many circumstances, the model could generate a copyrighted work from its training data. Copyright law has not previously had to decide whether storing information that might or might not produce output similar to a copyrighted work is itself a copy of the work. The answer to this question is important, because it may determine the legality of many LLMs. The statute and caselaw are largely unhelpful. We argue that copyright law will likely take a functional approach to the question, finding that LLMs contain a copy of a particular work only if it is straightforward to extract that work in outputs. That result is unsatisfying as a policy matter, and we suggest potential changes to the law, but it is the most likely outcome under current law.

papers.title: Ace! Motion Planning of Professional-Level Table Tennis Serves with a Robot Arm
papers.abstract: Table tennis, a dynamic, compact, and popular sport, has for many years received significant attention as a robotics benchmark. Most of the research has focused on the rally aspect -returning an incoming ball-requiring high-speed vision, agile motion planning, and tight closed-loop control. On the other hand, getting robots to serve competitively remains a rather unexplored research problem, which in fact requires pushing physics modeling and control to the extremes.
