In this work, we present the first-ever approach capable of generating official rule-compliant serves that produce ball spins of up to 550 rad/s and speeds of up to 6.7 m/s, matching and even surpassing the capabilities of elite table tennis players. In official matches against these competitors, our serves score direct points in up to 21% of attempts and push the win rate of robot-initiated rallies above 50%. The motion plans for serving are generated in simulation by combining optimization-based control and Bayesian optimization, and are executed zero-shot in open-loop on our hardware.

papers.title: The Gauss periods and cyclotomic matrices involving Gauss sums over cyclic groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, by using the arithmetic properties of the Gauss periods and character sums over cyclic groups, we study the cyclotomic matrix $$A_k(χ)=\left[G_N(χ^{ki+ki})\right]_{0\le i,j\le φ(N)/k-1},$$ where $N=p^m$ is a prime power, $φ(\cdot)$ is the Euler totient function, $k$ is a divisor of $φ(N)$, $χ$ is a generator of character group $\widehat{(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^{\times}}$, and $$G_N(χ^{ki+kj})=\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}}χ^{ki+kj}(x)e^{2πix/N}$$ is the Gauss sum over $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$.

papers.title: Existence of weak solutions of the surface Beris-Edwards model
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of weak solutions to the surface Beris-Edwards model for nematic liquid crystals posed on a $d$-dimensional ($d \in \{2,3\}$) closed hypersurface of class $C^{2,1}$. This thermodynamically consistent model, recently introduced by Bouck, Nochetto and Yushutin (2024), couples the incompressible tangent Navier-Stokes equations with a kinematic equation for the Q-tensor field that encodes the orientation of the liquid crystal particles with a general state of orientational order. Extending ideas by Abels, Dolzmann and Liu (2014) and Guillén-González and Rodríguez-Bellido (2015) for the Beris-Edwards model in flat domains, we design a Faedo-Galerkin scheme based upon eigenfunctions of an appropriate tangent Stokes operator and tensor-valued Laplace-Beltrami operator and recover a weak solution via standard compactness arguments.

papers.title: Deconfined criticality between an antiferromagnetic insulator and a nodal d-wave superconductor: a quantum Monte Carlo study
papers.abstract: We present a quantum Monte Carlo study of the transition between the insulating Néel state and the nodal $d$-wave superconductor on the square lattice at half-filling. We access a regime of frustrated magnetic order without a sign problem using a parton representation of the electron in terms of fermionic spinons and bosonic chargons. Both partons move in a background $π$-flux (so the electron experiences no net flux) and are coupled to a quantum fluctuating SU(2) lattice gauge field. In contrast to earlier studies directly on the electronic degrees of freedom, we find evidence for a second-order deconfined quantum phase transition at which both the Néel and $d$-wave superconductivity orders vanish continuously. We compute correlators of the spinon-chargon composite with the same quantum numbers as the electron: we find a gapless Dirac dispersion inside the $d$-wave superconductor, turning into a gapped dispersion in the antiferromagnet.

papers.title: Competing redox and material redistribution during electrode ageing
papers.abstract: Electrochemical processes can involve coupled redox reactions, active-material redistribution and morphological evolution at buried electrode-electrolyte interfaces1-3. Operando imaging has revealed nanoscale heterogeneity in these processes3-9, but how reversible redox and cumulative material redistribution interact during cycles to govern electrode ageing remains unclear. Here we develop fast operando soft X-ray spectro-ptychography to track oxidation state, morphology and iron redistribution in the same nanoscale region of an alkaline iron anode over 20 h of cycling. We distinguish two coexisting processes operating on different timescales. Within each cycle, iron undergoes rapid, reversible conversion between metallic iron and iron oxyhydroxide (FeOOH) with little net iron redistribution. Across cycles, slower iron redistribution, consistent with dissolution and redeposition, promotes FeOOH-rich particle growth. Particle-resolved trajectories reveal that reversible conversion and iron accumulation coexist within individual particles, while particles with similar apparent growth exhibit markedly different changes in iron content. Local capacity initially increases as particles grow, then declines as more iron remains oxidized after charging and the reversible redox swing narrows. These findings suggest that cumulative Fe redistribution competes with reversible redox by progressively limiting the Fe available for charge storage. More generally, electrode ageing can begin during nearly reversible cycling, before capacity loss becomes apparent.

papers.title: A note on the image of graded multilinear polynomials on upper triangular matrices
papers.abstract: We investigate the image of polynomials multilinear in graded variables evaluated on the algebra of upper triangular matrices endowed with a group grading. We show that, in general, such an image need not be a vector subspace. However, under the additional assumption that the identity component of the grading is commutative, we prove that the image is always a vector subspace. We further investigate the image of polynomials evaluated on inverse and direct limits of algebras. As a consequence, we prove that the image of a polynomial evaluated on a direct limit of upper triangular matrix algebras whose identity component is commutative is always a vector subspace.

papers.title: Declarative Skills for AI Agents in Knowledge-Grounded Tool-Use Workflows
papers.abstract: We study how orchestration affects tool-using large language model (LLM) agents in customer-service workflows over an unstructured knowledge base, comparing a declarative agent that reads natural-language skill files, an imperative agent built on a state machine, and an unscaffolded baseline. The three are formalized as policy classes within one decentralized partially observable Markov decision process and evaluated on a complete design of five models, two retrieval regimes, and three agents, with paired tests. Averaged over all conditions, orchestration does not improve task success. The effect, however, depends on the quality of the agent's observation channel. Under perfect retrieval, skill files are neutral-to-negative on four of the five models; under embedding retrieval they are neutral-to-positive on four of the five. On the tasks where baseline and scaffold disagree, the declarative win rate rises from 42.4% to 62.7% (p = 0.016), and the same interaction is present for the state machine (p = 0.003). Orchestration thus substitutes for information the agent lacks rather than supplementing information it has. Since deployed systems never attain perfect retrieval, the regime in which skill files help is the realistic one. Skill files also improve write-argument accuracy in all ten conditions (p = 0.002) without improving end-to-end success, and reduce unauthorized writes only where a compliance gap exists. The state machine lowers task success on four of the five models, and its verification gate is phase routing that misclassification can bypass. Enforcing the same precondition at the tool-execution layer eliminates unauthorized writes while preserving task success.

papers.title: Moment-Video: Diagnosing Temporal Fidelity of Video MLLMs on Momentary Visual Events
papers.abstract: Video multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress in general and long-form video understanding, yet their ability to capture and use brief, answer-critical visual evidence remains underexplored. Momentary actions or state transitions may determine an answer while occupying only a small fraction of the video. Performance on broad video understanding tasks alone does not establish whether models can reliably identify and use this temporally localized evidence. We introduce Moment-Video, a benchmark for evaluating temporal fidelity through momentary visual event understanding. Questions are constructed around visually observable events or event sequences, requiring models to notice, count, describe, or reason about transient evidence. The benchmark contains 1,000 human-verified video-QA pairs across seven domains and 25 subcategories, covering four tasks: Temporal Occurrence, Temporal Counting, Action Description, and Temporal Reasoning. We evaluate 34 proprietary and open-source MLLMs. Under the main evaluation settings, the best-performing model, Seed-2.0-Pro, achieves 39.6% overall accuracy, while most open-source models remain below 25%. Diagnostic analyses show that denser frame sampling improves some models, but substantial errors persist in an audited subset even when human review judges the sampled visual evidence sufficient to answer. Performance also declines on longer videos, suggesting additional temporal-localization challenges. By exposing these limitations, Moment-Video provides a diagnostic benchmark to guide the evaluation and development of video MLLMs that more reliably understand brief, answer-critical visual events.

papers.title: Energy spectra and cascade in the spin turbulence of a driven spinor Bose-Einstein condensate
papers.abstract: We investigate the spin-interaction energy spectrum of spin turbulence in a driven spinor Bose-Einstein condensate. Continuous spin driving of a spin-1 condensate produces a nonequilibrium steady state with spatially fluctuating magnetization. We observe a power-law scaling consistent with the $-7/3$ exponent predicted for spin-wave turbulence, which persists across our full range of drive strengths despite substantial changes in the spectral anisotropy. After switching off the drive, we track the free-decay evolution and find evidence consistent with a direct cascade of spin-interaction energy toward higher wavenumbers. These results establish an energy-spectral hallmark of spin turbulence and enable quantitative studies of cascade dynamics in spinor superfluids.

papers.title: Probing the Prompt KV Cache: Where It Becomes Dispensable
papers.abstract: Prior KV cache compression schemes empirically demonstrate that the prompt cache can be dropped or summarised during decoding with little accuracy loss, indicating that it is partly redundant. We ask when and what kind of redundancy, i.e., at which layers, after how many decoding steps, and in what form can the prompt span KV cache be replaced without breaking the task. A controlled splice intervention swept over layers and decoding steps shows this redundancy is about form rather than content. Replacing the upper layer prompt span KV cache with KV cache from a chat template scaffold with empty user content or filler tokens recovers near clean accuracy, while zeroing the entire prompt KV collapses accuracy. The dissociation replicates across the Qwen3, Gemma 3, and Llama 3 model families of varying sizes on multiple datasets. A serving implementation of this technique reduces KV memory by $15.4\%$, supports $18\%$ more HBM-constrained concurrent requests, and improves throughput by $13$-$21\%$.

papers.title: A Two-Parameter Weibull Framework for Diagnosing Transformer Weight Distributions
papers.abstract: Transformer checkpoints contain billions of weights, yet how their element-wise distributions vary across components, models, and training is hard to characterize. We fit the magnitude distribution of each analyzed weight matrix with a two-parameter Weibull reference model under a fixed middle-80% protocol. For i.i.d. Gaussian initialization, the corresponding half-Normal target has protocol-fitted shape $k_0 \approx 1.20$. Matched comparisons with gamma and lognormal favor Weibull for most component groups; support is less decisive for separately stored MHA query/key projections, and no tested single family cleanly describes matrices carrying a secondary weight population. Across 12 model entries spanning seven families, terminal FFN shape medians fall in a narrow band, $k \in [1.186, 1.204]$ (CV $= 0.51\%$), whereas query/key projections show architecture-associated departures. This stability is macroscopic only: in the five Pythia models whose released step-0 checkpoints permit a paired comparison, FFN and attention-output matrices remain near the reference shape despite large displacement and reorientation, so terminal shape similarity is not explained by parameter proximity alone. The fitted shape $k$ is read as a reference-relative central-body shape indicator and the scale $λ$ as a magnitude coordinate; neither is presented as a predictor of downstream performance. In a Qwen case study, the screen localizes a shallow-FFN secondary small-magnitude population, and direct raw-weight analysis of a flagged block traces much of that population to coherently suppressed intermediate channels. The method requires only released checkpoints and complements behavioral and structural analyses. The code and reference database are available at https://github.com/tiexinding/NPM-Weibull-public.

papers.title: A Survey of Advancing Audio Super-Resolution and Bandwidth Extension from Discriminative to Generative Models
papers.abstract: Audio super-resolution (SR), also referred to as bandwidth extension (BWE), aims to reconstruct high-fidelity signals from low-resolution (LR) or band-limited (BL) observations, an inherently ill-posed task due to the ambiguity of missing high-frequency (HF) content. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of the field, with a particular focus on the paradigm shift from discriminative mapping to modern generative modeling. We first review early discriminative deep neural network (DNN) models, which formulate BWE/SR as a deterministic mapping problem and are prone to regression-to-the-mean effects and spectral over-smoothing. We then systematically review generative approaches, including autoregressive (AR) models, variational autoencoders (VAEs), generative adversarial networks (GANs), diffusion and score-based models, flow-based methods, and Schrödinger bridges. Across these approaches, we examine key design aspects, including representation domain, architecture, conditioning mechanisms, and trade-offs among reconstruction fidelity, perceptual quality, robustness, and computational efficiency. We further conduct unified experiments on representative discriminative and generative methods to provide controlled empirical evidence for these trade-offs. Furthermore, we discuss emerging directions involving large language models (LLMs) and multimodal foundation models, and highlight open challenges in perceptual evaluation, practical deployment, and real-world generalization. By providing a structured taxonomy and unified perspective, this survey establishes a comprehensive foundation and offers a practical roadmap for advancing BWE/SR from deterministic point estimation toward distribution-aware generative modeling.

papers.title: StreamPro: Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Grained Rewards for Proactive Streaming Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Proactive streaming video understanding requires models to continuously monitor evolving video streams and decide whether, when, and what to respond. However, training models with such proactive capabilities remains challenging. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) suffers from severe imbalance between silence and response signals, while reinforcement learning (RL) faces sparse response-level rewards and difficulties in optimizing interdependent response sequences. To address these challenges, we propose StreamPro, a two-stage training framework. We first introduce CB-Stream Loss to alleviate supervision imbalance during SFT. We then employ Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with two complementary rewards: a refined Response-Matching (RM) reward that provides denser feedback for individual response decisions, and a rubric-based Sequence-Quality (SQ) reward that encourages globally coherent response sequences. To support the two training stages, we construct StreamPro-SFT-63K and StreamPro-RL-3K, respectively. To address the limited task coverage of existing proactive benchmarks, we further introduce StreamPro-Bench, encompassing three task categories: Perceptual Understanding, Temporal Reasoning, and Anticipatory Assistance, along with StreamPro-F1 to evaluate response correctness, timing, and frequency. Experiments demonstrate that StreamPro substantially improves proactive streaming video understanding, achieving an average StreamPro-F1 of 32.8 on StreamPro-Bench, compared with 9.2 for the strongest baseline, while maintaining strong performance on real-time streaming tasks, reaching 79.8 on StreamingBench-RTVU.

papers.title: Faster PBWT prefix-array access via batching
papers.abstract: The positional Burrows-Wheeler Transform (PBWT) is commonly used to store haplotype panels compactly in such a way that, given a query haplotype, we can quickly find the set-maximal exact matches (SMEMs) between the query and the haplotypes in a panel. There are generally two steps in this process: first we find the maximal substrings of the query that occur in the same positions in haplotypes in the panel and then, for each such substring, report the IDs of the haplotypes in the panel in which the substring occurs in the same position as in the query. Very recently, Bonizzoni, Gagie and Gao (2026) gave two time-space tradeoffs for the second step: they use either $O ((r + h) \log n)$ bits and $O (\log \log_w \min (h, \ell) + k)$ time to report $k$ haplotype IDs, or $O (r \log h + h \log n)$ bits and $O (k \log \log_w h)$ time, where $r$ is the number of runs in the panel's PBWT, $h$, $\ell$ and $n = h \ell$ are the panel's height, length and size, respectively, and $w$ is the number of bits in a machine word. We observe here that if we can batch queries until we have found $r \lg (h) / \lg r$ such substrings, then for the second step we can easily use $O (r \log h)$ bits and $O (r + K)$ total time to report all $K$ haplotype IDs, which is $O (\log (r) / \log h)$ amortized time for each haplotype ID, assuming the haplotypes in the panel are distinct. With that assumption, this is the same space bound as for Bonizzoni, Gagie and Gao's second tradeoff, with a time bound that is asymptotically smaller when $\lg (r) / \lg h \in o (\log \log_w h)$. Compared to their first tradeoff, our space bound is smaller by a factor of about $\lg (n) / \lg h$ and our time bound is larger by a factor of at most $\lg (r) / \lg h$. Our approach is based on an algorithm for constructing the prefix arrays quickly from the PBWT, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: RefDecoder: Enhancing Visual Generation with Conditional Video Decoding
papers.abstract: Video generation powers a vast array of downstream applications. However, while the de facto standard, i.e., latent diffusion models, typically employ heavily conditioned denoising networks, their decoders often remain unconditional. We observe that this architectural asymmetry leads to significant loss of detail and inconsistency relative to the input image. To address this, we argue that the decoder requires equal conditioning to preserve structural integrity. We introduce RefDecoder, a reference-conditioned video VAE decoder by injecting high-fidelity reference image signal directly into the decoding process via reference attention. Specifically, a lightweight image encoder maps the reference frame into the detail-rich high-dimensional tokens, which are co-processed with the denoised video latent tokens at each decoder up-sampling stage. We demonstrate consistent improvements across several distinct decoder backbones (e.g., Wan 2.1 and VideoVAE+), achieving up to +2.1 dB PSNR over the unconditional baselines on the Inter4K, WebVid, and Large Motion reconstruction benchmarks. Notably, RefDecoder can be directly swapped into existing video generation systems without additional fine-tuning, and we report across-the-board improvements in subject consistency, background consistency, and overall quality scores on the VBench I2V benchmark. Beyond I2V, RefDecoder generalizes well to a wide range of visual generation tasks such as style transfer and video editing refinement.

papers.title: Self-organized photonic time quasicrystal from a single imposed clock
papers.abstract: A photonic time crystal usually writes a clock into a medium. Here one clock does more than program the medium: it seeds a quasiperiodic temporal order that the nonlinear medium selects for itself. In a guided-wave lattice of nonlinear dipoles, a single-tone pump modulates the polarization sector, while Maxwell--polarization back-action selects two response frequencies whose only resolved low-order relation is the pump-locked sum condition. Their sum phase locks to the pump and the complementary phase winds, producing a photonic discrete time quasicrystal with torus-like phase dynamics and a discrete combination spectrum. Site-resolved measurements show locked-phase coherence across the measured lattice sites over a finite control-parameter window. These results establish a route from externally programmed time-varying media to self-organized temporal order in nonlinear photonic systems.

papers.title: ScrapMem: A Bio-Inspired Framework for On-Device Personalized Agent Memory via Optical Forgetting
papers.abstract: Long-term personalized memory for LLM agents is challenging on resource-limited edge devices because multimodal histories grow continually and are costly to store. To address this challenge, we propose ScrapMem, a bio-inspired framework that consolidates each day's heterogeneous records into a unified "Scrapbook Page." ScrapMem introduces Optical Forgetting, an optical compression mechanism that progressively reduces the resolution and JPEG quality of older pages, lowering storage costs while keeping recent evidence at higher fidelity. To preserve semantic consistency and support structured retrieval, we construct an Episodic Memory Graph (EM-Graph) that organizes semantic nodes into causal-temporal EM-Paths. This design separates a stable retrieval structure from aging visual evidence, allowing relevant episodes to remain accessible as page fidelity decreases. Under the common ATM-Bench protocol, ScrapMem without forgetting establishes a new non-oracle state of the art with 51.0% Joint@10 and reaches 70.3% Recall@10. Optical Forgetting reduces the persistent memory footprint by up to 93.0% relative to the raw corpus while retaining over 90% of No-Forget performance. ScrapMem offers a storage-efficient and interpretable approach to long-term multimodal memory for on-device LLM agents. The code is available on GitHub.

papers.title: What's on Your Mind? Exploring Privacy of Mental Health Apps
papers.abstract: Therapy and life-coaching apps have grown rapidly in popularity, yet their users often share highly sensitive information, including mental health issues, trauma, and relationship difficulties. This prompts the need to examine privacy practices across the ecosystem. In this paper, we present a comprehensive analysis of 25 popular Android mental health and life-coaching apps, combining static analysis, dynamic network traffic analysis, and identifying gaps between observed app behavior and privacy policies. Our analysis highlights serious concerns and substantial transparency gaps. First, all but one app embeds at least one tracker SDK not named in its privacy policy, and 90\% of the apps we instrument fail to disclose at least half of their detected trackers. Second, more than half of the apps declare dangerous permissions without corresponding privacy-policy disclosures, including camera or microphone permissions. Third, 14 of the 25 apps disclose third-party AI processing, but only five name the providers (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, and Groq), while the others use only generic language (e.g., "AI services"). Overall, our results highlight shortcomings in current disclosure practices that undermine meaningful informed consent. We argue for stronger privacy protections for therapy apps, more closely aligned with the confidentiality expectations associated with licensed human therapists.

papers.title: Quantum Metric and Nonlinear Hall Effect of Photons
papers.abstract: Using the path-integral formalism, we show that photons possess a nontrivial quantum metric in momentum space. We derive the semiclassical action and equations of motion by taking into account the quantum metric. In media with a spatially varying refractive index $n(\mathbf{x})$, the quantum metric induces a shift in the trajectory of light at second order in spatial gradients of $n$, whose transverse component may be regarded as a nonlinear Hall effect of light. The quantum metric also gives rise to corrections to photon propagation relevant to gravitational lensing in curved spacetime at second order in wavelength, including a gravitational nonlinear Hall effect arising from the interplay between the geometry of position space and that of momentum space.

papers.title: A bivariate cure copula model with zero-inflated gamma frailty for right-censored data
papers.abstract: In biomedical studies, paired survival data arise naturally when two event times are observed within the same subject. Existing statistical models seldom accommodate both cure fractions and complex dependence structures. In this paper, we propose a novel bivariate cure frailty-copula model for paired survival data with a cure fraction. By incorporating a zero-inflated gamma frailty, the proposed framework simultaneously accommodates a cure fraction and continuous unobserved heterogeneity among uncured subjects. Dependence between cure statuses is modeled naturally via an odds-ratio parameter, while dependence between survival times conditional on frailty is captured through a copula. To provide interpretable measures of overall dependence in the presence of cure, we derive population-level rank correlation coefficients, namely tie-adjusted versions of Kendall's tau and Spearman's rho. For suitable choices of baseline marginal survival functions and copulas, the joint survival function admits a closed-form expression, enabling maximum likelihood estimation and likelihood ratio testing. Simulation studies demonstrate satisfactory finite-sample performance and favorable comparisons with existing bivariate cure models. In a real-data analysis, the proposed model is favored by information criteria. An R package, curecopula, implementing the proposed methods is publicly available on GitHub.

papers.title: Rippled graphene pores as fluidic memristive devices with synaptic and neuromorphic functionalities
papers.abstract: Nanofluidic memristive devices work with nanoscale pores and ions dissolved in water, which harness the ionic memory effect aiming to store and process information. These devices share the same charge carriers as biological systems and bring hope for better emulating the neural functions and developing ionic circuits for neuromorphic applications. Specially, theory and experiments suggest that nanoconfinement is essential for inducing a memory effect, which places limit on the pore size to nm-scale or smaller. Such devices are difficult to scale up with precision and operate with long-term stability. Here, we show that a micrometer size pore, generally expected to exhibit a linear ion transport, can display a pronounced memory effect, if its rim is wrapped by strongly curved and tightly stacked graphene. We attribute the observation to slow ion dynamics confined in the rippled graphene edges. The devices are easy to scale up and integrate into fluidic circuits. The memory effect is ion-selective and exhibits long endurance comparable to the lifetime of synaptic proteins, which enables reversible modification of the conductance states using programmable voltage spikes and various electrolytes over a long time, akin to biological synaptic plasticity. Thanks to this plasticity, our devices and their integrated circuits enable storing, transmitting and processing information with high reliability, fidelity and accuracy, as evidenced in the identification of both greyscale and color images, and in the real-time analysis of emulated neural signals. Our results highlight nanoscale morphology of the pore wall as an important parameter regulating ion transport and indicate that the stringent nanoconfinement for ionic memory can be lifted from restricting the pore size to designing its rim structure. The devices and their integrated circuits may find use in ionic neuromorphic applications.

papers.title: A Survey on Long-Term Memory Security in LLM Agents: Attacks, Defenses, and Governance Across the Memory Lifecycle
papers.abstract: The emergence of writable, cross-session persistent memory in LLM agents introduces a qualitatively different threat landscape from conventional input-centric security concerns, characterized by three properties: persistence, statefulness, and propagation. To systematically characterize this landscape, we propose a Memory Lifecycle Framework that organizes attacks, defenses, and their cross-phase dependencies along two axes: six lifecycle phases (Write, Store, Retrieve, Execute, Share & Propagate, Forget & Rollback) and four security objectives (Integrity, Confidentiality, Availability, Governance). This analysis in turn exposes the need for explicit security requirements at the system level, motivating Verifiable Memory Governance (VMG), a framework of five architectural primitives for specifying and evaluating auditable, recoverable control over memory state within declared system and threat-model boundaries. Our analysis motivates integrating provenance, versioning, and policy-aware retention with retrieval and execution defenses to support auditable prevention, containment, and recovery across the lifecycle.

papers.title: Opportunistic Cooperative Sensing in mmWave ISAC Networks: A Meta-Distribution Analysis
papers.abstract: We propose an opportunistic cooperative sensing architecture for millimeter-wave (mmWave) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks that harvests bistatic echoes from already-active transmissions of neighboring base stations (BSs). Each target is sensed by its nearest BS, while neighboring BSs contribute only when their scheduled beams opportunistically illuminate the target. Cooperation requires neither beam reconfiguration nor dedicated air-interface resources and can leverage existing 5G transport and edge-computing infrastructure for synchronization and local echo processing. Using stochastic geometry, we characterize the sensing meta-distribution for cooperative ISAC, quantifying target-level reliability beyond spatial averages when multiple cooperative echoes are combined, while also analyzing sensing and communication coverage and ergodic rates. Results show that opportunistic cooperation substantially improves average sensing performance and target-level reliability. For instance, at a sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) threshold of 5 dB, increasing the maximum cooperative-cluster size from 1 to 6 raises the percentage of targets whose conditional sensing success probability exceeds 90% by over 55 percentage points. The results further reveal practical design tradeoffs in cluster sizing, BS densification, and sensing-communication energy allocation.

papers.title: Type-IV 't Hooft Anomalies on the Lattice: Emergent Higher-Categorical Symmetries and Applications to LSM Systems
papers.abstract: 't Hooft anomalies impose fundamental constraints on quantum matter and often lead to emergent symmetry structures upon gauging. We analyze a lattice model with four global symmetries realizing a mixed anomaly described by $\sim a_1\wedge a_2\wedge a_3\wedge a_4$, where the $a_i$ denote background gauge fields for the global symmetries. Through explicit lattice gauging, we demonstrate the emergence of higher symmetry structures, including 2-group, non-invertible, and higher fusion categorical symmetries. We also provide a field theoretical understanding of these results. Applying this framework to systems with Lieb-Schultz-Mattis anomalies, obtained by promoting part of the internal symmetries to translational symmetries, we demonstrate that modulated (dipole) symmetries and non-invertible translation symmetry arise as direct counterparts of those in systems with purely internal type-IV anomalies. Importantly, we uncover a qualitatively new feature absent in previously studied modulated symmetries and non-invertible translation: their realization can become intrinsically defect-dependent. In particular, the emergent symmetry structure changes depending on whether symmetry defects are present. This work establishes a concrete lattice realization of mixed anomalies and reveals a rich structure of emergent symmetries, thereby clarifying their role in constraining quantum phases of matter.

papers.title: X-ray spectroscopic responses to magnetoelastic symmetry breaking in altermagnets
papers.abstract: The multipole description of x-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), established through the sum rules of x-ray dichroism, provides a framework to describe magnetic and orbital responses in terms of ferroic multipole order parameters. X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) is known to probe spin, orbital, and anisotropic magnetic dipole moments. Its applications to altermagnets and noncollinear antiferromagnets have revealed that the XMCD response is often governed by the ferroic component of the photoexcited electronic states. In this work, we apply the multipole-based analysis of x-ray magnetic linear dichroism (XMLD) to altermagnets and demonstrate that XMLD response in altermagnets can be understood as a manifestation of magnetoelastic couplings between magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole moments. Using symmetry analysis combined with exact diagonalization calculations of $L_{2,3}$-edge XAS, we systematically investigate representative altermagnets, including $α$-MnTe, MnF$_2$, and CrSb. We show that the ferroic ordering of higher-rank magnetic multipoles, particularly spinful magnetic octupoles, gives rise to characteristic field-odd XMLD responses that directly reflect the underlying piezomagnetic response tensors allowed by magnetic point-group symmetry. Furthermore, we discuss XMCD responses induced by piezomagnetic effects, in which strain generates magnetic dipole moments. Our results establish XMLD and XMCD responses as element-specific probes of magnetoelastic multipole order in altermagnets and provide a general symmetry-based pathway to identify hidden ferroic multipoles and strain-controllable spin phenomena beyond conventional ferromagnetism.

papers.title: Loss-insensitive reduction of amplified quantum noise in a Raman amplifier with coherent feedback
papers.abstract: A quantum amplifier usually adds extra noise inevitably through coupling to internal degrees of freedom while amplifying the signal. The introduction of quantum correlations can effectively suppress this extra noise. In this work, we utilize the established quantum correlation between the Stokes field and atomic spin waves in the Raman amplification process to feed back a portion of the Stokes field into the amplifier. This leads to a reduction in amplified quantum noise that is independent of the feedback loss at high gain. A maximum of 6 dB noise reduction is observed. The single-path feedback amplifier is found to be sensitive to the feedback phase due to quantum interference, and we experimentally demonstrate an improvement in the signal-to-noise ratio of $4.4\pm 0.7$dB for a phase signal encoded in the feedback loop compared to the case without feedback. This general concept can be extended to integrated optics and fiber-optic systems with potential applications in quantum precision measurement.

papers.title: Image Generation with a Sphere Encoder
papers.abstract: We introduce the Sphere Encoder, an efficient generative framework capable of producing images in a single forward pass and competing with many-step diffusion models using fewer than five steps. Our approach works by learning an encoder that maps natural images uniformly onto a spherical latent space, and a decoder that maps random latent vectors back to the image space. Trained solely through image reconstruction losses, the model generates an image by simply decoding a random point on the sphere. Our architecture naturally supports conditional generation, and looping the encoder/decoder a few times can further enhance image quality. Across several datasets, the sphere encoder approach yields performance competitive with state of the art diffusions, but with a small fraction of the inference cost. Project page is available at https://sphere-encoder.github.io .

papers.title: Train Short, Inference Long: Training-Free Horizon Extension for Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models such as CausVid and Self Forcing enable efficient long-video generation through chunk-wise rollout with local sliding-window attention, yet suffer from visual degradation, appearance drift, and motion collapse beyond their training horizons. From a long-context sequence modeling perspective, we identify two underexplored inference-time bottlenecks in AR video length extrapolation. First, scarce high-quality long-video data and high training costs restrict video models to short training horizons. Consequently, low-frequency dimensions of 3D temporal RoPE remain under-exposed during training, inducing stronger spectral bias than in LLMs and hindering direct transfer of LLM context-extension methods. Second, both standard independent noise initialization and consistency-oriented methods with positive inter-frame correlation lack high-frequency dynamic priors to counter motion decay over long rollouts. To address these issues, we propose FLEX (Frequency-aware Length EXtension), a training-free, plug-and-play inference framework comprising three complementary components. Frequency-aware 3D RoPE modulation interpolates under-exposed low frequencies while extrapolating well-exposed high frequencies. Antiphase Noise Sampling (ANS) introduces negative intra-chunk correlation to inject high-frequency motion priors at initialization. An inference-only attention sink works with RoPE modulation to anchor global consistency. Experiments on Self Forcing and CausVid show substantial gains in long-horizon synthesis, with Self Forcing + FLEX matching or surpassing both training-free and training-based baselines on VBench-Long at $6\times$ to $12\times$ length extrapolation. Additional evaluations on Krea-14B and minute-level generation with LongLive demonstrate strong generalization across model scales, inference pipelines, and native long-video generators.

papers.title: Probing Plasmonic Oscillations in 2D Moir'e Nanocrystal Superlattices by Low-Loss EELS
papers.abstract: Electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) has been established as a powerful analytical technique for investigating the oxidation state, band structure, and dielectric properties of materials with exceptional spatial resolution. Inspired by twisted 2D materials, we utilize low-loss EELS to examine the plasmonic excitations in 2D moiré Au nanocrystal superlattices (NCSLs) formed by liquid-air interface self-assembly using a double-dipping method. This approach produces stacked hexagonal layers that can be twisted, forming moiré patterns in NCSLs whose twist angles are precisely measured via scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). Low-loss EELS effectively mitigates challenges arising from fabrication-induced non-uniformity and reveals a blue shift in plasmonic excitation when comparing single-layer, double-layer, and twisted configurations. This sharply contrasts with the optical spectroscopy measurements, which show an overall red shift relative to the EELS data. The high spatial resolution of STEM-EELS further demonstrates that twist-induced symmetry breaking strongly influences plasmonic behavior. Coupled dipole modeling explains the observed discrepancies: the electron beam excites out-of-plane polarization modes unavailable to optical probes, while optical measurements average over ensembles. Our findings highlight that EELS provides complementary information to optical spectroscopy for understanding how structural arrangements at the nanoscale influence collective electronic properties, advancing the design of plasmonic metamaterials.

papers.title: Geometry-Preserving Neural Architectures on Manifolds with Boundary
papers.abstract: A growing number of neural architectures have been developed to enforce geometric constraints, including projection-based networks, exponential-map updates, and manifold neural ODEs. In this paper, we study several such architectures, with the goal of understanding their approximation-theoretic properties and trade-offs. We distinguish between architectures that enforce constraints at intermediate layers and those that enforce constraints only at the output. For projected neural ODEs on uniformly prox-regular sets, we establish stability estimates and derive universal approximation results on compact smooth manifolds, including manifolds with boundary. In particular, we establish universal approximation of measurable manifold-valued maps in the $L^2$ topology. In contrast, architectures that enforce constraints only at the output can admit uniform approximation guarantees for continuous target maps under suitable geometric assumptions. We further investigate how the choice of constraint-enforcing map, namely metric projection or the Riemannian exponential map, affects these guarantees. While both constructions can be used to preserve constraints at intermediate layers, their use at the output leads to different approximation properties. In particular, exponential-map output architectures can encounter topological obstructions to uniform approximation, motivating approximation guarantees in $L^2$. On the other hand, metric projection-based output architectures can retain uniform approximation guarantees when the constraint set has positive reach. Our study raises the broader question of when the additional complexity of enforcing constraints at intermediate layers, as motivated by neural ODE approaches, and different choices of constraint-enforcing map are justified by the resulting benefits in approximation and learning performance.

papers.title: SAME: Stabilized Mixture-of-Experts for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance through instruction tuning, but real-world deployment requires them to continually expand their capabilities, making Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT) essential. Recent methods leverage sparse expert routing to promote task specialization, but we find that the expert routing process suffers from drift as the data distribution evolves. For example, a grounding query that previously activated localization experts may instead be routed to irrelevant experts after learning OCR tasks. Meanwhile, the grounding-related experts can be overwritten by new tasks and lose their original functionality. Such failure reflects two problems: router drift, where expert selection becomes inconsistent over time, and expert drift, where shared experts are overwritten across tasks. Therefore, we propose StAbilized Mixture-of-Experts (SAME) for MCIT. To address router drift, SAME stabilizes expert selection by decomposing routing dynamics into orthogonal subspaces and updating only task-relevant directions. To mitigate expert drift, we regulate expert updates via curvature-aware scaling using historical input covariance in a rehearsal-free manner. SAME also introduces adaptive expert activation to freeze selected experts during training, reducing redundant computation and cross-task interference. We also introduce a new benchmark to evaluate MCIT with long task sequence, and extensive experiments demonstrate SAME's SOTA performance. Code is available at https://github.com/LAMDA-CL/Prism.

papers.title: Self-Distilled Reasoner: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation improves large language model (LLM) reasoning by compressing the knowledge of a teacher LLM to train smaller LLMs. On-policy distillation advances this approach by having the student sample its own trajectories while a teacher LLM provides dense token-level supervision, addressing the distribution mismatch between training and inference in off-policy distillation methods. However, on-policy distillation typically requires a separate, often larger, teacher LLM and does not explicitly leverage ground-truth solutions available in reasoning datasets. Inspired by the intuition that a sufficiently capable LLM can rationalize external privileged reasoning traces and teach its weaker self, we introduce On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), a learning algorithm where a single LLM acts as both teacher and student with different contexts. The teacher policy conditions on privileged information (e.g., verified reasoning traces) while the student policy sees only the question; training minimizes the per-token divergence between these distributions over the student's own rollouts. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method on multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks, achieving superior token efficiency compared to reinforcement learning methods and better performance over off-policy distillation methods. Code repo: https://github.com/siyan-zhao/OPSD.

papers.title: Lattice QCD determination of the $γZ$ box contribution to the proton weak charge
papers.abstract: We present the first lattice QCD determination of the $γZ$ box contribution to parity-violating electron-proton scattering, $\square_{γZ}$, a key ingredient for the precise tests of the Standard Model via the proton weak charge. Our calculation covers the electron beam energies up to $E=155$ MeV. At $E=0$, the vector contribution is known analytically and excluded by convention; for the remaining axial-vector component we obtain $\square_{γZ}(0)=0.00411(9)$. Incorporating this result implies a value for weak charge of $Q_W^p=0.06987(50)$. The calculated energy dependence of $\square_{γZ}$ is directly relevant to the upcoming P2 experiment at Mainz, which will operate at the optimized beam energy of 155 MeV to extract $Q_W^p$.Although the systematic error budget in this exploratory study is not yet complete, this work establishes a lattice-QCD framework for computing the $γZ$ box contribution and demonstrates the feasibility of a first-principles approach, providing a foundation for future calculations with improved systematic control.

papers.title: PsyAgent: Constructing Human-like Agents Based on Psychological Modeling and Contextual Interaction
papers.abstract: Human-like agents must express stable dispositions while adapting to roles, relationships, and norms. We present PsyAgent, a schema-first framework that operationalizes the trait-context interface by coupling a Big Five trait prior with explicit social-structural conditioning. PsyAgent comprises (i) Individual Structure (IS), a machine-usable trait-grounded profile, and (ii) Multi-Scenario Contexting (MSC), a curated library of role-relationship-norm frames spanning eight everyday arenas. At inference, fixed structured prompts couple the active MSC frame with the IS profile, encouraging behavior that is stable yet context-sensitive. To demonstrate learnability beyond prompt engineering, we use IS x MSC to synthesize supervision and fine-tune compact backbones with PEFT (SFT and optional DPO). Under a controlled psychometric-style evaluation protocol in percentile space, PsyAgent improves trait-faithfulness and multi-turn persona consistency, and is competitive with several larger general-purpose instruction-tuned baselines under matched decoding and scoring controls. We further triangulate the automatic protocol with external benchmarks and a small blinded human study. Overall, PsyAgent provides a precise and data-efficient approach to personality-grounded, norm-aware agents.

papers.title: Bounds on screened dark energy from near-Earth space-based measurements
papers.abstract: We test screened dark energy with near-Earth, space-based measurements. In a post-Newtonian framework, we compute leading corrections to geodetic precession (Gravity Probe B), LAGEOS-2 pericenter advance, and the Sagnac delay in a prospective orbital configuration, yielding bounds on chameleon, symmetron, and dilaton models. LAGEOS-2 sets the strongest Earth-orbit limits on symmetron and dilaton, while a Sagnac setup at the projected sensitivity of state-of-the-art space clocks gives the tightest chameleon constraint. These results show that low-density, space-based experiments sensitively probe screened dark energy and exclude previously allowed parameter space. Notably, at an assumed delay precision of $\mathcal{O}\big(10^{-19}\big)$, a Sagnac test would exclude the entire chameleon parameter space considered.

papers.title: DEBATE: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Evaluating Opinion Dynamics in Role-Playing LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Modeling opinion change through social interactions is important for understanding polarization, misinformation, and societal conflict. Recent work simulates opinion dynamics with role-playing LLM agents (RPLAs), but multi-agent simulations often display unnatural group behavior (e.g., premature convergence) and lack empirical benchmarks for assessing alignment with real human group interactions. We introduce DEBATE, a benchmark for evaluating the authenticity of opinion dynamics in multi-agent RPLA simulations. Its three-round design makes each participant's public interaction history complete and traceable. DEBATE contains multi-round public messages and private Likert-scale beliefs from U.S.-based participants across 107 topics. The dataset covers 2,788 participants in 697 groups, enabling evaluation at the utterance and group levels. We instantiate "digital twin" RPLAs with seven LLMs and evaluate across two settings: Next Message Prediction and Full Dynamics Simulation, using stance-based opinion-dynamics metrics. In zero-shot settings, RPLA groups exhibit strong opinion convergence relative to human groups. Across group-generalization tests with unseen participant groups and topic-generalization tests with unseen discussion topics, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen3.5-4B, and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 improves stance-based alignment and reduces excessive convergence, bringing RPLA group convergence closer to that observed in the corresponding human groups, though discrepancies in opinion change and belief updating remain. The dataset, benchmark website, and codebase are publicly available.

papers.title: Mega-MMDF and DeepfakeBench-MM: Benchmarking Multimodal Deepfake Detection Across Diverse Forgery Pipelines
papers.abstract: Audio-visual deepfakes can spread misinformation and enable impersonation, undermining trust in digital media. However, existing datasets provide limited coverage of forgery operations and their combinations, constraining detector development and systematic evaluation. We introduce Mega-MMDF, containing 100,000 real and 1.2 million forged clips across 22 pipelines spanning modality-specific manipulations, stacked forgeries, and joint audio-video generation. To assess its training value and enable fair comparisons, we develop DeepfakeBench-MM, which standardizes training and evaluation across 8 datasets and 10 detectors. Training-based detectors achieve their highest mean AUC when trained on Mega-MMDF, with gains of up to 0.0784 over the best alternative training dataset for each detector. Experiments on data scale and pipeline coverage further support the value of large, diverse training data. Cross-pipeline evaluations reveal bidirectional and asymmetric generalization. Training on composite forgeries does not necessarily enable detection of their constituent operations in isolation. Our analysis of altered inputs shows that modality masking can increase false alarms and missed detections, and temporal misalignment can raise mean predicted forgery probabilities. Together, these resources provide a foundation for understanding and improving multimodal deepfake detection, with publicly available code and dataset access subject to application and usage terms.

papers.title: Trajectory-based cycle-level pedestrian crash prediction at intersections: A novel non-linear link function for block maxima led Bayesian GEV framework addressing heterogeneous traffic conditions
papers.abstract: This study develops a cycle-level framework for estimating pedestrian crash risk at signalized intersections under heterogeneous, non-lane-based traffic. Existing approaches often assume linear relationships between covariates and parameters, oversimplifying the complex, non-monotonic interactions among motorized vehicles (MVs), non-motorized vehicles (NMVs), and pedestrians. To address this limitation, the framework introduces a non-linear link function within a Bayesian generalized extreme value (GEV) structure to capture how traffic effects vary. It applies extreme value theory through the block maxima approach using post-encroachment time as a surrogate safety measure, with each signal cycle serving as an analysis block. It also proposes a behaviour-normalized modified crash risk (MRC) metric to account for pedestrians' habitual risk-taking behaviour in Dhaka's mixed traffic. Seven hierarchical Bayesian models were estimated using Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulation and compared using the deviance information criterion. Models with a non-linear link function only in the GEV location parameter fit the data better than their linear counterparts. Results suggest pedestrian speed is negatively associated with crash risk, while flow and speed of MVs, pedestrian flow, and NMV conflicting speed show positive associations, though all remain uncertain. The selected model's MRC estimate was close to the observed crashes at a 93% confidence level tuned to this dataset. These results suggest that the non-linear structure adds flexibility for capturing the non-stationary and non-linear nature of traffic extremes. This framework is a step towards proactive identification of pedestrian crash risk and after wider validation, it could support adaptive signal control and safety interventions in mixed-traffic environments.

papers.title: Fractal basin geometry and the limits to predictability and reproducibility in deep learning
papers.abstract: Fundamental limits to predictability are central to our understanding of many physical and computational systems. In deep learning, training outcomes are often difficult to predict and reproduce even when extrinsic sources of randomness are controlled, yet the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Here we propose riddled basin geometry as a unifying dynamical systems mechanism: every initialization leading to one solution lies arbitrarily close to initializations leading to different solutions, forming a fat fractal with structure at arbitrarily fine scales. Using a minimal neural network model, we analytically establish the classical route to riddling and derive a near-zero uncertainty exponent: even sharp increases in initialization precision yield only marginal gains in outcome predictability. In deep networks, intertwined training destinations and near-zero parameter-space exponents provide robust signatures consistent with riddling across the tested architectures, optimizers and training protocols, offering a common dynamical account of otherwise disparate empirical observations. We further introduce functional uncertainty exponents, extending these diagnostics of scale-insensitive irreproducibility from parameter space to the learned functions themselves. Together, our results support riddled basin geometry as a candidate organizing principle for irreproducibility in deep learning, with practical implications for optimization and the reliable deployment of artificial intelligence.

papers.title: Imprints of screened dark energy on nonlocal quantum correlations
papers.abstract: We investigate how screening mechanisms, reconciling light scalar fields driving cosmic acceleration with local fifth force constraints, can be probed via their impact on nonlocal quantum correlations between entangled spin pairs, whose evolution on a curved background is affected by General Relativity (GR) and screened modified gravity effects. We consider a gedankenexperiment featuring a pair of massive, spin-$1/2$ particles orbiting the Earth, evaluating their nonlocal correlations through spin observables associated to the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality. Using a general formalism developed earlier for curved space-time spin evolution, we compute the effects of screening on the CHSH inequality, finding its degree of violation to be suppressed relative to the flat space-time case. Applying this formalism to the chameleon, symmetron, and dilaton mechanisms, we identify currently unconstrained regions of parameter space where the screening contribution is comparable to that of GR. While detecting these effects will be challenging, our work provides a proof-of-principle for testing screened dark energy through quantum nonlocality.

papers.title: Exceptional Jordan spectra and fermion finite selectors and joint quark tests
papers.abstract: We study an aligned direct-pairing construction of fermion masses from exceptional Jordan spectra. A coassociative restriction on an equal-diagonal Euclidean Albert element gives an equally spaced spectrum, while leaving its dimensionless spacing free. Restriction of the auxiliary symmetric cube to the monomial groups $Δ(3n^2)$ and $Δ(6n^2)$, for every $n\ge4$, classifies its invariant triplet selectors. Each triplet occurs once, but covariant mass operators retain substantial freedom beyond a fixed pairing. Our principal result is a complete joint quark test within this aligned class. Keeping a common spectral spacing and the centre ratio $s_u/s_d=2/3$, we allow every real spacing, all invariant triplets and independent positive hierarchy exponents in the two quark sectors. Logarithmic mass-shape ratios eliminate both exponents and reduce the down-sector constraint to seven inverse branches. Outward-rounded interval bounds show that every branch fails the up-sector test in the published marginal-input boxes at nine Standard Model benchmarks from the electroweak scale to $10^{16}\,\mathrm{GeV}$. The result also survives explicit padding for printed-number rounding. These boxes carry no joint confidence level and do not include model-dependent theoretical corrections. Earlier monomial prescriptions and one-parameter modular models provide complementary comparisons. The results constrain a specified mass law while leaving the broader Clifford-Jordan programme open. Reproducibility code is supplied.

papers.title: Towards Comprehensible Recommendation with Large Language Model Fine-tuning
papers.abstract: Recommender systems have become increasingly ubiquitous in daily life. While traditional recommendation approaches primarily rely on ID-based representations or item-side content features, they often fall short in capturing the underlying semantics aligned with user preferences (e.g., recommendation reasons for items), leading to a semantic-collaborative gap. Recently emerged LLM-based feature extraction approaches also face a key challenge: how to ensure that LLMs possess recommendation-aligned reasoning capabilities and can generate accurate, personalized reasons to mitigate the semantic-collaborative gap. To address these issues, we propose a novel Content Understanding from a Collaborative Perspective framework (CURec), which generates collaborative-aligned content features for more comprehensive recommendations. CURec first adapts the LLM with recommendation objectives through post-training, equipping it with instruction-following and chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities. Next, we use the LLM-generated features to train the recommender model. Then, we treat the user-item prediction scores produced by the trained recommender model as reward signals to guide RL-based refinement of the LLM, thereby improving the quality of generated reasons and pattern. The corrected reasons are directly integrated into the recommender model to enhance comprehensibility and recommendation performance. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of CURec over existing methods.

papers.title: An introduction to the symmetric group algebra
papers.abstract: This is an introduction to the group algebras of the symmetric groups, written for a quarter-long graduate course. After recalling the definition of group algebras (and monoid algebras) in general, as well as basic properties of permutations, we introduce several families of elements in the symmetric group algebras $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$ such as the Young--Jucys--Murphy elements, the (sign-)integrals and the conjugacy class sums. Then comes a chapter on group actions and representations in general, followed by the core of this text: a study of the representations of symmetric groups (i.e., of left $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$-modules), including the classical theory of Young tableaux and Young symmetrizers. We prove in detail the main facts including the characterization of irreducible representations (in characteristic $0$), the Garnir relations, the standard basis theorem, the description of duals of Specht modules, and the hook length formula, as well as a number of less known results. Finally, we describe several bases of $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$ that arise from the study of Specht modules, including the Murphy cellular bases. The methods used are elementary and computational. We aim to assume as little as possible of the base ring $\mathbf{k}$, and to use as little as possible from representation theory (nothing more advanced than Maschke and Jordan--Hölder). Over 100 exercises (without solutions) are scattered through the text.

papers.title: Rapid Mixing of Glauber Dynamics for Monotone Systems via Entropic Independence
papers.abstract: We study the mixing time of Glauber dynamics on monotone systems. For monotone systems satisfying the entropic independence condition, we prove a new mixing time comparison result for Glauber dynamics. For concrete applications, we obtain mixing time bounds from specified extremal configurations: $\tilde{O}(n)$ for the random cluster model induced by the ferromagnetic Ising model with consistently biased external fields, and $\tilde{O}(n^2)$ for the bipartite hardcore model under the one-sided uniqueness condition, where $n$ is the number of variables in the corresponding models, improving the best known results in [Chen and Zhang, SODA'23] and [Chen, Liu, and Yin, FOCS'23], respectively. Our proof combines ideas from the stochastic dominance argument in the classical censoring inequality and the recently developed high-dimensional expanders. The key step in the proof is a novel comparison result between the Glauber dynamics and the field dynamics for monotone systems.

papers.title: LoopNav: Benchmarking Spatial Consistency in World Models
papers.abstract: The ability to simulate the world in a spatially consistent manner is a crucial requirement for effective world models. Such a model enables high-quality visual generation, and also ensures the reliability of world models for downstream tasks such as simulation and planning. It must not only retain long-horizon observational information, but also enables the construction of explicit or implicit internal spatial representations. However, existing datasets do not explicitly enforce spatial consistency constraints, limiting both the ability to systematically evaluate this capability and to learn it through data-driven approaches. Furthermore, most existing benchmarks primarily emphasize visual coherence or generation quality, neglecting the requirement of long-range spatial consistency. To bridge this gap, we propose LoopNav, a dataset and corresponding benchmark centered on loop-based navigation for evaluating spatial consistency. The dataset comprises 200 hours of loop-based navigation videos with actions, collected from diverse locations in the open-world environment of Minecraft. We further introduce a Scene Graph Consistency Score(SGCS) to quantify spatial consistency while remaining invariant to pixel-level variations. Dataset, benchmark, and code are open-sourced to support future research.

papers.title: Structure of the Cayley-Dickson algebras
papers.abstract: Viewing the Cayley-Dickson process as a graded construction provides a rigorous definition of associativity consisting of three classes, which divides the non-associ\-ative parts into four types. These simplify the Moufang loop identities and Malcev's identity and categorise non-associative loops. Analysing the non-associativity structure of sedenions and higher level Cayley-Dickson algebras uncovers octonion and three quasi-octonion, power-associative subalgebras. Power-associativity is proved to grow by multiples of seven that introduce zero divisors in factors of 84 for all Cayley-Dickson algebras. It is convenient to replace the terminology hypercomplex numbers with ultracomplex numbers to capture the fact that sedenions and all higher level Cayley-Dickson algebras contain quasi-octonions that are ultracomplex. The non-associative types reduce the 84 zero divisors in sedenions via three cycles and four modes down to seven primary zero divisor pairs of two-term sums of basis elements providing new techniques to analyse the seven quasi-octonions loops in sedenions. The graded notation allows the eight octonion and seven quasi-octonion subalgebras of sedenions to be uniquely derived, up to representation. The zero divisors for split sedenion algebras are analysed and mappings between three of these are described showing 180 zero divisors and the other split algebra is analogous to sedenions with 84 zero divisors. These split algebras are shown to involve quasi-octonion algebras with mixed signature.

papers.title: Performance guarantees for optimization-based state estimation using turnpike properties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop novel accuracy and performance guarantees for optimal state estimation of general nonlinear systems (in particular, moving horizon estimation, MHE). Our results rely on a turnpike property of the optimal state estimation problem, which essentially states that the omniscient infinite-horizon solution involving all past and future data serves as turnpike for the solutions of finite-horizon estimation problems involving a subset of the data. This leads to the surprising observation that MHE problems naturally exhibit a leaving arc, which may have a strong negative impact on the estimation accuracy. To address this, we propose a delayed MHE scheme, and we show that the resulting performance (both averaged and non-averaged) is approximately optimal and achieves bounded regret with respect to the infinite-horizon solution, with error terms that can be made arbitrarily small by an appropriate choice of the delay. In various simulation examples, we observe that already a very small delay in the MHE scheme is sufficient to significantly improve the overall estimation error by 20-25% compared to standard MHE (without delay). This finding is of great importance for practical applications (especially for monitoring, fault detection, and parameter estimation) where a small delay in the estimation is rather irrelevant but may significantly improve the estimation results.

papers.title: Quantum state transfer of superposed multi-photon states via phonon-induced dynamic resonance in an optomechanical system
papers.abstract: We propose a method to transfer macroscopically superposed states between two optical cavities mediated by a mechanical oscillator, which works in a nonlinear regime of optomechanical interaction. The scheme relies on phonon-induced dynamic resonance, where the motion of the mechanical oscillator dynamically sets on/off the resonance between the two cavities. It assumes the high-amplitude limit of the oscillator, weak coupling between optical cavities, and the adiabatic approximation. We show that, under these conditions, various multi-photon quantum states, especially Schr{ö}dinger cat states, can be faithfully transferred in a deterministic process. Our approach thus suggests the possibility of transferring large-photon-number quantum states, beyond the few-photon regime typically accessible with linearized optomechanical interactions.

papers.title: Deep Learning-based Approaches for State Space Models: A Selective Review
papers.abstract: State-space models (SSMs) offer a powerful framework for dynamical system analysis, wherein the temporal dynamics of the system are assumed to be captured through the evolution of the latent states, which govern the values of the observations. This paper provides a selective review of recent advancements in deep neural network-based approaches for SSMs, and presents a unified perspective for discrete-time deep state space models and continuous-time ones such as latent neural Ordinary Differential and Stochastic Differential Equations. It starts with an overview of the classical maximum likelihood based approach for learning SSMs, reviews the variational autoencoder as a general learning pipeline for neural network-based approaches in the presence of latent variables, and discusses in detail representative deep learning models that fall under the SSM framework. Very recent developments, where SSMs are used as standalone architectural modules for improving efficiency in sequence modeling, are also examined. Finally, we present examples involving nowcasting and irregularly sampled time-series data, together with a brief overview of scientific applications based on mechanistically structured SSMs.

papers.title: The Well: a Large-Scale Collection of Diverse Physics Simulations for Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Machine learning based surrogate models offer researchers powerful tools for accelerating simulation-based workflows. However, as standard datasets in this space often cover small classes of physical behavior, it can be difficult to evaluate the efficacy of new approaches. To address this gap, we introduce the Well: a large-scale collection of datasets containing numerical simulations of a wide variety of spatiotemporal physical systems. The Well draws from domain experts and numerical software developers to provide 15TB of data across 16 datasets covering diverse domains such as biological systems, fluid dynamics, acoustic scattering, as well as magneto-hydrodynamic simulations of extra-galactic fluids or supernova explosions. These datasets can be used individually or as part of a broader benchmark suite. To facilitate usage of the Well, we provide a unified PyTorch interface for training and evaluating models. We demonstrate the function of this library by introducing example baselines that highlight the new challenges posed by the complex dynamics of the Well. The code and data is available at https://github.com/PolymathicAI/the_well.

papers.title: A Chinese Continuous Sign Language Dataset Based on Complex Environments
papers.abstract: The current bottleneck in continuous sign language recognition (CSLR) research lies in the fact that most publicly available datasets are limited to laboratory environments or television program recordings, resulting in a single background environment with uniform lighting, which significantly deviates from the diversity and complexity found in real-life scenarios. To address this challenge, we have constructed a new, large-scale dataset for Chinese continuous sign language (CSL) based on complex environments, termed the complex environment - chinese sign language dataset (CE-CSL). This dataset encompasses 5,988 continuous CSL video clips collected from daily life scenes, featuring more than 70 different complex backgrounds to ensure representativeness and generalization capability. To tackle the impact of complex backgrounds on CSLR performance, we propose a time-frequency network (TFNet) model for continuous sign language recognition. This model extracts frame-level features and then utilizes both temporal and spectral information to separately derive sequence features before fusion, aiming to achieve efficient and accurate CSLR. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves significant performance improvements on the CE-CSL, validating its effectiveness under complex background conditions. Additionally, our proposed method has also yielded highly competitive results when applied to three publicly available CSL datasets.

papers.title: Secure Distributed Matrix Multiplication with Precomputation
papers.abstract: We consider secure distributed matrix multiplication, in which a user computes the product of two matrices with the help of honest-but-curious servers, any $T$ of which may collude. Using the outer-product partition, the matrices are split into $K$ and $L$ blocks and hidden by random masks. Assuming the user has precomputed the products of the random matrices, we develop methods that use this precomputation to reduce the number of servers required. Polynomial codes are designed through degree tables, whose distinct entries count the servers. We show that precomputation can reduce the minimum number of servers by designing degree tables specifically for this setting. For Gap Additive Secure Polynomial (GASPr) codes, we give a precise formula and show that it is monotone in the chain length $r$, so only the extremes GASP_small and GASP_big matter. We also prove lower bounds attained by GASP_small in several regimes. Consequently, any fraction of colluding servers below one can be tolerated, compared to the threshold of one half without precomputation, and the order of the total computational complexity decreases when the colluders are a fixed fraction of the servers. We show that no existing construction uses fewer servers than the better of GASP_small and GASP_big once the mask products are precomputed. We introduce Gap-Reduced Additive Secure Polynomial (GRASP) codes, which retain a single interval for the mask degrees while selecting the information degrees carefully. For $K = T = 4$ and every $L \geq 3$, we give an explicit GRASP code that uses one fewer server than every GASPr code and is within two servers of optimal. For large $T$, the configuration becomes an integer packing problem independent of $T$, and the number of servers saved by GRASP over GASPr grows quadratically in $K$ and $L$.

papers.title: A characterization of compactness via bilinear $T1$ theorem
papers.abstract: In this paper we develop the bilinear $T1$ theorem to characterize the (weighted) compactness of bilinear Calderón-Zygmund operators. Let $T$ be a bilinear operator associated with a standard bilinear Calderón-Zygmund kernel. We prove that $T$ can be extended to a compact bilinear operator from $L^{p_1}(w_1^{p_1}) \times L^{p_2}(w_2^{p_2})$ to $L^p(w^p)$ for all exponents $\frac1p = \frac{1}{p_1} + \frac{1}{p_2}>0$ with $p_1, p_2 \in (1, \infty]$ and for all weights $(w_1, w_2) \in A_{(p_1, p_2)}$ if and only if the following hypotheses hold: (H1) $T$ is associated with a compact bilinear Calderón-Zygmund kernel, (H2) $T$ satisfies the weak compactness property, and (H3) $T(1,1), T^{*1}(1,1), T^{*2}(1,1) \in \mathrm{CMO}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. This is also equivalent to the endpoint compactness: (1) $T$ is compact from $L^1(w_1) \times L^1(w_2)$ to $L^{\frac12, \infty}(w^{\frac12})$ for all $(w_1, w_2) \in A_{(1, 1)}$, or (2) $T$ is compact from $L^{\infty}(w_1^{\infty}) \times L^{\infty}(w_2^{\infty})$ to $\mathrm{CMO}_λ(w^{\infty})$ for all $(w_1, w_2) \in A_{(\infty, \infty)}$. Besides, any of these properties is equivalent to the fact that $T$ admits a compact bilinear dyadic representation. Our main approaches consist of the following new ingredients: (i) a resulting representation of a compact bilinear Calderón-Zygmund operator as an average of some compact bilinear dyadic shifts and paraproducts; (ii) extrapolation of endpoint compactness for bilinear operators; and (iii) compactness criterion in weighted Lorentz spaces. Finally, to illustrate the applicability of our result, we demonstrate the hypotheses (H1)-(H3) through examples including bilinear continuous/dyadic paraproducts, bilinear pseudo-differential operators, and bilinear commutators.

papers.title: Space-Efficient Interior Point Method, with applications to Linear Programming and Maximum Weight Bipartite Matching
papers.abstract: We study the problem of solving linear programs in the streaming model. Given a constraint matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and vectors $b\in\mathbb{R}^m, c\in\mathbb{R}^n$, we develop a space-efficient interior point method that optimizes solely on the dual program. To this end, we obtain efficient algorithms for various different problems. For general linear programs whose feasible region lies in a ball of radius $R$ and contains a ball of radius $r$ with known center, we can solve them in $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{n}\log(mR^2\|c\|_2/(rε)))$ passes and $\widetilde{O}(n^2)$ space for an $ε$-approximate solution. To the best of our knowledge, this is the most efficient LP solver in streaming with no polynomial dependence on $m$ for both space and passes. For bipartite graphs, we can solve the minimum vertex cover and maximum weight matching problems (with polynomially bounded integer weights) in $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{m})$ passes and $\widetilde{O}(n)$ space. In addition to our space-efficient IPM, we also give algorithms for solving SDD systems and the isolation lemma in $\widetilde{O}(n)$ space, which are the cornerstones for our graph results.

papers.title: Non-Abelian Quantum Turbulence in Spinor Bose-Einstein Condensates
papers.abstract: We numerically investigate statistically steady quantum turbulence in the cyclic phase of a spin-2 spinor Bose--Einstein condensate (BEC) driven by large-scale energy injection via a divergence-free external velocity field. In the full non-Abelian cyclic system, the mass-current spectrum exhibits an anomalous $k^{-7/3}$ scaling, whereas the spin-current spectrum approximately follows a $k^{-5/3}$ power law. To isolate the role of non-Abelian vortex dynamics, we compare this system with an Abelian-restricted cyclic system sharing the same Hamiltonian parameters and driving conditions. Strikingly, the Abelian restriction collapses both the mass- and spin-current spectra into a single $k^{-5/3}$ scaling, identical to that of a scalar BEC, despite the three distinct turbulent states maintaining nearly identical vortex-line densities. A Helmholtz decomposition reveals that the mass- and spin-current spectra are predominantly incompressible and transverse, respectively, thereby confirming that the anomalous scaling cannot be attributed simply to compressible fluctuations or to the transverse nature of the energy injection. Local spectral exponents further quantify these distinct scaling regimes.
