In initially neutral models, shock ionization can overcome geometric dilution: the total DM reverses from decline to growth after approximately $10$--$20$ yr and later turns over as the finite reservoir is processed. Ionized-upstream models instead generally decline or flatten. Without fitting individual sources, our models span both signs and the approximate magnitudes of the secular DM-variation rates measured among repeaters. In this dynamical framework, DM evolution is set by shock propagation through the circumsource density and ionization structure, rather than the contemporaneous burst rate, distinguishing it from photoionization-driven scenarios. Consequently, in our model, an instantaneous \(d{\rm DM}/dt\) is not a unique indicator of source age. We suggest that the observed distribution of secular DM variation slope amplitudes and signs will be important for distinguishing among different models of DM variations in repeating FRBs.

papers.title: Thermalization and quantum chaos in a pure gauge discrete non-Abelian lattice gauge theory
papers.abstract: Gauge theories constitute the basis of our microscopic description of fundamental physical laws, and they are a cornerstone of contemporary scientific research. Yet, how such systems thermalize far from equilibrium remains a fundamental open question at the crossroads of statistical, high-energy, and condensed-matter physics. In this work, we investigate the thermalization properties of non-Abelian lattice gauge theories, focusing on the discrete gauge group $D_3$, which is ideally suited for current qudit-based quantum simulators. Specifically, we study a linear plaquette chain in a gauge-fixed formulation that removes unphysical degrees of freedom. A numerical analysis of the Hamiltonian spectrum and expectation values of local operators shows a behavior broadly aligned with the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH). We also study thermalization through the real-time dynamics of the entanglement spectrum, confirming the emergence of random-matrix level statistics after an initial transient. Our results expand the rich phenomenology of dihedral non-Abelian gauge systems. Once the relevant symmetry structure is properly resolved, the model displays the same qualitative ETH-based thermalization scenario observed in Abelian gauge models and generic non-integrable quantum many-body systems.

papers.title: Onset of quantum chaos in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories
papers.abstract: We exhibit random matrix statistics in the scaling dimensions of non-BPS primary operators in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories. Specifically, we consider the sigma model with K3 target space and $\mathcal N=(4,4)$ supersymmetry in a neighborhood of the Kummer orbifold point $\mathbb T^4/\mathbb Z_2$. At the free-fermion radius, the spin-zero spectrum of the $\mathbb Z_2^4$-invariant sector is exactly degenerate at integer energies. The exactly marginal blow-up deformations that preserve this symmetry form a four-dimensional space, whose directions we parametrize by unit quaternions. Along each deformation direction, we compute the first-order splitting of the degenerate levels, i.e., the leading anomalous dimensions as the coupling goes to zero. In sectors where all exact symmetries are resolved, including a hidden $\mathbb Z_2$ at the even levels, the non-zero first-order shifts along a generic direction follow the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (GOE), as we verify by computing several spectral diagnostics. We compare quantitatively with the well-known singlet deformation, which has enhanced symmetry: even after all its known symmetries are resolved, its first-order spectrum has exact degeneracies, its gap ratio approaches the GOE value only slowly as the energy increases, and its unfolded spectrum lacks the long-range rigidity of the GOE.

papers.title: Topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry
papers.abstract: Chiral (or sublattice) symmetry describes bipartite systems such as the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain where same-sublattice A-A and B-B hoppings are forbidden, enabling the protection of topological phases. Here we identify new topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry wherein chiral symmetry is preserved on only one sublattice, as may occur with sublattice imbalance (e.g. graphene-hBN) or localized orbitals (e.g. zincblende). Unlike conventional symmetry operators described by group theory, half-chiral symmetry is an algebraic constraint on the sublattice-projected Hamiltonian such as $PHP=0$, requiring a new framework for topological protection. We develop such a framework, identifying real-space bulk topological invariants and corresponding topological boundary modes that stick to zero energy. In two dimensions we construct a half-chiral Kekule honeycomb model and show that its unusual higher-order topology protects a single zero-energy mode at a single corner.

papers.title: Moment bounds and UV reconstruction from curved positivity cones
papers.abstract: The fundamental principles of the S-matrix impose positivity bounds on the Wilson coefficients of EFTs, including the SMEFT. These bounds form convex cones that often have curved boundaries when there are degeneracies among the irreducible two-particle low-energy states. Numerical approximations have previously been used to evaluate these curved cones. We develop a moment-based framework to analytically carve out these cones, particularly those associated with anomalous quartic gauge couplings in the SMEFT. The framework also allows us to reverse engineer UV models from the curved boundaries of the positivity cones.

papers.title: The cosmological lithium problem and how decaying relics still solve it
papers.abstract: Lithium-7 in old stars is about three times below the prediction of standard big-bang nucleosynthesis, and deuterium lies slightly above it. Precise measurements of deuterium, helium-4, and the effective number of neutrino species now disfavor most previously proposed particle solutions. We find that relics that decay or evaporate with lifetimes of a few hours, mostly into electron antineutrinos of about a hundred MeV and into electrons or photons, still lower lithium-7 while respecting these measurements. Such relics include gauge bosons of $L_e-L_τ$ or $B-3L_e$ and heavy neutral leptons with a dipole coupling or mixing with $ν_τ$, with masses of a few hundred MeV, and populations of evaporating Q-balls that carry lepton number. The decaying particles substantially alleviate the lithium problem, while Q-ball populations reach the $2σ$ range of lithium-7 adopted by the Particle Data Group. These relics can shift the effective number of neutrino species by up to about $2.5$ times the precision expected from the Simons Observatory, and a future Galactic supernova can test the particles.

papers.title: Off-diagonal long-range order and $p$-wave pairing in one dimension from critical density fluctuations
papers.abstract: A central theme in the theory of unconventional superconductivity is that Cooper pairing can be mediated by bosonic collective modes other than lattice vibrations. However, collective fluctuations in reduced dimensions can also have a destabilizing effect on superconductivity, by suppressing long-range order or by destroying Fermi-liquid quasiparticles in the normal state. In this work, we study a one-dimensional (1D) model of spinless fermions with local interactions that exhibits a continuous quantum phase transition from a Luttinger liquid to a phase-separated state. Combining field-theoretic arguments with numerical exact diagonalization and matrix-product-state methods, we find that the quantum critical point exhibits two-particle off-diagonal long-range order and $p$-wave pairing. Our work shows that critical density fluctuations at a phase-separation instability can act as pairing glue for unconventional superconductivity in 1D, overcoming the disordering effect of phase fluctuations and the absence of long-lived fermionic quasiparticles in the normal state.

papers.title: The MURALES survey. IX. MUSE observations and results for 3C radio sources at 0.3 < z < 0.82
papers.abstract: This is the ninth paper in the MUse RAdio Loud Emission lines Snapshot (MURALES) project series, presenting the results of observations of 3C radio sources obtained with the VLT/MUSE integral field spectrograph. Here, we investigate the morphology and kinematics of the extended emission line regions (EELRs) of 26 radio galaxies at intermediate redshift 0.3 < z < 0.82 and their relation with the radio ejecta. EELRs are observed in all but 4 of the 26 sources extending as far as 160 kpc from the host galaxy. They show different morphologies and kinematics usually related with the radio properties. The five sources associated with the smaller radio sources show highly disturbed gas kinematics. Several EELRs have a filamentary morphology, often forming bubbles inflated by the radio lobes. The more extended EELRs usually have elongated morphologies and show well-ordered rotation. We then confirm the general results obtained from the study of the source at lower redshift: radio galaxies are surrounded by super-disks, that is, structures of ionized gas on scales of many tens of kiloparsec, whose properties depend on a combination of the evolutionary state of the radio source and its orientation with respect to the super-disks.

papers.title: Agent-guided construction of Feynman integral bases
papers.abstract: Finding bases of Feynman integrals whose differential equations are suitable for phenomenology is a remarkably verifiable task. We exploit this to design two \emph{skills} with which Claude Opus~5.5 produces novel results autonomously, working for several days. For a two-loop five-point family (with two masses and 18 elliptic sectors) and a two-loop superfamily for the radiative jet function with a K3 sector, the agent finds bases whose differential equations are free of poles in the dimensional regulator $\varepsilon$ and at most quadratic in it, and takes the jet-function one to $\varepsilon$-factorized form.

papers.title: A matrix model of an M5--brane on a plane--wave background
papers.abstract: We construct the maximally supersymmetric deformation of the recently proposed $\mathcal{A}_6$ matrix model on a plane--wave background. We derive the same theory independently, by reducing the light--cone M5--brane on a five--sphere in this background to its lowest harmonics, including the dynamics of its chiral two--form and of its fermions. We then classify all its classical vacua. We show that one of them is the fivebrane giant graviton, and that its fluctuations form a single $\mathfrak{su}(2|4)$ multiplet, which reproduces the $\ell=1$ level of the spherical transverse fivebrane identified in the large $N$ limit of BMN theory. Moreover, the dynamical tensor supports new families of vacua, where the flux balances the size of the brane, and whose spectrum contains that of a fuzzy membrane. Finally, we show that BLG theory sits inside the model, both on a Coulomb branch of the massless theory and around the giant graviton of the massive one, where the two membranes are polarized into the fivebrane.

papers.title: Topologically Obstructed Kondo Hybridization: A Route to Kondo Semimetals
papers.abstract: The interplay of strong correlations, topology, and symmetry can reshape the low-energy electronic structure of quantum materials and drive the emergence of novel quantum phases. In heavy-fermion systems, the Kondo effect entangles localized $f$ moments with conduction electrons, giving rise to coherent heavy-electron bands at low temperatures, typically characterized by a Kondo hybridization gap. Here we show, however, that the topology and symmetry of the conduction-electron Fermi surface can obstruct the opening of the Kondo hybridization gap at certain momenta. Treating the Fermi surface of a three-dimensional system as an effective two-dimensional manifold, we demonstrate that nontrivial topological invariants defined on this manifold impose a topological obstruction to opening a full hybridization gap, forcing the $fc$ hybridization to vanish at certain momenta on the Fermi surface. These hybridization zeros lead to crossings between $c$ and $f$ bands, giving rise to nodal points or lines near the Fermi energy within the Kondo phase. Our results establish topological obstructions to Kondo hybridization as a route to Kondo semimetals, revealing a fundamental connection between Fermi-surface topology and the emergence of correlated electronic phases.

papers.title: Little Red Dots at Cosmic Noon: Spectroscopy Reveals Declining Abundance but a Non-Evolving Luminosity Function Shape
papers.abstract: Little red dots (LRDs) are an extremely abundant population of red, compact, broad-line objects primarily found in the early universe. At $5<z<8$, they are at least 10 times more abundant than UV-selected quasars. Yet, how this population evolves towards lower redshift is unclear. In this work, we present our search for LRDs at cosmic noon ($2\lesssim z\lesssim 4$) in nearly 20 deg$^2$ of the Deep/UltraDeep fields of the Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program (HSC-SSP). Combining multiwavelength wide-field imaging surveys from 0.3 to 4.5 $μ$m, we identify 266 photometric LRD candidates. With spectroscopic follow-up from Keck/NIRES, VLT/X-shooter, and Magellan/FIRE on 24 candidates, we identify a sample of four LRDs with broad H$α$ emission. With the purity of the photometric sample calibrated by spectroscopy, we estimate the number density of LRDs to be approximately $6.8\times10^{-7}$ cMpc$^{-3}$ at $2.10<z<2.55$---this is nearly a factor of 35 decrease from their flat number density evolution at $4\lesssim z\lesssim8$ estimated from JWST spectroscopic surveys. The knee of the LRD optical luminosity function also remains consistently at $M_{5500}\approx-22$ mag across $2<z<5$, below that of quasars. We further speculate that only the abundance of LRDs, but not the shape of their optical luminosity function, evolves with redshift, and the Roman Space Telescope will be able to test this decisively with a substantially larger sample of low-redshift LRDs.

papers.title: Charge Exchange Illuminates Turbulent Cold-Hot Interfaces
papers.abstract: Cold-hot interfaces are ubiquitous in the multiphase circumgalactic medium (CGM), galactic winds, and the Galactic Center (GC), yet their microscopic contact regions are difficult to observe. Charge exchange (CX), in which a highly ionized metal ion captures an electron from a neutral donor and emits soft X-ray lines, directly probes these interfaces. We develop a subgrid CX model coupled to a nonequilibrium ionization (NEI) network in hydrodynamic simulations of radiative turbulent mixing layers. CX soft X-rays are confined to a thin, highly corrugated cold-hot interface (corrugation factor $\sim10$), whereas thermal emission fills the hot phase. Turbulent transport sustains high-charge ions at $T\sim 10^4$-$10^5$ K, where they encounter neutral donors. The low-temperature O VIII fraction exceeds that in a uniformly cooling isobaric parcel, demonstrating the importance of mixing to the ionization history. CX depletes this cool ion population, while continued entrainment maintains the supply. Including a metagalactic ionizing background changes the ion distribution and enhances CX surface brightness by a factor of a few in our CGM comparison, but preserves the cool origin of most CX emission. In the limit of sufficient neutral column, CX surface brightness is ion-supply limited: higher donor density increases local emissivity but shortens the reaction layer. The system-wide CX-to-thermal soft X-ray ratio also depends on the volume-to-interface scale $V/A_{\rm int}$, making CX a potential probe of multiphase structure in the CGM, galactic winds, and the GC.

papers.title: Water-ice formation in Ophiuchus follows the local irradiation
papers.abstract: Water ice only appears on interstellar dust grains beyond a certain depth into a molecular cloud. This depth has so far been quoted as one extinction threshold per cloud. We measured the threshold along 43009 sightlines through the Ophiuchus cloud with the ice color-excess method, which converts archival WISE and Spitzer photometry of background stars into the peak optical depth of the 3 $μ$m water-ice band. We sorted the sightlines by the 12 $μ$m surface brightness of the cloud at fixed extinction, a proxy for the ultraviolet field that excites the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons at the cloud surface. The onset of ice formation lies at higher extinction toward sightlines with brighter 12 $μ$m emission, ranging from $A_{K_S}^{\rm th} = 0.67$ to $1.15$ mag. It increases by 0.58 to 0.90 mag in $A_{K_S}$ per factor of ten in 12 $μ$m brightness, depending on the adopted reddening coefficient. Because the 12 $μ$m-bright and -faint sightlines lie in different parts of the cloud, we repeated the comparison within each of the five subregions, and four of the subregions show the same trend. The trend also persists among sightlines with a similar amount of diffuse material around them. A later onset in more strongly irradiated gas is expected from photodesorption by external ultraviolet light, although a comparison of its size with models requires a calibration of the 12 $μ$m brightness against the strength of the field. The extinction at which water ice appears thus varies with the local environment, which complicates comparisons between clouds. Photometric ice maps resolve this variation across entire clouds, and the SPHEREx and JWST ice surveys can test it spectroscopically.

papers.title: Blazars through the eyes of REDSoX and GOSoX
papers.abstract: Blazar polarimetric properties provide key constraints on the physical conditions within relativistic jets, offering insights into particle acceleration mechanisms, high-energy radiation processes, and jet composition. The Rocket Experiment Demonstration of a Soft X-ray Polarimeter (REDSoX) will serve as a precursor to the Globe Orbiting Soft X-ray Polarimeter (GOSoX), a state-of-the-art polarimeter designed for observations in the soft X-ray range (0.2-0.4 keV), with a planned launch for 2030. REDSoX and GOSoX will be the first (and currently only) X-ray polarimeters capable of performing observations below 1 keV, opening a new observational window into high-energy polarimetry. In this work, we investigate the soft X-ray polarimetric properties of blazars expected in the REDSoX and GOSoX band and assess the detectability of different samples of sources: one drawn from the RoboPol Monitoring Program, a statistically complete sample of gamma-ray-selected blazars spanning the low-, intermediate-, and high-synchrotron-peaked sources, and one cross-matched between the CAZ (CRTS, ATLAS, and ZTF) and eROSITA catalogs. We estimated the expected source fluxes in the selected energy bands through spectral energy distribution fitting performed with the Bjet-MCMC tool. We investigated the expected polarimetric properties under three competing emission scenarios: leptonic, hadronic, and hybrid, each one predicting distinct observational signatures. We assessed the detectability of every source by comparing our polarization degree predictions with the instrument's minimum detectable polarization function (MDP). Finally, we computed the detection probability for each source. This work offers a set of promising blazar targets for future observations with GOSoX, highlighting the mission's potential for probing relativistic jet physics through soft X-ray polarimetry.

papers.title: Lost in the Signal Model: Confusion Between Deterministic and Stochastic Gravitational Wave Signals in Pulsar Timing Array Data
papers.abstract: With growing evidence for the presence of a gravitational wave background (GWB) in pulsar timing array (PTA) data, it is imperative to understand how this signal will act as a foreground for other GW signals, particularly those from individual supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs), which are predicted to be detected in the next decade. For PTAs, since these two types of signals are long-timescale persistent signals, a signal from an SMBHB system may already be present in the latest PTA datasets. In this work, we analyze how the presence of this signal could affect our detection statistics for the GWB, and how the presence of the GWB can affect our search for the SMBHB system. We find that individual SMBHB signals can significantly skew the recovery of the GWB amplitude and spectral index. However, when the SMBHB signals are recovered consistently, we are again able to recover the GWB power-law parameters, highlighting the importance of joint searches in future PTA searches for GWs. We also explore the rate of improvement of parameter estimation uncertainty, giving insight to the types of signals most likely to be identified well enough to enable multimessenger analyses.

papers.title: PLATON 7: An ultra-fast exoplanet atmospheric retrieval code
papers.abstract: PLATON is an open source Python package for atmospheric retrieval, first released in 2018. We introduce PLATON 7, a complete rewrite of PLATON using Claude Fable 5. The biggest changes are that PLATON now uses JAX for all intensive calculations, and these calculations are now performed in single precision instead of double precision. These two changes speed up the code by a factor of ~60 with negligible decrease in accuracy, allowing it to compute a 0.8--5.3 um transmission spectrum at R=20k in 0.35 ms on a RTX 5090. We also introduce several new features, including support for two-limb retrievals, patchy clouds, and more opacities (particularly OCS and CS2). PLATON is available on GitHub at https://github.com/ideasrule/platon.

papers.title: Feynman integrals, coactions and Lie-algebra representations
papers.abstract: We outline a link between canonical differential equations of Feynman integrals and matrix representations of flat connections taking values in certain Lie algebras. Leveraging insights from string theory and properties of periods associated with these Lie algebras, we deduce single-valued solutions to the differential equations and coactions for the integrals. We introduce a novel form of the differential equations which connects with the representation theory of the Lie algebras and may depart from $\varepsilon$-factorisation in a controlled way. We illustrate the formalism through relevant examples.

papers.title: A posteriori estimates for inverse evolutionary problems
papers.abstract: The paper is focused on a posteriori error analysis of evolutionary problems, which are ill-posed in the sense of Hadamard. They may have no solutions and respective approximations may be highly unstable. For these problems, the a posteriori error estimation concept applicable to well-posed problems is not valid and requires a significant reformulation. A posteriori estimates of the functional type provide the basis for addressing this issue. They generate computable quantities that estimate the distance between a function (approximate solution to the inverse problem) and exact solution of a "close" well-posed initial boundary value problem associated with the same differential equation. The solution of this close problem exactly satisfies one part of the imposed conditions and the others are satisfied approximately with the accuracy $\eps$. This idea is elaborated for several evolutionary problems generated by the reaction-convection-diffusion equation: backward parabolic problem, problem with non-local time conditions, Cauchy parabolic problem, and parameter(s) identification problem. The estimates derived not only control the accuracy of approximate solutions, but also suggest a unified approach to calculating them numerically.

papers.title: Puzzles, People, and Publications: Measuring Shared Significance in Crosswords from 1942 to 2024
papers.abstract: Crossword puzzles are cultural objects that encode shared significance. We use interpretable, large-scale computational methods to analyze how crossword constructors, editors, and publications have adopted and adapted language to convey significance. Focusing on approximately 2.4 million crossword clue/answer pairs published in The New York Times between 1942 and 2024, we find shifting significance and differing editorial practices to be quantitatively measurable. By computationally measuring shared significance over time in crossword puzzle production, we are able to better understand cultural changes in the United States through the 20th and early 21st centuries.

papers.title: One Behavior, Out of Order: Deterministic Execution and Parallel Simulation of ROS 2 Applications
papers.abstract: System-level simulation is widely used to validate robotic applications before hardware deployment. However, Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2), a popular middleware for such applications, uses asynchronous publish-subscribe communication, which can make application behavior depend on scheduling and the platform. The behavior can then vary across runs and machines even with the same inputs. This nondeterminism makes faults hard to reproduce and tests unreliable. In this paper, we first give ROS 2 applications a lightweight coordination scheme in which every component, including event-driven ones, reads its inputs and writes its outputs at predefined time instants. By decoupling computation and communication, the scheme makes an application deterministic, that is, it always has one behavior for given inputs. Tests are thus repeatable, but for large applications they still take a long time. To speed up these tests, we then present an out-of-order parallel simulation algorithm. From the predefined read and write instants, it knows before the run which activations of components depend on which. It starts each activation as soon as those it depends on have finished. Finally, we implement the algorithm in a simulator that runs existing ROS 2 applications without any change to them or to ROS 2. We evaluate the simulator on industrial use cases and synthetic graphs. On the industrial use cases, it is up to 2.6 times faster than synchronous parallel simulation and needs an order of magnitude less memory for messages than asynchronous parallel simulation.

papers.title: Uniformising random greedy maximal independent sets on graphs with at most five vertices
papers.abstract: A random greedy algorithm scans the vertices of a finite graph in increasing order of independent exponential arrival times and accepts each vertex unless an accepted neighbour blocks it. We ask an inverse question: can strictly positive finite arrival rates be chosen so that the terminal inclusion-maximal independent sets are all equally likely? We call this exact property exponential greedy uniformisability (EGU). We establish the complete small-order classification: every finite simple graph on at most five vertices is EGU, with the unique exception of the five-vertex path $P_5$ up to graph isomorphism. A strict $2\times2$ probability minor provides an explicit obstruction for the exceptional graph; the positive cases are certified by graph-isomorphism reduction and exact constructive witnesses. We explain the independent-exponential-clock probability law and the formal Lean 4 verification, registered as Palomar PALOMAR-2026-11-19-000021 (version 1). The registration is a formal proof record, not a claim of novelty certification or journal peer review.

papers.title: A unified closed-form theory for elastic waves in polycrystals of any crystal symmetry
papers.abstract: The coherent elastic wave in random polycrystals is described by the first-order smoothing approximation, whose mass operator remains an integral evaluated only numerically. Here we derive its closed form for equiaxed, untextured polycrystals of any crystal symmetry with an exponential correlation function, giving an explicit dispersion equation at all frequencies. Unlike the integral form, which fails beyond one inverse correlation radius from the real axis, the closed form holds deep in the complex wavenumber plane, where heavily attenuated roots lie. It is compact, reproduces the dispersion equations of Stanke and Kino for cubic grains, extends them to any symmetry and contains the Born and far-field approximations as special cases. It reveals the structure of the roots and their partitions of the coherent field: three roots per polarization, one from the incident wave and one from each of the two scattering channels, without and with mode conversion. It also yields closed-form limits of their velocity, attenuation and partition in the Rayleigh, stochastic and geometric regimes, which show why a single coherent wave has been observed at long wavelengths, whereas more than one can be observed at short wavelengths. These results underpin further theory and quantitative characterization of polycrystalline microstructure.

papers.title: Error analysis for the numerical approximation of the quantile hedging problem
papers.abstract: We analyse numerical approximations of quantile hedging in complete linear markets with Markovian diffusion dynamics. The problem is formulated as stochastic control for an augmented state $(X,P)$, where the probability martingale $P$ is constrained to $[0,1]$ and controlled through an unbounded volatility coefficient. We combine control truncation with piecewise-constant policy time-stepping (PCPT), stopping controls continuously upon boundary hitting to preserve the state constraint. Using one-step dynamic programming principles and regularisation, we derive a generator inequality and explicit value-function error bounds. Under standard coefficient regularity and a Lipschitz payoff, optimising the truncation and regularisation parameters yields an error exponent arbitrarily close to $1/8$ from below, uniformly in the probability variable. For controls bounded from the outset, we obtain exponents arbitrarily close to $1/4$ from below, approaching the exponent established by Jakobsen, Picarelli and Reisinger without state constraints. We also implement a fully discrete scheme with neural-network controls. Grid-time projection onto $[0,1]$ introduces a martingale defect and a pricing bias. We quantify this bias in a toy problem and mitigate it using a state-dependent control bound. Experiments in Black--Scholes and Lipschitz local-volatility models illustrate the correction and the decrease in pricing errors under grid refinement.

papers.title: Cohomological $k$-Equivalence Does Not Capture Graph Isomorphism
papers.abstract: Ó Conghaile introduced cohomological $k$-equivalence $\equiv^{\mathbb{Z}}_k$, a refinement of equivalence in $k$-variable counting logic that is decidable in polynomial time for each fixed $k$: the local isomorphisms that survive must extend, in both directions, to compatible families of integer combinations of local isomorphisms. He asked whether, for every finite relational signature $σ$, some $k$ makes $\equiv^{\mathbb{Z}}_k$ coincide with isomorphism of $σ$-structures (Question 14 of his MFCS 2022 paper). We show that the answer is negative already for graphs: for every $k\ge 1$ there are finite simple graphs $A_k\not\cong B_k$ with $A_k\equiv^{\mathbb{Z}}_k B_k$. Every isomorphism of the pair would induce a permutation $g$ of a common index set $D$. One part of the graphs, over $\mathbb{F}_3$, admits exactly the even permutations, because $g$ acts by its sign on a nonzero class in the cokernel of the unsigned boundary map on subsets of $D$. A second part, over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and built on the Johnson graph $J(|D|,2)$, admits exactly the odd permutations. No set of at most $k$ vertices detects the parity: every local isomorphism of a common family is realised, with the same images, by permutations of both parities. We complement the main result with three observations. For the pair built from an index set of size $n$, the least width at which cohomological equivalence distinguishes the two graphs is $\log_4 n+O(1)$; so within this construction the doubly exponential size is unavoidable. The pairs are nevertheless distinguished in polynomial time by an explicit invariant that combines the class of the part over $\mathbb{F}_3$ with the parity of the part over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Finally, cohomological $2$-equivalence already distinguishes the coloured graphs with which Berkholz and Grohe show that no level of the Diophantine relaxation decides isomorphism.

papers.title: On the loss landscape of the linear neural network: beyond critical points
papers.abstract: While the critical points of the loss landscape in linear neural networks have been extensively studied since the seminal work of Baldi \& Hornik in the late 1980s, a description of this landscape at an intermediate or global scale is still lacking. Such a characterization is crucial, particularly as a substantial body of literature indicates that gradient descent circumvents critical points. The present article introduces an intermediate structure, termed the critical thalweg, which encompasses all critical points and exhibits key geometric properties. Beyond providing a geometric proof of Baldi \& Hornik's results using simpler assumptions than the existing literature, this framework offers a global view of the loss landscape that can be easily visualized in a two-dimensional plane. Empirical observations suggest that gradient descent is attracted toward the critical thalweg, along which the loss continues to decrease to its global minimum.

papers.title: A Solvency II-Based Framework for Pricing Structural Longevity Risk under an Affine Mortality Model
papers.abstract: This paper develops a Solvency II-based pricing framework for structural longevity risk in incomplete longevity markets. The valuation scheme relies on the Cost-of-Capital principle underlying the Risk Margin and combines it with a continuous-time affine mortality model. Mortality dynamics are specified in calendar time, with age-dependent mortality patterns linked to a latent longevity factor driving long-term mortality improvements. The affine structure preserves closed-form survival probabilities and provides a tractable basis for repeated Best Estimate, Solvency Capital Requirement and Risk Margin calculations. We derive the conditional distribution of one-year discounted Best Estimate variations, obtaining analytical expressions for their asymmetry and Value-at-Risk under the Gaussian affine specification. Within this setting, we introduce a stress-based assessment by applying adverse shocks to the deterministic parameters governing the longevity trend. The trend-based stress is compared with a mortality-level stress and with a Value-at-Risk-based capital assessment. The methodology links stochastic mortality modelling, prudential capital valuation and longevity-linked payoff assessment within a unified actuarial framework. A numerical application based on Belgian mortality data illustrates the implementation and shows that the mortality-level stress produces substantially larger scenario-based capital-cost measures than the trend-based stress. These findings highlight the sensitivity of longevity risk valuation to the specification of adverse mortality scenarios. The approach offers a transparent and operational basis for assessing and pricing structural longevity risk under a Solvency II Cost-of-Capital perspective.

papers.title: On the number of edge-disjoint $K_r$ in $K_{r+1}$-free graphs
papers.abstract: Gy\H ori and Keszegh [\emph{Combinatorica} \textbf{37} (2017), 1113--1124] proved that every $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+k$ edges contains at least $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint triangles. We extend this result to cliques of arbitrary fixed order. Specifically, we prove that for every fixed integer $r\ge 3$ and all sufficiently large $n$, every $K_{r+1}$-free graph on $n$ vertices with $t_{r-1}(n)+k$ edges contains at least $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint copies of $K_r$, where $t_{r-1}(n)$ denotes the number of edges in the Turán graph $T_{r-1}(n)$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $G$ is obtained from $T_{r-1}(n)$ by adding edges within one of its parts, with the added edges forming a triangle-free graph.

papers.title: How developers split roles among them and a coding agent and what "collaboration" means
papers.abstract: Background: Coding agents such as Claude Code become more and more competent, so that their role in the development process can grow. Objective: How do developers characterize the role-split between them and their agent? How would they ideally want to collaborate with their agent? Methods: We perform a 3-step, mixed-methods study. We apply qualitative open coding to 2025 early adopters' blog articles; perform a quantitative survey of 2026 practitioners; develop and apply a method for coding-agent-supported open coding of survey freetext responses. Results: The 2025 practitioners have the agent work in supporting roles only. Accountability was firmly human. In 2026, both are fundamentally still true. Gradually, however, the role-split is now different, with much more agent involvement. The developers' notion of collaboration has three facets: Predominantly a separation into human-only, agent-only, and collaborative work steps, with defined conditions and goals. Second, accommodating personal preferences without engineering justification. Third, a holistic view of collaboration covering the entire development process. Conclusions: Defining one's role relative to the agent will need to be a recurring activity. The different views on collaboration are likely a source of friction and conflict for teams; future work should find out how to cope with that.

papers.title: Stellar activity demotes GJ 9404 b to a planetary candidate
papers.abstract: GJ 9404 is a nearby M dwarf ($d=23.8\,\text{pc}$), around which a $13.4586^{+0.0044}_{-0.0067}\,\text{d}$ planet has been claimed in a recent study using 54 publicly available HARPS-N radial velocities (RVs). We re-analyse the spectroscopy associated with this study, and carry out a joint modelling of: (i) stellar rotation in RV, FWHM, and Mount Wilson S-index through Gaussian processes; (ii) long-term trends in all physical quantities; (iii) planetary signals in RV. Current evidence supports the existence of planets in the period range $2-100\,\text{d}$ by at most $Δ\ln Z=-0.4$ for any considered stellar-activity model, which is insufficient for a widely accepted planet detection. Additional spectroscopy is necessary to accurately quantify the stellar activity of GJ 9404 and determine whether any RV signals warrant further attention.

papers.title: Which Archived Results Survive a Rule Change? A Case Study in Revalidating Decisions
papers.abstract: A research workflow can retain a correct numerical result after the evidence or approval that supported its use has expired. Common incremental build methods identify reusable computations, while deciding what remains usable also requires knowing which policy justified each approval. We examined a recorded parser migration across 312 paired research records, replayed both parsers with the same inputs, applied a calculation-file omission to the complete cohort, and evaluated current proof in a GNU Make comparison. Treating the prior projections as current would change at least one field in 11 of 312 records, and controlled cases show that even matching values can lack a current proof. The study separates numerical recovery from applicable approval and sets out the conditions under which a maintained dependency graph can preserve both.

papers.title: Testing Settlement Flags after Late Evidence and Process Restart
papers.abstract: A settlement flag can survive an application restart while the economic effects remain ambiguous. We define a contract linking the fixed plan, source admission at two cutoffs, identity-keyed ledger effects and post-invocation state. We generated 504 synthetic histories, ran each through a file implementation and a separately coded SQLite implementation, and observed 672 controlled process exits. The file implementation missed 54 same-identity payment-date conflicts, including 27 that credited cash early, and a monitor using run flags, artifact presence and purchase counts accepted all 54. The same contract distinguishes a purchase awaiting closure from a correct quote wait for a single writer on a running kernel and filesystem.

papers.title: Eigenvalues and Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator in the Large-Friction Limit
papers.abstract: We study the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator by the methods of analytic dilation and phase-space deformation. We prove that in the large-friction limit $γ\to+\infty$, there are neither eigenvalues nor resonances away from the thresholds $γN$, and that near each threshold $γk$, there exists a bijection between the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and those of the Witten Laplacian at the level $k$, $-Δ_V^{(k)}=-Δ_V\otimes 1_{μ_k}-dΓ_k(\operatorname{Hess}V)$. We also show that each negative eigenvalue of $-Δ_V^{(k)}$, $k\geq 1$, produces a pole of the resolvent at distance of order $γ^{-1}$ below $γk$, whose imaginary part is $O(e^{-cγ})$ for every $c<2δ_V$. Here $δ_V$ is the width of a strip of analyticity of $V$.

papers.title: Adding One More Agent: How AI Team Size and Formation Shape Productivity and Diversity in Human-AI Brainstorming Teams
papers.abstract: Generative AI has improved individual productivity, but whether adding a plurality of AI partners helps or hurts remains open. We crossed AI partnership (one versus two) with behavioral formation (calibrated to average human behavior versus customized by the participant) in a brainstorming experiment ($N$=168) with human-human dyads as reference. Two-AI rooms posted more ideas to the shared board, but human-authored ideas dropped substantially. With one AI partner, formation mattered: humans paired with an average-calibrated AI posted more than any other condition. With two, this effect vanished. Humans continued talking but converted fewer ideas into board posts. AI social talk predicted more human posts, while AI posting volume predicted fewer. AI presence increased global diversity of human-authored ideas, but only a second AI increased within-session differentiation. The number of AI partners and their formation can reshape what the human contributes; single-agent results do not generalize to multi-agent teams.

papers.title: Detection of GRB 261010A with GRID-11B
papers.abstract: We report GRID-11B observations of the main emission episode of GRB 261010A. We measure $T_{90}=5.68^{+1.04}_{-0.32}$ s and a minimum variability timescale of $51.6^{+10.5}_{-9.8}$ ms. Its spectrum is described by a cutoff power law with $E_{\rm p}=1089^{+171}_{-80}$ keV. At both candidate host redshifts ($z=0.070$ and $0.785$), the low $\varepsilon$ values and their positions relative to the Amati relation suggest Type-I-like properties. These properties, despite the long duration, resemble those of GRB 211211A and motivate investigation of a possible compact-object merger origin.

papers.title: Möbius expansion and pointwise energy transfer over arbitrary fields
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a field of positive characteristic $p$, and let $A\subset F^\times$ have $N$ elements. We prove that, for every $λ\in F^\times$, \[ \card{A+λA^{-1}}\gg\min\{N^{10/9},(pN^2)^{1/3}\}. \] This improves the exponent $31/30$ to $10/9$ in the common small-set range. Over prime fields the bound strengthens to $\min\{N^{10/9},(pN)^{1/2}\}$. Analogous bounds hold for $Af(A)$ when $f$ is a Möbius transformation satisfying the stated nondegeneracy conditions. In characteristic zero, the bound $N^{10/9}$ remains valid. No subfield-avoidance condition is required.

papers.title: An ALMA Survey of Molecular Gas in the Host Galaxies of Fast Radio Bursts
papers.abstract: We present ALMA observations of CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) emission and millimeter continuum measurements for 9 localized fast radio burst (FRB) hosts at z=0.05-0.38. CO emission is significantly detected in 6 hosts and tentatively detected in one, yielding molecular gas masses of 2.2x10^8-1.0x10^10 Mo for a Milky Way CO-to-H2 conversion factor. All 6 detections show spatially resolved emission and large-scale velocity gradients, several consistent with ordered disk rotation. FRB positions do not necessarily coincide with the brightest CO emission, and no distinct kinematic component is identified at the burst positions at the present kpc-scale resolution. Together with published data, we assemble the largest FRB-host sample with CO measurements or upper limits to date. CO-detected hosts tend to have larger molecular gas reservoirs and longer depletion times than stellar-mass- and star-formation-rate-matched xCOLD GASS galaxies. They also tend to have higher molecular gas fractions and longer depletion times than expected from molecular-gas scaling relations. However, survival analyses including non-detections do not establish a significant difference in molecular gas mass or gas fraction. Both hosts detected in CO and HI have molecular-to-atomic mass ratios within the broad scatter of comparison galaxies. Our results highlight diverse cold-gas environments rather than a uniformly molecular-gas-rich FRB host population. At the position of the repeating FRB20201124A, the measured 98 GHz continuum flux density is above the predicted star-formation contribution and lies at the lower end of or below an extrapolation of the VLA spectrum. These results allow a compact persistent-source contribution and a possible spectral turnover between centimeter and millimeter wavelengths, although the present sensitivity and resolution prevent a firm separation from surrounding star-forming emission.

papers.title: Gravitational Wave Detection via Massive-Particle Interferometry
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) observations provide a powerful means of testing general relativity and exploring the physics of black holes and the early universe, motivating the development of complementary detection techniques. Here, we propose and theoretically investigate a GW detector based on massive-particle interferometry, in which the signal is encoded in the relative phase accumulated by a quantum particle traversing a closed-loop trajectory and a reference path. We derive the frequency-dependent GW-induced phase response and examine the parameters on which it depends. These parameters provide a means of tuning the detector response over a broad frequency range, motivating the exploration of tabletop detectors for GW signals at frequencies comparable to and below the LIGO band, in the idealized limit. By exploiting the trajectory-dependent gravitationally induced phase, the proposed scheme offers a distinct and potentially complementary approach to GW detection and motivates further investigation of its experimental feasibility and practical sensitivity.

papers.title: Cancellation-Free Constrained SquareCB for Safe Controller Selection
papers.abstract: We study constrained contextual bandits, in which a learner chooses one of $K$ actions in each round to minimize loss while keeping the expected cost of its play below a budget. Existing reductions to online regression weight the cost by a Lagrange multiplier learned from past constraint residuals, so slack in some rounds can offset violations in others. We instead run SquareCB proposed in \citep{foster2020beyond} with a rectified weight on the cost: it is zero when the estimated cost is within the budget, and otherwise just large enough to bring it back to the budget. Under realizability and Slater's condition with margin $δ$, the algorithm attains regret $O(\sqrt{KT\,\mathrm{Reg}_{\mathsf{Sq}}(T)}/δ)$ and cancellation-free violation $\sum_t(V_c^{p_t}-b)^+=O(\sqrt{KT\,\mathrm{Reg}_{\mathsf{Sq}}(T)})$, where $\mathrm{Reg}_{\mathsf{Sq}}$ is the error of the regression oracle. The same bounds hold when the budget must be met in every context, potentially adversarially chosen contexts. In controller selection for a safe-control-gym quadrotor and a BOPTEST building, the violation is 6 to 9 times lower than that of primal-dual and virtual-queue baselines, with a lower or comparable regret.

papers.title: All-Genus 2D $\mathcal{N}=1$ Superconformal Blocks
papers.abstract: We develop a numerical algorithm for two dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal blocks at arbitrary genera, in arbitrary plumbing channels, and for arbitrary spin structures. The algorithm utilizes two commuting copies of Virasoro subalgebras of the direct sum of the $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal algebra with an auxiliary free fermion algebra, which allows us to reduce the $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal blocks to Virasoro conformal blocks.

papers.title: A Scalable Decentralized Event-Triggered Topology-Switching Protocol for Verifiable Safe Control in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: This paper develops a decentralized event-triggered topology-switching protocol that allows agents to disconnect from the communication network while preserving state safety and excluding Zeno behavior. We establish a robust barrier function condition that guarantees safety as long as the estimation error remains within a prescribed threshold. Each agent uses locally computable certificates to determine when to connect and disconnect from the network. The certificate construction improves scalability by reducing the complexity of topology-dependent computations from $O(2^N)$ to $O(N)$, where $N$ is the number of agents. We formally prove that the protocol ensures the estimation error does not exceed the prescribed threshold and is non-Zeno. An alternating method computes an error-weighting matrix and a quadratic barrier function that guarantee safety under the proposed protocol. Finally, we evaluate the protocol on four interconnected microgrids. Compared with maintaining network connectivity at all times, the protocol reduces the time agents remain connected while keeping phase and frequency within their safe operating region.

papers.title: Equivariant geometry of quadrics blown-up along a twisted quartic
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be the blow-up of a smooth quadric threefold along a twisted quartic, and let $G\subset\operatorname{Aut}(X)$ be a finite subgroup such that $\mathrm{Pic}^G(X)$ has rank one. We prove that $X$ is $G$-birationally superrigid if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{A}_5\times\mathbb{Z}_2$. The action of $G$ on $X$ is linearisable if and only if it is projectively linearisable, and this holds precisely when $G$ contains no subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$.

papers.title: Estimating a Rational Inattention Discrete Choice Model: A Semiparametric Approach
papers.abstract: People's choices depend on both the payoffs of the available options and what they learn about those payoffs before deciding. This paper shows how choice data identify both unobserved payoff heterogeneity and the cost of information acquisition in a rational inattention discrete-choice model. I establish conditions for semiparametric point identification using exogenous payoff and information-cost shifters, without imposing parametric forms on the taste-shock distribution or on how the unit cost of information varies with observed characteristics. In the model with binary choice, I construct an unobserved choice threshold whose cumulative distribution function is the choice probability as a function of the payoff shifter. Moments of this threshold identify the payoff coefficients and the unit cost of information at each value of the information-cost shifter. A deconvolution argument then identifies the taste-shock distribution. I then extend identification to the model with multinomial choice. To estimate the model, I propose a sieve minimum-distance estimator based on observed market shares and establish its consistency. For inference, I construct confidence regions by test inversion because binding parameter constraints can make the estimator's limiting distribution nonnormal. In an application to Amazon Mechanical Turk, model counterfactuals show that lower unit costs of information raise the average task-taking probability and reduce wage elasticity.

papers.title: Toward Cross-Rubric Surgical Skill Assessment via Joint Embedding Prediction
papers.abstract: Expert review of surgical videos is essential for surgical training but labor-intensive, motivating AI-assisted skill assessment to provide feedback at scale. Although surgical assessment rubrics may use different language to describe similar skills, existing automated methods commonly predict predefined skill levels or numerical scores tied to fixed rubrics, limiting their ability to transfer across semantically equivalent assessment criteria. We propose Predictive Rubric Alignment (PRA), a joint embedding prediction approach that scores surgical videos using natural-language descriptions of skill levels. Rather than matching level probabilities, PRA predicts a rater-weighted combination of skill-level description embeddings. Adjacent description features define a score-parameterized path, and the predicted embedding is projected onto this path to read the score. We introduce two variants: \textit{PRA-item}, which uses learned queries for predefined assessment items, and \textit{PRA-cond}, which generates queries from textual item names to enable assessment of unseen items without retraining. On AIxSuture, a dataset of expert-rated suturing videos, PRA outperforms published baselines in skill classification. We further evaluate zero-shot transfer to the smaller surgical skill assessment benchmark JIGSAWS. Trained on only two AIxSuture rubric items, PRA-cond assesses unseen JIGSAWS items without further training, yielding positive score correlations and greater Grad-CAM overlap with instruments and suture than a description-matching baseline. These results support predictive rubric alignment as a promising direction for flexible and explainable automated surgical skill assessment.

papers.title: Broad-Persistent Advising in Interactive Reinforcement Learning via Latent State Encoding
papers.abstract: Deep Interactive Reinforcement Learning (Deep IntRL) accelerates reinforcement learning training by incorporating external advice. However, conventional Deep IntRL uses each piece of advice only in the current step and discards it after a single interaction. Persistent Advising and Broad-Persistent Advising (BPA) extend this process by storing advice in persistent memory and reusing it in similar states through state generalisation based on K-means clustering. This research proposes Encoder BPA, which employs a latent encoder to retrieve and reuse advice. In this framework, a trained encoder is used to map a state sequence into a latent representation at every time step. Advice can be retrieved through latent comparison, together with a top-(k) aggregation and a consistency condition to improve reuse stability. Experimental results show that Encoder BPA improves learning efficiency and advice utilisation at an early stage of training compared with different Deep IntRL approaches, especially in complex and partially observable environments.

papers.title: Riemannian Real-Time Optimization for Robotics: Active Set SQP Parametric Pathfollowing
papers.abstract: Robot optimal control often combines Euclidean states with configurations on Lie groups and other smooth manifolds. This paper develops a parametric Riemannian Newton pathfollowing method based on homotopy quadratic programs and parallel strict-working-set tasks. It specifies the event handling, working-set exchanges, matrix factor updates, synchronization, and residual checks used by the algorithm. Tracking guarantees are given under mildly degenerate regularity conditions and the Riemannian strong second-order sufficient condition. Drone navigation and arm manipulation are formulated as geometric optimal-control problems, including finite-force grasp acquisition, transport and supported release. Numerical examples illustrate drone navigation and arm pick-and-place through KKT-residual histories and MuJoCo simulations, together with preliminary initialization results for the full-horizon optimal-control problems.

papers.title: MARS: Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams for Video Forgery Detection
papers.abstract: Generalizing deepfake detection across facial manipulation and fully generated video remains challenging due to forgery traces varying with the manipulation method and scene content. Explicit spatial and temporal feature differences offer a way to capture this variation, but also respond to natural texture and motion, motivating their joint interpretation with appearance features. We investigate whether combining multiscale feature differences with adapted appearance representations improves detection across both forgery categories. We introduce Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams (MARS), a two-path video detector. The residual path applies fixed spatial and temporal difference-of-Gaussians operators to frozen intermediate features and models the resulting differences alongside appearance context across frames. The semantic path adapts the encoder's normalization parameters for frame classification, and a clip-dependent gate combines their predictions. Under a shared protocol across seven datasets, MARS achieves the highest average AUROC of 91.43\%, outperforming seven compared detectors. When trained on facial manipulations alone, MARS achieves 93.99\% AUROC on GenVideo and 75.50\% on DF26, demonstrating transfer to generated videos without generated-video training data. MARS also provides signed patch and frame contributions, whose faithfulness we evaluate through controlled spatial and temporal removal against random controls. MARS is publicly available for research: Project page: https://vectorinstitute.github.io/mars/ Github: https://github.com/VectorInstitute/mars

papers.title: Audit Before You Merge: Provenance, Probing, and Continual LoRA Composition
papers.abstract: Post-hoc merging of public LoRA adapters is an attractive gradient-free path to continual adaptation, but reliable measurement of catastrophic forgetting in this setting depends on infrastructure that prior work has not addressed. We treat each adapter merge as a sequential task in a continual-learning setting, with the instruction-tuned base model's capabilities as Task 0, and study forgetting on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Public adapter hubs contain modules that fail basic provenance checks: silent base-version mismatches and near-zero delta norms whose inclusion inflates measured interference by ~10pp. We propose a two-check audit (base-model match, non-trivial delta norm) and a leakage-free probing protocol as preconditions for any forgetting study in this setting. On an audited 4-adapter set, naive merging causes -10.5pp on GSM8K and -18.3pp on HumanEval, while Task Arithmetic at lambda=0.5 sits within a standard error of the unmerged baseline. A coordinate search including negative coefficients identifies the math adapter as probe-optimal at lambda=-0.5, outside the reach of positive-only mergers, suggesting forgetting has structure that negation-aware merging may exploit. The same protocol replicates on Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, where 2 of 4 candidate adapters fail the audit and the audited merge reproduces the same merge-method ranking on GSM8K, supporting that our findings are not Llama-specific.

papers.title: Physics-Based Differentiable Beamforming for Deep Learning-Based Contrast Enhanced Ultrasound Super-Resolution Imaging
papers.abstract: Ultrasound is widely used for vascular imaging because it is non-invasive, real-time, and cost-effective. However, its spatial resolution remains limited by diffraction to an order of the acoustic wavelength. This limitation is particularly restrictive for imaging of the microvasculature and high-resolution vector-flow-imaging. In this work, we present a multi-channel physics-based deep learning approach to super-resolve monodisperse microbubbles directly from multi-channel radio-frequency (RF) data. We also present a novel image-based metric for model evaluation. The proposed pipeline combines a learnable deconvolution network with a differentiable beamforming layer, enabling a direct deconvolution of the microbubble (MB) signature prior to image formation. By operating on multi-channel RF data, the method aims to improve localization robustness in the presence of dense microbubble populations and deconvolve the lateral direction in a relatively low-frequency regime (1.7 MHz) where MBs exhibit nonlinear behavior. The model is trained and evaluated on simulated data using monodisperse lipid-coated MBs over a broad range of acoustic pressures and microbubble densities. The proposed method improves the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) compared to the single-channel approach. It achieves sub-wavelength axial and lateral resolution while slightly improving robustness to dense microbubble populations outside the training domain. It also demonstrates generalizability across transmit configurations without requiring explicit training on each transmit configuration.

papers.title: On the dynamics of weighted shifts on Fréchet sequence spaces over trees
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give characterizations of Li--Yorke chaos, mean Li--Yorke chaos and distributional chaos for weighted backward shifts acting on general Fréchet sequence spaces over directed trees. As corollaries, we obtain explicit characterizations in the setting of Köthe spaces $λ_p(A,V)$, where $p\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ and $V$ is a directed tree. In particular, we obtain criteria for the case of the classical Banach spaces $\ell^p(V)$, $p\in[1,\infty)$, and $c_0(V)$.

papers.title: Precedence Constraint Scheduling on a Fixed Number of Machines
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic exact algorithm for $P_m\mid\mathrm{prec},p_j=1\mid C_{\max}$ for every fixed $m\ge3$. The algorithm constructs an optimum schedule in $$ O(L)+m^{O(m^2)}\, n^{6m^2+13m+1} \, {\log n} $$ elementary RAM operations, where $n \ge 2$ is the number of jobs and $L$ is the binary input length. Its word size is $O(m^2 \log n)$ bits. A direct implementation on a deterministic Turing machine with a fixed number of tapes uses $O(L)+m^{O(m^2)} \, n^{6m^2+13m+1} \, \log^2 n$ steps. Thus both models have polynomial degree $94$ for three machines, apart from the displayed logarithmic factors.

papers.title: How Many Shots Does a Quantum Reservoir Need? Measurement Cost and Its Scaling in Buffered Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) inherits from classical reservoir computing the property that only a linear readout is trained, but unlike a classical reservoir its state is never directly observable: every feature is an expectation value estimated from a finite number of measurement shots. The shot budget is therefore a first-class hyperparameter with no classical analogue. Its effect on QRC has recently begun to be studied; what remains unsettled is how a required budget should be defined, and whether competing definitions agree. This paper argues that they do not, and that the disagreement is systematic rather than incidental. This paper distinguishes a \emph{precision budget} $N_\varepsilon$, the shots needed to estimate the reservoir features to a fixed relative accuracy, from a \emph{convergence budget} $N_\star$, the shots needed for the trained readout to approach its own noise-free ceiling. Proposition~\ref{prop:confound} shows that $N_\star$ depends on the noise-free error floor by construction, so that a configuration with a worse floor appears cheaper, and that configurations should therefore be compared at a fixed measurement budget rather than by the budget each needs to reach its own ceiling.

papers.title: No Significant Rotation of the Spiral Structure in the IM Lup Protoplanetary Disk
papers.abstract: Spiral structures are often observed in protoplanetary disks, but their origins remain uncertain. Yoshida et al. (2025) reported a pattern speed consistent with local Keplerian rotation for the $m=2$ spiral in the dusty disk around IM Lup using multi-epoch ALMA observations, supporting a gravitational instability (GI)-driven origin. However, recent studies revise the disk geometry of IM Lup, motivating a reassessment of its spiral pattern speed. In this study, we reanalyze the disk geometry of the same multi-epoch data using visibility-based continuum emission modeling. The inferred disk geometries differ from those adopted in previous studies by a few degrees but are consistent across epochs and with recent independent estimates based on gas emission analyses. The revised geometries yield weaker residuals and more physically plausible radial spiral phase profiles. Unlike previous studies, our remeasured spiral pattern speeds are consistent with zero rotation within the uncertainties. We conclude that the previously reported Keplerian-like motion can be explained by a mismatch in the adopted disk geometry, which affects the spiral phases measured in Band 6 (2017, 2019) and Band 7 (2024) differently. In addition, we identify a tentative large-scale one-armed spiral-like structure extending beyond the known $m=2$ spiral, which may provide clues to additional perturbations, such as an embedded planet or late-stage infall. Future high-resolution Band 6 observations with a longer time baseline will be essential for more accurately determining the spiral pattern speed.

papers.title: StepX-OPD: Rethinking Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: A deployable text-to-image diffusion model must hold several capabilities at once, such as instruction following, text rendering and human preference, and must sample in a few steps. Capabilities and few-step sampling are built in separate stages: a full-step model first consolidates capabilities through multi-teacher on-policy distillation, then serves as a fixed teacher for step distillation. Every full-step model we evaluate scores lower once compressed, and the second stage cannot begin until the first finishes. We introduce StepX-OPD, which merges the two stages: one student acquires every capability while learning to sample in a few steps, so frozen specialists supervise it on the states its own rollout visits rather than on a longer trajectory it never runs. Motivated by a decomposition of the rollout's KL, we also regress the student's velocity on the low-noise part of the rollout. Separately, we find that capability integration makes models write prompt words into images on prompts that never asked for text, and we give a variant that lowers it. We evaluate on SD3.5-Medium and FLUX.1-dev across instruction following, text rendering, image quality and human preference. On both architectures, StepX-OPD attains the highest normalized average score among the four-step methods compared and exceeds the forty-step Flow-OPD model, and on SD3.5-Medium it trains with about 37% fewer GPU-hours than sequential DiffusionOPD followed by step distillation.

papers.title: Permitted but Unauthorized: Affordance-Induced Delegated-Scope Violations in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems place several agents on shared infrastructure, where each agent holds permissions far broader than the task it is delegated -- so every agent is routinely permitted to act on a peer's resources it was never assigned. We ask: under competitive pressure, what determines whether an agent crosses from its delegated scope into a peer's resources, and can such crossings be enforced away? We study this across eight LLMs in two simulated environments -- a CI/CD release pipeline and a security-operations incident queue -- using a deterministic, no-model-in-the-loop detector over hash-chained, replay-verified logs. In a controlled 2x2x2 factorial over competitive incentive, candidate visibility, and payoff information (three models, n=52 per cell), we find that action representation, not permission, governs the behavior: no agent crosses when the peer action is unlisted, whereas listing it under competitive pressure with a stated payoff raises crossings sharply -- up to 52 of 52 episodes for Claude Sonnet 4.5. We also observe a model-dependent split: two newer models (Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5) refuse the identical attack in 0 of 100 episodes, where prior-generation models cross in 9 of 10. We then evaluate two defenses -- a deterministic reference monitor and a model-based pre-execution judge -- both block every crossing and, when the task is winnable, cut avoidable peer deadline misses from 15/40 and 14/40 to at most 1/40. But scope enforcement is not harm prevention: an agent can still set a peer back through an authorized action on its own resources -- misreporting its incident's severity -- which neither defense detects. Our results establish action representation, not permission alone, as a controllable driver of inter-agent scope violations, and show that enforcing delegated scope is distinct from preventing harm, motivating effect-aware authorization.

papers.title: Eliminating Servers in State Machine Replication
papers.abstract: State Machine Replication (SMR) underpins many stateful systems, including distributed databases, coordination services, and metadata stores. Fundamentally, SMR requires state to be materialized from a durable total order of commands. Existing SMR systems rely on servers to materialize, locally store, and serve snapshots of state; while the durable total order either resides on the same servers, or on an external, disaggregated shared log. Unfortunately, servers act as brittle, expensive choke-points in such systems, causing service unavailability when they fail; incurring provisioning latency on cold starts; and red-lining when exposed to bad clients. In this paper, we propose Serverless SMR (S^2MR), where both the materialized state and the durable total order are stored on disaggregated storage; clients concurrently maintain a single copy of materialized state on external storage. Our key technical insight is that the shared log abstraction is useful not just for consistently ordering commands in SMR, but also for enabling distributed materialization, thus becoming the only interface for ac hieving SMR. We demonstrate S^2MR by developing AirDB, a transactional key-value store. In our evaluation, AirD B over S^2MR achieves higher availability than existing SMR-based systems like etcd over Raft: it is oblivious to server failures and bad client activity; and spins up 10x-45x faster from a cold start.

papers.title: A DG algebra structure for the edge ideal of any split graph
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit DG algebra structure on the minimal free resolution of the quotient of a polynomial ring by the edge ideal of any split graph (that is, a graph whose vertex set is a disjoint union of a clique and an independent set). The algebra structure is based on a simple combinatorial notion, which we call the fixing edge of a pair of edges, that directly captures the structure of the underlying graph. Our construction involves an explicit description of the minimal free resolution of the edge ideal of such a graph, including formulas for both the Betti numbers and the differentials.

papers.title: Time-Switching Energy-Harvesting Quantum Relay-Assisted FSO Communication with Displaced Squeezed Signaling
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a quantum relay-assisted free-space optical (FSO) communication system in which a decode-and-forward relay is powered by time-switching optical energy harvesting and forwards the decoded information using displaced squeezed signaling (DSS). To obtain a physically con sistent description of turbulence-induced loss for non-classical signaling, each hop is modeled as a pure-loss bosonic chan nel whose random transmissivity follows a truncated Gamma Gamma law, i.e., the Gamma-Gamma irradiance conditioned on the physically admissible range of a transmittance. Under this channel, coherent states remain pure, whereas squeezed states are mapped to mixed Gaussian states. Under Helstrom-optimal detection, the average error of the coherent hop is derived in exact Laplace-series form. For the DSS hop, we derive the output states, a closed-form Gaussian fidelity with rigorous two sided bounds on the Helstrom error, and prove the existence of a loss-aware optimal photon partition. Furthermore, we prove that optimized squeezing preserves both the turbulence-induced diversity order and the leading asymptotic constant of coherent relaying, so that its benefit is a finite-photon-budget effect, and that an interior throughput-optimal harvesting fraction exists. A covariance-preserving benchmark with an exact series representation yields an analytical upper bound on the achievable throughput whose absolute gap vanishes as the relay photon budget grows. Numerical results based on the exact mixed-state Helstrom error quantify the benefit of squeezing and the regime in which it is useful.

papers.title: Spin Space Symmetry Without Spin Space Groups
papers.abstract: Spin space groups provide a complete symmetry classification of magnetic structures in the non-relativistic limit. Each spin space group with a given parent space group is specified, up to spin-only symmetries, by a real representation of that space group acting in spin space. We argue that working directly with this representation not only avoids the construction and identification of the group, but also organizes and simplifies the resulting symmetry constraints on allowed responses. The presence or absence of magnetic compensation, piezomagnetism, spin and charge transport, the Edelstein effect, and momentum-space spin textures becomes an ordinary problem in the representation theory of space groups. The conditions reduce to overlaps between the three exterior powers of the defining representation and multipole representations of the point group. Several physically distinct responses then reduce to the same condition: a $p$-wave spin texture and the time-even Edelstein effect are allowed together, as are piezomagnetism and a $d$-wave spin texture in compensated order. The wave-vector content of the exterior powers gives a hierarchy of selection rules: depending on the power, a uniform response requires one, two, or three ordering wave vectors to sum to a reciprocal lattice vector. A non-relativistic anomalous Hall effect in compensated order at zero wave vector requires a defining representation built from three one-dimensional irreducible representations, a purely odd-parity spin texture requires a pair of nonzero ordering wave vectors that cancel, and coplanar order at nonzero wave vector in the interior of the Brillouin zone is always a $p$-wave magnet. We illustrate the approach with collinear, coplanar and non-coplanar magnets, and discuss extensions to magnetic space groups, connections to Landau theories of collinear order, and the characterization of odd-parity magnets.

papers.title: Semiclassical dynamics of higher-order squeezing: self-adjoint extensions and coherent returns
papers.abstract: Higher-order squeezing Hamiltonians have several self-adjoint realizations, while their classical trajectories reach infinity in finite time. We relate these extension problems through boundary amplitudes and the semiclassical propagation of coherent states. A discrete Fourier transformation gives the sink-to-source ray matrix of each quantum realization. After the first passage through infinity, the full Husimi probability measure converges to point masses on outgoing classical branches, with weights equal to the squared moduli of the matrix entries. The proof combines finite-order approximate tail solutions satisfying the exact extension boundary condition with full-norm Gaussian matching and a square-summable residual estimate. For positive energy, we determine the limit after any fixed number of passages: amplitudes evolve by powers of the unitary ray matrix, not by iterations of its squared-modulus matrix. We also realize these limits by concentrated complex amplitudes for an energy-preserving Liouville extension, distinguishing deterministic classical gluings from coherent boundary mixing.

papers.title: ReDence: A Hybrid Agentic and System One Model Framework for Rapid, Evidence-Grounded Detection of Social Engineering Scams
papers.abstract: Detecting online social engineering (SE) scams often requires examining website workflows, verifying claims against external sources, and connecting evidence across multiple pages. Existing detectors provide limited support for these tasks and rarely produce actionable evidence to support their decisions, leaving analysts to manually investigate flagged websites, which inevitably delays detection and subsequent takedown of these attacks. To address this gap, we present ReDence, a hybrid framework for automated, evidence-grounded scam investigation, detection, and reporting across diverse SE scam categories. ReDence combines two locally deployed, fine-tuned models: a multimodal agentic Investigator (Qwen3.5-4B) for investigative planning, evidence interpretation, and report generation, and a specialized System One model (Tev1) that handles binary and multiple-choice decisions, including browser action selection and evidence assessment, significantly reducing response generation overhead while preserving the Investigator's reasoning capabilities for complex tasks. The reports produced by ReDence also document investigative actions, collected evidence, and the reasoning behind each decision. Our evaluation shows that ReDence has a detection accuracy of over 96%, outperforming existing detectors while being at least four times faster. When deployed on a real-world URL stream over the period of 28 days, ReDence identified 4,042 new SE scam websites across 17 categories, of which at least 71% were missed by all four popular anti-scam blocklists evaluated. Feedback from twelve domain providers indicated that ReDence's investigative reports helped analysts recognize the scams documented in reported websites, understand the supporting evidence, and validate cases more efficiently. We open-source ReDence to aid automated, evidence-grounded scam investigation and reporting.

papers.title: Tracing Subliminal Learning Through Pretraining
papers.abstract: Large language models trained on data generated by other models can sometimes inherit traits unrelated to that data, a phenomenon called subliminal learning. We study this phenomenon under both hard-label distillation, where students train on numbers generated by a biased teacher, and on-policy soft-label distillation, where students generate the data and the teacher's logits provide the learning signal. Using Pythia, PolyPythia, and DataDecide OLMo models, we find that transfer persists in both settings across differences in weight initialization, pretraining data order, pretraining corpus, model size, and architecture, showing that none of these shared properties is necessary for transfer. Across pretraining checkpoints, the ability to transmit a preference and the ability to acquire one develop separately: some checkpoints are more effective teachers but weaker students, and vice versa. Consistent with this distinction, cross-model transfer can be strongly asymmetric in magnitude when teacher and student roles are reversed.
