Inspired by the BKY algorithm, we use interpolations to extend our approach to the settings of folded Reed--Solomon and multiplicity codes, resulting in fast algorithms for unique decoding against semi-adversarial errors. Our new decoders for FRS and multiplicity codes replace the sophisticated root-finding step in traditional algorithms, such as the Guruswami--Wang algorithm, with a straightforward polynomial long division. Analysis of these algorithms requires more robust monomial-tracking arguments than IRS codes.

papers.title: A Tail-Respecting Splitting Numerical Scheme for Lévy-Driven SDEs With Superlinear Drifts
papers.abstract: We present an explicit numerical approximation scheme, denoted by $\{X^n\}$, for the effective simulation of solutions $X$ to a multivariate stochastic differential equation (SDE) with a superlinearly growing $κ$-dissipative drift, where $κ>1$, driven by a multiplicative heavy-tailed Lévy process that has a finite $p$-th moment, with $p>0$. We show that the strong $L^{p_X}$-convergence $\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\mathbf E \|X^n_t-X_t\|^{p_X}=\mathcal O (h_n^γ)$ holds for any $p_X\in (0,p+κ-1)$, which is exactly the range where the $p_X$-moment of the solution is known to be finite. Additionally, for any $p_X\in (0,p)$ we establish strong uniform convergence: $\mathbf E\sup_{t\in[0,T]} \|X^n_t-X_t\|^{p_X}=\mathcal{O} ( h_n^δ )$. In both cases we determine the convergence rates $γ$ and $δ$. In the special case of SDEs driven solely by a Brownian motion, our numerical scheme preserves super-exponential moments of the solution. The scheme $\{X^n\}$ is realized as a combination of a well-known Euler method with a Lie-Trotter type splitting technique.

papers.title: The Cesàro Value Iteration
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider undiscouted infinite-horizon optimal control for deterministic systems with an uncountable state and input space. We specifically address the case when the classic value iteration does not converge. For such systems, we use the Ces`aro mean to define the infinite-horizon optimal control problem and the corresponding infinite-horizon value function. Moreover, for this value function, we introduce the Cesàro value iteration and prove its convergence for the special case of systems with periodic optimal operating behavior. For this instance, we also show that the Cesàro value function recovers the undiscounted infinite-horizon optimal cost, if the latter is well-defined.

papers.title: Exceedance and force of centrality for functional data
papers.abstract: Exceedance refers to instances where a dynamic process surpasses given thresholds, e.g., the occurrence of a heat wave. We propose a novel exceedance framework for functional data, where each observed random trajectory is transformed into an exceedance function, which quantifies exceedance durations as a function of threshold levels. An inherent relationship between exceedance functions and probability distributions makes it possible to draw on distributional data analysis techniques such as Fréchet regression to study the dependence of exceedances on Euclidean predictors, e.g., calendar year when the exceedances are observed. We use local linear estimators to obtain exceedance functions from discretely observed functional data with noise and study the convergence of the proposed estimators. New concepts of interest include the force of centrality that quantifies the propensity of a system to revert to lower levels when a given threshold has been exceeded, conditional exceedance functions given Euclidean covariates, and threshold exceedance functions, which characterize the size of exceedance sets in dependence on covariates for any fixed threshold. We establish consistent estimation with rates of convergence for these targets. The practical merits of the proposed methodology are illustrated through simulations and applications for annual temperature curves and medfly activity profiles.

papers.title: Veech groups of covers of the Chamanara surface
papers.abstract: We study finite abelian covers of the Chamanara surface, an example of a finite-area infinite translation surface with interesting dynamics and a large Veech group. Specifically, the Veech group of the Chamanara surface is a virtually free group on two generators. We characterize when finite abelian covers have large Veech groups themselves, namely when their Veech group has finite index in that of the Chamanara surface. For degree-2 covers, we provide a detailed analysis of these finite-index Veech groups. As an application, we prove that every free group arises as the projective Veech group of a finite-area infinite translation surface.

papers.title: tempdisagg: A Python Framework for Temporal Disaggregation of Time Series Data
papers.abstract: tempdisagg is an open-source Python package that estimates a high-frequency time series from low-frequency benchmarks and, optionally, high-frequency indicators, such that the estimates aggregate exactly to the benchmarks. It implements the regression-based estimators of Chow-Lin, Fernández and Litterman, the dynamic Chow-Lin model, the Denton and Denton-Cholette benchmarking procedures and uniform distribution, with the formulas and defaults of the R package tempdisagg, together with the autoregressive distributed-lag model of Proietti as an experimental extension. All generalised least squares estimators share one engine in which the residual covariance is applied through its triangular factor, so that one likelihood evaluation costs $O(n\,n_l^2)$ instead of $O(n^2 n_l)$. The package reports complete inference (coefficients, standard errors, likelihood-based criteria, prediction variances and a full profile of the autoregressive parameter with identification diagnostics), accepts additional exact linear constraints, multiple indicators and aggregation weights, and provides exact non-negative and cross-sectional reconciliation, rolling-origin backtesting, revision analysis, conformity diagnostics and a common-factor test. Agreement with R is enforced by an automated test suite over 29 reference cases: with a fixed autoregressive parameter predictions and statistics agree to relative differences between $10^{-15}$ and $10^{-7}$, and with an estimated parameter they agree to about $10^{-8}$ once the difference in optimiser tolerance is removed. Experiments with series whose high-frequency values are known illustrate how the reported tools support the choice of method.

papers.title: Persistent Stiefel-Whitney Classes of Tangent Bundles
papers.abstract: Stiefel--Whitney classes are invariants of the tangent bundle of a smooth manifold, represented as cohomology classes of the base manifold. These classes are essential in obstruction theory, embedding problems, and cobordism theory. In this work, we propose a concrete algorithm to compute persistent cohomology classes representing these characteristic classes. Given a point cloud, we construct a Čech or alpha filtration and apply the Wu formula using the cup product and Steenrod squares. The algorithm runs in polynomial time in the number of simplices without estimating tangent spaces or constructing a classifying map. Under suitable hypotheses on the filtration, the resulting classes represent those of a closed smooth manifold even when the filtration contains additional wedge summands on whose reduced cohomology all positive Steenrod squares vanish. For sufficiently large samples drawn independently and uniformly from the manifold, recovery holds with high probability over an interval of scales. We present experiments on triangulated four-manifolds and on point clouds from image patches and a molecular conformation space.

papers.title: Further Generalization of Ramanujan Sums with Regular A-Functions
papers.abstract: In the study of Ramanujan sums, the so-called regular $A$-function is a set-valued multiplicative function that tracks certain subsets of the divisor sets of natural numbers. McCarthy provided a generalization of the Ramanujan sum using these regular $A$-function based arithmetic convolutions. This approach has recently attracted considerable interest from several researchers. In this paper, we extend McCarthy's generalization by introducing two regular $A$-functions corresponding to both parameters in the Ramanujan sum. Our generalization exhibits several properties of the Ramanujan sums. Using the regular $A$-function, We also generalize the greatest common divisor (GCD) function and the Von Sterneck formula. Our introduction of two regular $A$-functions into these expressions enables us to explore a novel perspective on the connection between these expressions and the order relation between the two regular $A$-functions. In particular, we establish the necessary and sufficient conditions for orthogonality and Dedekind-Hölder's identity (i.e., Ramanujan sum = Von Sterneck function) to hold. Our primary motivation for the proposed generalization is Ramanujan expansions of arithmetic functions based on arbitrary regular $A$-functions. These expansions of arbitrary $A$-functions discussed here are new in the literature.

papers.title: Can Explanations Improve Recommendations? Evidence from Prediction-Informed Explanations
papers.abstract: Recommender systems are central to digital platforms, yet they face a fundamental trade-off between accuracy and explainability: Black-box models achieve strong performance but lack interpretability needed for trust and adoption, while existing explainable AI approaches often generate explanations post hoc or sacrifice accuracy. We challenge this view, proposing that explanations, when designed as an integral component of the system and aligned with predictions, can improve \emph{both} interpretability and accuracy. We introduce RecPIE (Recommendation with Prediction-Informed Explanations), a framework that jointly optimizes recommendation predictions and natural-language explanations. RecPIE embeds explanation generation into the learning loop: predictions guide explanation generation (prediction-informed explanations), which are fed back to refine subsequent predictions (explanation-informed predictions) via alternating training. The LLM is fine-tuned using LoRA and reinforcement learning with a usefulness reward derived from recommendation accuracy. We evaluate RecPIE on large-scale point-of-interest recommendation data from Google Maps, where consumer preferences span diverse place categories. RecPIE improves predictive accuracy by 1.7-3.6\% over state-of-the-art baselines and outperforms the strongest full-data baselines using only 25\% of the training data. In human evaluations with 566 participants, RecPIE explanations are preferred 61.5% of the time (versus 16.6% for the best baseline) and rated closer to human-generated explanations. Together, these results suggest that insights about consumer behavior and AI decisions need not be imposed externally or generated post hoc; they can be learned as an integral component \emph{within} the AI systems, allowing systems themselves to discover which insights are useful for improving predictive performance.

papers.title: Inference in dynamic models for panel data using the moving block bootstrap
papers.abstract: Inference in linear panel data models is complicated by the presence of fixed effects when (some of) the regressors are not strictly exogenous. Under asymptotics where the number of cross-sectional observations and time periods grow at the same rate, the within-group estimator is consistent but its limit distribution features a bias term. In this paper we show that a panel version of the moving block bootstrap, where blocks of adjacent cross-sections are resampled with replacement, replicates the limit distribution of the within-group estimator. Confidence ellipsoids and hypothesis tests based on the reverse-percentile bootstrap are thus asymptotically valid without the need to take the presence of bias into account.

papers.title: CP-Guard+: A New Paradigm for Malicious Agent Detection and Defense in Collaborative Perception
papers.abstract: Collaborative perception (CP) is a promising method for safe connected and autonomous driving, which enables multiple vehicles to share sensing information to enhance perception performance. However, compared with single-vehicle perception, the openness of a CP system makes it more vulnerable to malicious attacks that can inject malicious information to mislead the perception of an ego vehicle, resulting in severe risks for safe driving. To mitigate such vulnerability, we first propose a new paradigm for malicious agent detection that effectively identifies malicious agents at the feature level without requiring verification of final perception results, significantly reducing computational overhead. Building on this paradigm, we introduce CP-GuardBench, the first comprehensive dataset provided to train and evaluate various malicious agent detection methods for CP systems. Furthermore, we develop a robust defense method called CP-Guard+, which enhances the margin between the representations of benign and malicious features through a carefully designed Dual-Centered Contrastive Loss (DCCLoss). Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on both CP-GuardBench and V2X-Sim, and demonstrate the superiority of CP-Guard+.

papers.title: Settling the no-$(k+1)$-in-line problem when $k$ is not small
papers.abstract: What is the maximum number of points that can be selected from an $n\times n$ square lattice so that no $k+1$ of them are collinear? This was asked more than $100$ years ago for $k=2$ and it remained wide open ever since. In this paper, we prove the exact answer is $kn$, provided that $ n\ge k\ge C\log n$ for an absolute constant $C<20$. The proof relies on carefully constructed block-uniform random bipartite graphs and concentration inequalities.

papers.title: Jordan-Hölder property for shifted quantum affine algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that finite length representations of shifted quantum affine algebras in category $\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ are stable by fusion product. This implies that in the topological Grothendieck ring $K_0(\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}})$ the Grothendieck group of finite length representations forms a non-topological subring. We also conjecture this subring is isomorphic to the cluster algebra discovered in arXiv:2401.04616. In the course of our proofs, we establish that any simple representation in category $\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ descends to a truncation, for certain truncation parameters as conjectured in arXiv:2010.06996 in terms of Langlands dual $q$-characters.

papers.title: OMINI: Towards Consistent 3D Object Manipulation via Generative Texturing and Adaptive Lighting
papers.abstract: Enabling object manipulation based on a single static image, from geometric editing to animation, remains a significant challenge. Existing methods often struggle to jointly support these tasks, while also suffering from fidelity degradation in object appearance and scene illumination. In this work, we introduce OMINI, a unified framework that addresses these challenges through two complementary strategies. First, OMINI lifts the 2D object into a 3D representation and adopts a Refine-before-Render design. Both geometric editing and animation are then performed by manipulating and rendering the refined 3D asset, maintaining appearance consistency throughout the manipulation process. Second, we propose two dedicated modules for fidelity enhancement: TextuRefiner refines rendered views of the 3D asset under appearance and geometric guidance, thereby generating fine-grained texture details; IllumiCorrector corrects environmental illumination using HSL-based color correction and VLM-guided intensity optimization, enabling visually plausible renderings with shadows. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OMINI outperforms existing methods, producing visually consistent results. The GPU stages of OMINI are run on a single NVIDIA RTX 3090.

papers.title: Itô formula for planarly branched rough paths
papers.abstract: The Itô formula is a cornerstone of stochastic calculus, providing a fundamental change-of-variables formula for stochastic processes. In rough path theory, Itô formulas have been proved for rough paths with roughness $\frac{1}{3}< α\leq \frac{1}{2}$ and branched rough paths with roughness $0< α\leq 1$. Planarly branched rough paths provide a natural framework for studying rough differential equations on homogeneous spaces, extending the theory of branched rough paths through the Munthe-Kaas-Wright Hopf algebra. In the present paper, we prove the Itô formula for planarly branched rough paths with roughness $\frac{1}{4}< α\leq \frac{1}{2}$.

papers.title: On finiteness of fiber space structures of klt Calabi-Yau pairs in dimension 3
papers.abstract: We prove that for a fixed klt Calabi-Yau pair $(X,Δ)$ of dimension $3$, the set of fiber space structures of $X$ is finite up to $Aut(X,Δ)$.

papers.title: First-Passage Time Fluctuation Theorem and Thermodynamic Bound in Cooperative Biomolecular Networks
papers.abstract: Using a pathway analysis technique, a dynamic fluctuation relation is derived for a kinetically cooperative biomolecular machine (e.g., an enzyme or a motor protein). This new relation indicates that, in the absence of hidden current, a fluctuation theorem can be established for the first-passage time of the observable process, and we show that this dramatic reduction is a general feature applicable to a wide variety of cooperative networks. This first-passage time fluctuation theorem can be experimentally tested, with its violation serving as a signature of hidden detailed balance breaking. Importantly, we obtain a compact exact expression for the integrated correction to this fluctuation theorem, as well as the general single-loop form, revealing a thermodynamic bound on the kinetic branching ratio (a measure of directionality defined as the forward-to-backward observable process probability ratio). These results provide detailed insight into the rich connections between dynamic measurements and the underlying nonequilibrium thermodynamics for cooperative biomolecular machines.

papers.title: Refined Strichartz Estimates for sub-Laplacians in Heisenberg and $H$-type groups
papers.abstract: We obtain refined Strichartz estimates for the sub-Riemannian Schrödinger equation on $H$-type Carnot groups using Fourier restriction techniques. In particular, we extend the previously known Strichartz estimates previously obtained for the Heisenberg group also to non radial initial data. The same arguments permits to obtain refined Strichartz estimates for the wave equation on $H$-type groups. Our proof is based on estimates for the spectral projectors for sub-Laplacians and reinterprets Strichartz estimates as Fourier restriction theorems for nilpotent groups in the context of trace-class operator valued measures.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Quantum Error Correction: A Comprehensive Review
papers.abstract: Quantum Error Correction (QEC) is the process of detecting and correcting errors in quantum systems, which are prone to decoherence and quantum noise. QEC is crucial for developing stable and highly accurate quantum computing systems, therefore, several research efforts have been made to develop the best QEC strategy. Recently, Google's breakthrough shows great potential to improve the accuracy of the existing error correction methods. This survey provides a comprehensive review of advancements in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to enhance QEC schemes for existing Noisy Intermediate Scale Quantum (NISQ) systems. Specifically, we focus on machine learning (ML) strategies and span from unsupervised, supervised, semi-supervised, to reinforcement learning methods. It is clear from the evidence, that these methods have recently shown superior efficiency and accuracy in the QEC pipeline compared to conventional approaches. Our review covers more than 150 relevant studies, offering a comprehensive overview of progress and perspective in this field. We organized the reviewed literature on the basis of the AI strategies employed and improvements in error correction performance. We also discuss challenges ahead such as data sparsity caused by limited quantum error datasets and scalability issues as the number of quantum bits (qubits) in quantum systems kept increasing very fast. We conclude the paper with summary of existing works and future research directions aimed at deeper integration of AI techniques into QEC strategies.

papers.title: dapper: Data Augmentation for Private Posterior Estimation in R
papers.abstract: This paper serves as a reference and introduction to using the R package dapper. dapper encodes a sampling framework which allows exact Markov chain Monte Carlo simulation of parameters and latent variables in a statistical model given privatized data. The goal of this package is to fill an urgent need by providing applied researchers with a flexible tool to perform valid Bayesian inference on data protected by differential privacy, allowing them to properly account for the noise introduced for privacy protection in their statistical analysis. dapper offers a significant step forward in providing general-purpose statistical inference tools for privatized data.

papers.title: A hypergeometric transformation formula of Ramanujan, its validity range and implications
papers.abstract: We extend the validity range of a hypergeometric transformation formula of Ramanujan proved by Berndt, Bhargava and Garvan [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 347, 4163 (1995)] and study its implications. Relations to special values of complete elliptic integrals of the first kind in singular value theory are established. Consequently, we derive several closed-form evaluations of hypergeometric functions $_2F_1$ with different sets of parameters and arguments. Connections with other hypergeometric transformations and some recent results are discussed.

papers.title: Kerr-Induced Impairments in Quantum-Classical Fiber Coexistence: A Quantum-Stochastic Analysis
papers.abstract: Quantum and classical optical signals sharing a fiber can interact through Kerr cross-phase modulation without interchannel photon transfer, potentially degrading phase- and mode-sensitive quantum communication even when direct spectral leakage is negligible. We develop a two-channel quantum-stochastic propagation framework based on the positive-P representation for a weak coherent pulse train co-propagating with a strong, quadrature-amplitude-modulated classical signal. Both fields are treated quantum mechanically, incorporating self- and cross-phase modulation, chromatic dispersion, group-velocity mismatch, attenuation, and Kerr-induced quantum diffusion. We characterize the classical-channel influence using three complementary observables: the frequency-resolved quadrature-fluctuation spectrum, complex temporal-mode overlap, and adjacent-pulse interference visibility. Simulations of a 100-km standard-fiber link reveal markedly different responses across these observables. As classical launch power increases, the extremal quadrature-fluctuation spectra remain close to the shot-noise level, whereas the temporal-mode and visibility penalties reach approximately 4.5% and 6.0%, respectively, at 100 mW. Applying a 1% mean-penalty criterion gives launch-power thresholds of approximately 46 mW for temporal-mode overlap and 40 mW for visibility, yielding a joint Kerr-limited threshold near 40 mW for the investigated configuration. These results demonstrate that temporal-mode deformation and reduced pulse-to-pulse coherence can occur while the evaluated quadrature-fluctuation spectra remain near shot noise, establishing a complementary criterion for selecting classical launch power in quantum-classical fiber co-propagation.

papers.title: A polyptych of multi-centered deformation spaces
papers.abstract: Extending Verdier's deformation space to the normal cone of a closed subscheme and Rost's double deformation space of a pair of nested closed subschemes, we introduce a notion of deformation spaces attached to chains of immersions of arbitrary lengths $n$. One main result, which builds on the formalism of multi-centered dilatations of schemes, is the existence of so-called panelization isomorphisms, which produce under suitable regularity conditions several canonical isomorphisms between a given deformation space of length $n$ and some deformation spaces of smaller lengths. Having these panelization isomorphisms also allows to give geometric descriptions of the strata -- certain restrictions of special interest -- of deformation spaces.

papers.title: Almost Sure Convergence Rates and Concentration of Stochastic Approximation and Reinforcement Learning with Markovian Noise
papers.abstract: This paper establishes, to our knowledge, the first almost sure convergence rate and the first maximal concentration bound with sub-Weibull tails for general contractive stochastic approximation algorithms with Markovian noise. As a corollary, we also obtain convergence rates in $L^p$. Key to our successes is a novel discretization of the mean ODE of stochastic approximation algorithms using intervals with diminishing (instead of constant) length. Applications yield the first almost sure convergence rate for $Q$-learning without count-based learning rates and the first maximal concentration bound for off-policy temporal difference learning, both with Markovian samples.

papers.title: The one-shot problem: Solution to an open question of finite-fuel singular control with discretionary stopping
papers.abstract: We resolve a long-standing open question posed by Karatzas, Ocone, Wang, and Zervos (Stochastics, 2000) on finite-fuel singular stochastic control with discretionary stopping. Our approach introduces a novel "one-shot" solution technique, based on reduction to an auxiliary optimal stopping problem. We prove that, despite the convexity of the objective function, the waiting region of the optimal strategy need not be connected. Furthermore, we identify a qualitative transition in the optimal policy: even with arbitrarily small positive fuel, the solution can differ from the zero-fuel (pure optimal stopping) limit. These results reveal a fundamental non-robustness in such control problems, showing that zero-fuel models need not approximate behaviour under small but positive fuel constraints.

papers.title: FlexTSF: A Flexible Forecasting Model for Time Series with Variable Regularities
papers.abstract: Generalizing across time series with irregular temporal structures poses a persistent challenge for universal time series forecasting models. Existing approaches often assume regular sampling or depend heavily on imputation, which limits their applicability in real-world scenarios where irregularities are prevalent due to diverse sensing devices and recording practices. To address this gap, we propose FlexTSF, a flexible and domain-adaptive forecasting model specifically designed for time series with variable temporal regularities. At its foundation lies the IVP Patcher, a continuous-time patching module leveraging Initial Value Problems (IVPs) to inherently handle uneven sampling intervals, variable sequence lengths, and missing values. Built upon a decoder-only Transformer architecture, FlexTSF integrates normalized timestamp inputs and domain-specific statistical descriptors through a specialized causal self-attention mechanism, enabling adaptability across domains. Extensive experiments on 16 datasets demonstrate FlexTSF's effectiveness, significantly outperforming existing models in classic forecasting scenarios, zero-shot generalization, and low-resource fine-tuning conditions.

papers.title: Regularity of the Semigroup of Regular Probability Measures on Locally Compact Hausdorff Topological Groups in which every element is of finite order
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group in which every element is of finite order, and let $P(\mathcal{G})$ denote the class of all regular probability measures on $\mathcal{G}$. In this note, it is observed that a characterization of algebraically regular elements in certain subsemigroups of $P(\mathcal{G})$ (Theorem~4.1 \cite{MNN}) for compact $\mathcal{G}$ remains true for locally compact $\mathcal{G}$. The results presented rely very much on Wendel's support theorem and the theory of doubly stochastic matrices (\cite{PLC} \cite{WEN}). A more general situation in which the assumption that every element is of finite order is not satisfied is also considered and illustrated with an example. This short article is a followup of \cite{MNN}.In addition,the random walk on an infinite discrete group associated with the generalised inverse of a probability measure is also studied.The last section is devoted to Fourier transform techniques to study the same problem using Bochner-type theorem in harmonic analysis.

papers.title: Fast Mixed-Precision Real Evaluation
papers.abstract: Evaluating real numbers to high precision is important in computational science, numerical computing, and in hardware and software design. Efficient algorithms exist for computing arithmetic operations and common elementary functions, but composing these primitives into larger expressions remains a challenge. The typical expression-evaluation algorithm computes all primitives in the expression to a uniform precision, doubling that precision until a sufficiently-accurate result is achieved. This is wasteful: usually only a few operations really need to be performed at high precision, and the bulk of the expression could be computed at a much lower, faster precision. However, no rigorous algorithm currently exists to compute these non-uniform precision assignments, nor to leverage non-uniform precision to reduce the number of primitive computations needed to evaluate an expression. We propose a new algorithm for deriving such rigorous precision assignments and reducing the number of primitive computations needed. This algorithm can leverage results computed at lower precisions to analytically determine a precision for each primitive that will result in a sufficiently-accurate evaluation. It can also use information from constant subexpressions, movability flags, and repeat flags to skip the computation of certain primitives, further reducing the time to evaluate real expressions. Our implementation, Reval, achieves an average speed-up of 3.97x compared to the widely-used Sollya tool, with the speed-up increasing to 9.26x on the most difficult inputs. A detailed evaluation shows that this speed-up results from both assigning lower precisions to the majority of primitives and from computing fewer primitives overall.

papers.title: Product Returns and the Value of Search Prominence
papers.abstract: Ordered-search models typically make prominence valuable because the first-listed seller receives more traffic. We show that product returns can overturn this logic by changing not only the volume but also the composition of demand. We develop a duopoly model in which consumers inspect products sequentially, learn a coarse match signal through search, discover realized taste only after purchase, and may return the product. With positive consumer hassle costs for product returns and a general taste distribution, optimal consumer behavior is characterized by pre-search inspection, post-search purchase, and retention cutoffs. In a low-hassle, full-refund benchmark with uniformly distributed taste values, the non-prominent firm charges a higher price because consumers who reach it are screened by their experience with the prominent product. Although prominence generates more visits and gross orders, it also exposes the first seller to less-screened, more return-prone demand. When seller-side return losses are sufficiently large, the prominent firm can earn less than its rival while both firms earn positive profits. The reversal also persists on local active pricing branches under small positive hassle costs, small departures from full refunds, and finite oligopoly. Sellers' willingness to pay for prominence therefore depends on how a higher ranking changes both the profits from retained sales and the losses on returned units.

papers.title: Generic local identifiability for ODE inverse problems from discrete observations
papers.abstract: We study local parameter identification from finitely many measurements of an analytic output along a single ODE trajectory. At a fixed initial state and parameter, the time derivatives of the output sensitivity define a decreasing sequence of parameter kernels. If the sequence reaches zero, any prescribed pattern of distinct positive sampling times gives full parameter rank after a sufficiently small common rescaling, provided the number of times is at least the number of strict kernel drops. The orders of these drops determine the asymptotic orders of all singular values of the sampled Jacobian. We also give a sharp worst-case bound on the number of freely chosen observation times needed for the sampled Jacobian to have full column rank. At a generic point, the maximum parameter rank determines how many local parameter coordinates can vary without changing the observations. A quantitative inverse estimate bounds the error of every estimate in the certified neighborhood that fits the data at least as well as the true parameter. For a \(d\)-dimensional homogeneous linear system with known initial state and \(d\) equally spaced positive-time full-state observations, cyclicity for the sampled propagator is equivalent to local identifiability of the generator. In this case, one additional exact full-state sample at a time incommensurate with the grid spacing gives global recovery.

papers.title: Ensemble Logic
papers.abstract: Ensemble Logic (EL) is a family of modal logics whose modal parameters are terms with quantified variables. We interpret formulas over metric monoids, that is, commutative monoids equipped with translation-invariant metrics. Displacement evaluates a formula at a translated point, while bounded existence and bounded universality evaluate it at some or every point of a window of prescribed length. Quantification over points and lengths allows the same variable to occur in the parameters of several operators. This provides a common framework for temporal and spatial reasoning in discrete, dense and multi-dimensional settings. Our main result establishes a sharp undecidability boundary for satisfiability over the natural numbers: satisfiability is undecidable already for formulas $\exists N\,\exists n\,Ψ$ in which $Ψ$ is built from the letters of a fixed alphabet by conjunction, disjunction, displacement and bounded universality. We prove this by a reduction from Post's Correspondence Problem. We also present results, in part from companion work, that place this theorem in the general theory of EL. These include an atomic-displacement normal form for covariant windows and composition laws for discrete and dense time. The discrete logic admits an embedding of linear temporal logic, defines the accepting runs of every Büchi automaton, and has a sound equational calculus. For the rational logic, we show that every fixed formula can be evaluated in polynomial time on interval models in which atomic propositions are interpreted by finite unions of intervals. Finally, we represent timed words over positions and real time and compare two window geometries; with rectangular windows, two shared lengths yield undecidability on finite timed words.

papers.title: A Unified Plug-and-Play Algorithm with Projected Landweber Operator for Split Convex Feasibility Problems
papers.abstract: In recent years Plug-and-Play (PnP) methods have achieved state-of-the-art performance in inverse imaging problems by replacing proximal operators with denoisers. Based on the proximal gradient method, some theoretical results of PnP have appeared, where appropriate step size is crucial for convergence analysis. However, in practical applications, applying PnP methods with theoretically guaranteed step sizes is difficult, and these algorithms are limited to Gaussian noise. In this paper,from a perspective of split convex feasibility problems (SCFP), an adaptive PnP algorithm with Projected Landweber Operator (PnP-PLO) is proposed to address these issues. Numerical experiments on image deblurring, super-resolution, and compressed sensing MRI experiments illustrate that PnP-PLO with theoretical guarantees outperforms state-of-the-art methods such as RED and RED-PRO.

papers.title: Incomplete-market CAPM equilibria in continuous time
papers.abstract: We study continuous-time CAPM equilibria with general mean-variance preferences of the form $U(μ,σ)$, where $U$ is strictly quasiconcave, increasing in the mean $μ$ and decreasing in the volatility $σ$ of terminal wealth. Our framework accommodates both financial and productive assets with nontradeable endowments. We allow for equilibria driven by general semimartingales in the case of linear mean-variance preferences and by continuous semimartingales in the case of general mean-variance preferences. The key insight is a connection between mean-variance efficiency and quadratic utility maximisation. We first characterise quadratic equilibria through an explicit family of equilibrium price processes indexed by the aggregate risk tolerance. We then show that each agent's optimal mean-variance strategy corresponds to a quadratic optimum with an endogenously determined risk tolerance. This correspondence reduces the mean-variance equilibrium problem to a one-dimensional fixed-point problem, whose solvability we establish using fine properties of (dynamic) mean-variance hedging and a novel stability result for quadratic BSDEs with BMO growth at the origin. Finally, examples illustrate how unspanned stochastic-volatility risk interacts with aggregate endowments to affect equilibrium asset prices, and how nonlinear mean-variance preferences influence equilibrium risk tolerance and asset-price comparative statics.

papers.title: Genomic Bottleneck, Neural Scaling, and the Emergence of Intelligence: A Theoretical Perspective on Biological and Artificial Neural Systems
papers.abstract: We study the biological evolution of low-latency natural neural networks for short-term survival, and its parallels in the development of low latency high-performance Central Processing Unit in computer design and architecture. The necessity of accurate high-quality display of motion picture led to the special processing units known as the GPU, just as how special visual cortex regions of animals produced such low-latency computational capacity. The human brain, especially considered as nothing but a scaled-up version of a primate brain evolved in response to genomic bottleneck, producing a brain that is trainable and prunable by society, and as a further extension, invents language, writing and storage of narratives displaced in time and space. We conclude that this modern digital invention of social media and the archived collective common corpus has further evolved from just simple CPU-based low-latency fast retrieval to high-throughput parallel processing of data using GPUs to train Attention based Deep Learning Neural Networks producing Generative AI with aspects like toxicity, bias, memorization, hallucination, with intriguing close parallels in humans and their society. We show how this paves the way for constructive approaches to eliminating such drawbacks from human society and its proxy and collective large-scale mirror, the Generative AI of the LLMs.

papers.title: An analogue of Reed's conjecture for digraphs
papers.abstract: Reed in 1998 conjectured that every graph $G$ satisfies $χ(G) \leq \lceil \frac{Δ(G)+1+ω(G)}{2} \rceil$. As a partial result, he proved the existence of $\varepsilon > 0$ for which every graph $G$ satisfies $χ(G) \leq \lceil (1-\varepsilon)(Δ(G)+1)+\varepsilonω(G) \rceil$. We propose an analogue conjecture for digraphs. Given a digraph $D$, we denote by $\vecχ(D)$ the dichromatic number of $D$, which is the minimum number of colours needed to partition $D$ into acyclic induced subdigraphs. We let $\overleftrightarrowω(D)$ denote the size of the largest biclique (a set of vertices inducing a complete digraph) of $D$ and $\tildeΔ(D) = \max_{v\in V(D)} \sqrt{d^+(v) \cdot d^-(v)}$. We conjecture that every digraph $D$ satisfies $\vecχ(D) \leq \lceil \frac{\tildeΔ(D)+1+\overleftrightarrowω(D)}{2} \rceil$, which if true implies Reed's conjecture. As a partial result, we prove the existence of $\varepsilon >0$ for which every digraph $D$ satisfies $\vecχ(D) \leq \lceil (1-\varepsilon)(\tildeΔ(D)+1)+\varepsilon\overleftrightarrowω(D) \rceil$. This implies both Reed's result and an independent result of Harutyunyan and Mohar for oriented graphs. To obtain this upper bound on $\vecχ$, we prove that every digraph $D$ with $\overleftrightarrowω(D) > \frac{2}{3}(Δ_{\max}(D)+1)$, where $Δ_{\max}(D) = \max_{v\in V(D)} \max(d^+(v),d^-(v))$, admits an acyclic set of vertices intersecting each biclique of $D$, which generalises a result of King. We finally give a short proof that every oriented graph $D$ with underlying graph $G$ satisfies $\vecχ(D) \leq \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \tildeΔ(D) + 2$ and $\vecχ(D) \leq \frac{1}{3}Δ(G)+2$, improving on results of Golowich and Steiner, respectively.

papers.title: Strange metal at the Lifshitz transition
papers.abstract: Strange metal behavior is widely observed in cuprates, ruthenates, and twisted bilayer graphene. We study quantum critical transport at a two-dimensional Lifshitz transition, where the Fermi surface hosts a van Hove singularity and changes from convex to concave. Self-consistently solving the fermion-boson coupled system, we demonstrate a linear-in-$1/ω$ optical conductivity driven by the interplay between impurity and critical scattering. The resistivity exhibits a persistent linear-in-$T$ in the quantum critical regime down to $T\rightarrow 0$. Spatially fluctuating Yukawa interaction further extends the linear-in-$T$ regime, providing a unified mechanism for strange metallic transport at the Lifshitz transition.

papers.title: Finite-difference least square methods for solving Hamilton-Jacobi equations using neural networks
papers.abstract: We present a simple algorithm to approximate the viscosity solution of Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) equations by means of an artificial deep neural network. The algorithm uses a stochastic gradient descent-based method to minimize the least square principle defined by a monotone, consistent numerical scheme. We analyze the least square principle's critical points and derive conditions that guarantee that any critical point approximates the sought viscosity solution. The use of a deep artificial neural network on a finite difference scheme lifts the restriction of conventional finite difference methods that rely on computing functions on a fixed grid. This feature makes it possible to solve HJ equations posed in higher dimensions where conventional methods are infeasible. We demonstrate the efficacy of our algorithm through numerical studies on various canonical HJ equations across different dimensions, showcasing its potential and versatility.

papers.title: On the cone conjecture for pairs of large Kodaira dimension
papers.abstract: In this paper, by running the minimal model program and considering the anti-canonical fibration, we prove the Morrison-Kawamata cone conjecture for klt Calabi-Yau pairs $(X,Δ)$ such that the Iitaka dimension $κ(X,-K_X)$ is at least $\dim X - 2$.

papers.title: Designing Algorithmic Recommendations to Achieve Human-AI Complementarity
papers.abstract: Algorithms frequently assist, rather than replace, human decision-makers. However, the design and analysis of algorithms often focus on predicting outcomes and do not explicitly model their effect on human decisions. This discrepancy between the design and role of algorithmic assistants becomes particularly concerning in light of empirical evidence that suggests that algorithmic assistants again and again fail to improve human decisions. In this article, we formalize the design of recommendation algorithms that assist human decision-makers without making restrictive ex-ante assumptions about how recommendations affect decisions. We formulate an algorithmic-design problem that leverages the potential-outcomes framework from causal inference to model the effect of recommendations on a human decision-maker's binary treatment choice. Within this model, we make a connection between algorithmic recommendations and instrumental variables. Leveraging this connection, we introduce a monotonicity assumption that leads to an intuitive classification of human responses to the algorithm. Under this assumption, we can express the human's response to algorithmic recommendations in terms of their compliance with the algorithm and the active decision they would take if the algorithm sends no recommendation. We showcase the utility of our framework using an online experiment that simulates a hiring task. We argue that our approach can make sense of the relative performance of different recommendation algorithms in the experiment and can help design solutions that realize human-AI complementarity. Finally, we leverage our approach to derive maximin-optimal recommendation algorithms that can be implemented with machine learning using limited training data.

papers.title: Univalent approximation by Fourier series of step functions
papers.abstract: We prove that univalent harmonic mappings can be approximated by univalent Fourier series of step functions.

papers.title: F-signature functions of diagonal hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a diagonal hypersurface in $A_p=\mathbb{F}_p[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]$. We study the behavior of the function $ϕ_{f,p}({a}/{p^e})=p^{-ne}\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}\big(A_p/(x_1^{p^e},\dots,x_n^{p^e},f^a)\big)$ which encodes information about the F-threshold, the Hilbert-Kunz, and the F-signature functions. We prove that when $p$ goes to infinity $ϕ_{f,p}$ converges to a piecewise polynomial function $ϕ_f$ and the left and right derivatives of $ϕ_{f,p}$ converge to $ϕ'_f$. We use this fact to prove the existence of the limit F-signature and limit Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity for diagonal hypersurfaces. When $f$ is a Fermat hypersurface, we investigate the shape of the F-signature function of $f$ and provide an explicit formula for the limit F-signature and, in some cases, also for the F-signature for fixed $p$. This allows us to answer negatively to a question of Watanabe and Yoshida.

papers.title: Open-Vocabulary Scene Text Recognition via Pseudo-Image Labeling and Margin Loss
papers.abstract: Scene text recognition is an important and challenging task in computer vision. However, most prior works focus on recognizing pre-defined words, while there are various out-of-vocabulary (OOV) words in real-world applications. In this paper, we propose a novel open-vocabulary text recognition framework, Pseudo-OCR, to recognize OOV words. The key challenge in this task is the lack of OOV training data. To solve this problem, we first propose a pseudo label generation module that leverages character detection and image inpainting to produce substantial pseudo OOV training data from real-world images. Unlike previous synthetic data, our pseudo OOV data contains real characters and backgrounds to simulate real-world applications. Secondly, to reduce noises in pseudo data, we present a semantic checking mechanism to filter semantically meaningful data. Thirdly, we introduce a quality-aware margin loss to boost the training with pseudo data. Our loss includes a margin-based part to enhance the classification ability, and a quality-aware part to penalize low-quality samples in both real and pseudo data. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art on eight datasets and achieves the first rank in the ICDAR2022 challenge.

papers.title: On co-dimension 2 defect anomalies in N=4 SYM and (2,0) theory via brane probes in AdS/CFT
papers.abstract: We consider a half-BPS solution for a D3 brane probe in AdS$_5 \times S^5$ that has world-volume geometry of AdS$_3 \times S^1$. It intersects the boundary over a surface that represents a dimension 2 defect in the boundary ${\cal N}=4$ SYM theory. The effective action of the probe brane is proportional to the logarithmically divergent volume of AdS$_3$ and may thus be interpreted as computing conformal anomaly of supersymmetric $S^2$ defect. The classical action scales as $N$. We compute the 1-loop correction to it due to quantum fluctuations of the D3 brane world-volume fields and compare the result to an earlier suggested expression for the defect anomaly. With the boundary condition for the zero mode of the world-volume vector required by supersymmetry the sum over the modes gives the 1-loop coefficient $-3$ instead of the expected $-6$. We suggest that the remaining part is due to the classical response of the background to the probe. We also perform a similar analysis of a half-BPS supersymmetric M5 brane probe solution in AdS$_7 \times S^4$ with the world-volume geometry of AdS$_5 \times S^1$ that represents a dimension 4 defect in the boundary (2,0) 6d theory. Here the classical M5 brane action computes the leading order $N^2$ term in $a$-anomaly of the supersymmetric $S^4$ defect. The fluctuations form a tower of chiral multiplets and a flavour current multiplet of the 4d ${\cal N}=2$ superconformal symmetry. We perform a detailed computation of the 1-loop correction to the M5 brane effective action and discuss prescription dependence of the prediction for the contribution to the $S^4$ defect $a$-anomaly coefficient.

papers.title: An almost effective proof of the class number 1 problem for imaginary quadratic fields via Frobenius--Rabinowitsch
papers.abstract: Let $D \neq 1$ be a square-free integer, and let $K = {\mathbb Q}(\sqrt D)$ be the corresponding quadratic field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ lying over an odd rational prime that splits in $K/\mathbb Q$. We obtain a necessary and sufficient condition in terms of a binary quadratic form for $\mathcal{P}$ to be a principal ideal. Then, when $K$ is imaginary with $D\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ and $|D|>16$, we use this result to prove $K$ has class number 1 only if $D=1-4p$ where $p$, $4p-1$, and $4p+3$ are prime. Finally, combining this condition with results on the representation of integers by the sum of three squares, the theorem of Frobenius and Rabinowitsch, and a theorem of Tatuzawa we provide a proof, up to at most one possible additional field, of the well-known theorem on imaginary quadratic fields with class number 1. If Dirichlet $L$-functions have no zeros in the half-plane $\mathrm{Re}(s)>11/12$, then the possible additional field of our result does not exist.

papers.title: Charged pion production in the annihilation reactions $e^+ + e^- \to p + \bar{n} +π^-$ and $e^+ + e^- \to n + \bar{p} +π^+.$ Contribution of the nonresonant mechanism
papers.abstract: The nonresonant mechanism in the reactions $e^+\,e^-\to π^-\,p\,\bar{n}$ and $e^+\,e^-\to π^+\,n\,\bar{p}$ is investigated in frame of the one-photon exchange approximation. The description of the hadronic phase space and the invariant amplitude formalism, earlier developed for the neutral pion channel, are applied here. Some modification is required to fulfill the conservation of the hadron electromagnetic current and to account for an additional contribution due to diagram with the pion pole. The double and single distributions over the invariant variables as well the total cross section, are obtained. The results are plotted for $s=$5,\,10,\,16\, GeV$^2$. The calculations are performed for the $π^-\,p\,\bar{n}$ channel and the rules to proceed to the $π^+\,n\,\bar{p}$ channel are formulated for every distribution.

papers.title: Nisnevich equivalences of local essentially smooth open pairs
papers.abstract: In this note, we prove a Nisnevich local equivalence \begin{equation*} X/(X-Z)\simeq X^\prime/(X^\prime-Z^\prime) \end{equation*} for essentially smooth local schemes $X$ and $X^\prime$ of the same dimension over a base scheme $B$, and arbitrary isomorphic closed subschemes $Z$ and $Z^\prime$, with immediate applications in motivic homotopy theory.

papers.title: Reconciling Overt Bias and Hidden Bias in Sensitivity Analysis for Matched Observational Studies
papers.abstract: Matching is one of the most widely used causal inference designs in observational studies, but post-matching confounding bias remains a critical concern. This bias includes overt bias from inexact matching on measured confounders and hidden bias from unmeasured confounders. Researchers routinely apply the famous Rosenbaum-type sensitivity analysis after matching to assess the impact of these biases on causal conclusions. In this work, we show that this approach is often conservative and may overstate sensitivity to confounding bias because the classical solution to the Rosenbaum sensitivity model may allocate hypothetical hidden bias in ways that contradict the overt bias observed in the matched dataset. To address this problem, we propose a new approach to Rosenbaum-type sensitivity analysis by ensuring compatibility between hidden and overt biases. Our approach does not need to add any additional assumptions (beyond mild regularity conditions) to Rosenbaum-type sensitivity analysis, and can produce uniformly more informative sensitivity analysis results than the conventional Rosenbaum-type sensitivity analysis. Computationally, our approach can be solved efficiently via iterative convex programming. Extensive simulations and a real data application demonstrate substantial gains in statistical power of sensitivity analysis. Importantly, our approach can also be applied to many other sensitivity analysis frameworks.

papers.title: Freeness conditions for intermediate $C^*$-algebras of crossed products
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be a separable $C^*$-algebra, let $Γ$ be a discrete countable group, let $α: Γ\to \text{Aut}(B)$ be an action, and let $A$ be an invariant subalgebra. We find certain freeness conditions which guarantee that any intermediate $C^*$-algebra $A \rtimes_{α,r} Γ\subseteq C \subseteq B \rtimes_{α,r} Γ$ is a crossed product of an intermediate invariant subalgebra $A \subseteq C_0 \subseteq B$ by $Γ$. Those are used to generalize related results by Suzuki.

papers.title: From Innermost to Full Almost-Sure Termination of Probabilistic Term Rewriting
papers.abstract: There are many evaluation strategies for term rewrite systems, but proving termination automatically is usually easiest for innermost rewriting. Several syntactic criteria exist when innermost termination implies full termination. We adapt these criteria to the probabilistic setting, e.g., we show when it suffices to analyze almost-sure termination (AST) w.r.t. innermost rewriting to prove full AST of probabilistic term rewrite systems (PTRSs). These criteria also apply to other notions of termination like positive AST. We implemented and evaluated our new contributions in the tool AProVE.

papers.title: Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for $321$-avoiding Kazhdan-Lusztig varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity of 321-avoiding Kazhdan--Lusztig varieties can be computed combinatorially in terms of $K$-theoretic skew excited Young diagrams. We present an algorithm which gives a lower bound for this regularity and describe a setting in which this algorithm provides precise regularity computations. This algorithm specializes to compute the regularity of all two-sided mixed ladder determinantal varieties.

papers.title: Proving Almost-Sure Innermost Termination of Probabilistic Term Rewriting Using Dependency Pairs
papers.abstract: Dependency pairs are one of the most powerful techniques to analyze termination of term rewrite systems (TRSs) automatically. We adapt the dependency pair framework to the probabilistic setting in order to prove almost-sure innermost termination of probabilistic TRSs. To evaluate its power, we implemented the new framework in our tool AProVE.

papers.title: Fitting height and lengths of laws in finite solvable groups
papers.abstract: Let G be a finite solvable group, and let h(G) denote its Fitting height, namely the length of a shortest normal series in G with nilpotent factors. We show, that h(G)/5 is a lower bound for the length of any law in G. It follows, that the cardinality of G is bounded from below by an exponential function of h(G). The proof is accomplished by showing an interesting result about the behaviour of non-trivial reduced words in permutation actions of finite solvable groups.

papers.title: Properties of Concurrent Algorithms that Allow Asynchrony
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the conditions under which a concurrent system is able to guarantee convergence deterministically even without synchronization. In general, an algorithm is deemed asynchrony-tolerant iff the global states form a DAG even if the nodes can execute based on outdated/stale values from each other. In this paper, we show that the induction of a partial order (PO) among the local states visited by individual nodes is necessary and sufficient to allow asynchrony. There are certain problems for which the predicate that defines the problem, itself, induces a partial order among the local states (called \textit{PO-inducing problems}). On the other hand, \textit{non-PO-inducing problems} is another class of problems in which a predicate defining the problem cannot induce a partial order among local states. We introduce these classes of problems. We study example PO-inducing and non-PO-inducing problems, and provide example PO-inducing (in other words, asynchrony-tolerant) algorithms (algorithms under which any node traverses a partial order of local states) for all these problems.

papers.title: Notes on modules of finite injective dimension
papers.abstract: Motivated by Bass' conjecture, we study finitely generated modules of finite injective dimension and the additional constraints they impose on the ambient ring. Beyond ensuring the Cohen--Macaulay property, the presence of such modules enforces further conditions on the ring, including reducedness, normality, being an integral domain, and various singularity conditions such as complete intersection, Gorenstein, and beyond. This continues to detect non-singularity as well. We also address the reflexivity (and also torsionlessness) of modules with finite injective dimension and show that this forces the ring to be quasi-normal. In the same vein, we investigate the injective dimension of tensor products and endomorphism rings. Finally, we study the behavior of R when high syzygies of ksurject onto a non-zero R-module of finite injective dimension.

papers.title: Security of Deep Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving: A Survey
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables agents to learn optimal behaviors through interaction with their environment and has been increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications, including autonomous driving. Despite its promise, RL is susceptible to attacks designed either to compromise policy learning or to induce erroneous decisions by trained agents. Although the literature on RL security has grown rapidly and several surveys exist, existing categorizations often fall short in guiding the selection of appropriate defenses for specific systems. In this work, we present a comprehensive survey of 86 recent studies on RL security, addressing these limitations by systematically categorizing attacks and defenses according to defined threat models and single- versus multi-agent settings. Furthermore, we examine the relevance and applicability of state-of-the-art attacks and defense mechanisms within the context of autonomous driving, providing insights to inform the design of robust RL systems.

papers.title: From Pre-Trends to Bounds: Robust Difference-in-Differences
papers.abstract: Difference-in-differences is a widely used method for estimating causal effects in non-experimental settings, relying on two key assumptions: the Parallel Trends (PT) assumption and the No-Anticipation Effects (No-AE) assumption. However, the validity of these assumptions are challenging to demonstrate empirically because they rely on unobservable quantities. This paper presents a unified framework that is robust to violations of either or both of these assumptions. By reinterpreting the PT assumption through the lens of selection bias, we introduce the concept of a robust difference-in-differences (RDID) estimand. We derive partial identification results for the Average Treatment Effect on the Treated under relaxed assumptions and characterize a misspecification-robust region based on minimum data-consistent relaxations of the standard model. Furthermore, our framework is extended to accommodate covariates and multiple post-treatment periods. We demonstrate the empirical importance of relaxing parallel trends and no anticipation assumptions with our proposed methods in three applications.

papers.title: Deciphering the role of Al$_2$O$_3$ formed during isothermal oxidation in a dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi$_{2.1}$ Eutectic High-Entropy Alloy
papers.abstract: In recent times,there has been a significant volume of work on Eutectic High Entropy Alloys (EHEAs) owing to their remarkable castability combined with excellent mechanical properties,which aids in clearing obstacles for their technological applications. One of the most common EHEAs,which has been of enormous interest at present, primarily owing to its solidification and tensile behavior, is AlCoCrFeNi$_{2.1}$. However,to aim for high-temperature applications,oxidation behaviour of material is one of the major aspects that needs to be extensively investigated.To this end,the present work aims to study the phases evolved during oxidation at elevated temperatures as high as 950 and 1000$^\circ$C in AlCoCrFeNi$_{2.1}$ using XRD and also to determine the rate law followed for isothermal oxidation of this alloy at 950 and 1000$^\circ$C,in order to understand the role of Al$_2$O$_3$ phase formed during isothermal oxidation at 950 and 1000$^\circ$C.

papers.title: Global-in-time L p -- L q estimates for solutions of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck equation
papers.abstract: In this work, we prove an optimal global-in-time $L^p \to L^q$ estimate for solutions to the Kramers-Fokker-Planck equation with short range potential in dimension three. Our result shows that the decay rate as t $\rightarrow$ +$\infty$ is the same as the heat equation in x-variables and the divergence rate as t $\rightarrow$ 0 + is related to the sub-ellipticity with loss of 1/3 derivatives of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator.

papers.title: Variance Reduction for Matrix Computations with Applications to Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: In addition to recent developments in computing speed and memory, methodological advances have contributed to significant gains in the performance of stochastic simulation. In this paper we focus on variance reduction for matrix computations via matrix factorization. We provide insights into existing variance reduction methods for estimating the entries of large matrices. Popular methods do not exploit the reduction in variance that is possible when the matrix is factorized. We show how computing the square root factorization of the matrix can achieve in some important cases arbitrarily better stochastic performance. In addition, we detail a factorized estimator for the trace of a product of matrices and numerically demonstrate that the estimator can be up to 1,000 times more efficient on certain problems of estimating the log-likelihood of a Gaussian process. Additionally, we provide a new estimator of the log-determinant of a symmetric positive-definite matrix where the log-determinant is treated as a normalizing constant of a probability density.

papers.title: Adversarial swarms as dynamical systems: a sharp outcome transition at population parity and short predictability horizons
papers.abstract: We study an agent-based model of two adversarial swarms as a dynamical system. Attackers seek a fixed goal while evading defenders; defenders are bound to the goal by a Morse potential and pursue attackers that enter a sphere of influence around it. Agents are self-propelled, interact through Morse and inverse-distance potentials, and are removed on contact, so every encounter ends with a dominant swarm. For 22 population ratios $N_A/N_D$ between 0.05 and 20 (1000 trials each), the probability that the attackers dominate jumps from 0.046 at $N_A/N_D = 1$ to 0.971 at 1.1, and both outcomes occur only for $0.24 \le N_A/N_D \le 1.33$. Without attrition, the center-of-mass motion of both swarms passes the 0-1 test for chaos at every ratio, the goal-bound defenders diverging faster and carrying more entropy. With attrition, twin trajectories differing by a $10^{-8}$ displacement separate to the swarm scale within 0.9 to 1.4 time units, and the displacement changes the winner in about 4% of trials near parity; before contact the attackers damp the perturbation and the defenders amplify it. Over the 22,000-trial ensemble the defenders' largest Lyapunov exponent is positive in 97 to 100% of trials across the contested band, whereas the attackers relax to a regular orbit once it resolves. A finite sensing radius leaves the outcomes far from parity unchanged but produces stand-offs near parity and, at the smaller radius, replaces attrition by fast breaches and stand-offs: the sharp transition is a property of long-range sensing.

papers.title: Nonabelian mirrors and Gromov-Witten invariants
papers.abstract: We propose quantum differential equations (QDEs) for periods of nonabelian mirror theories and develop an algorithm for constructing them directly from the mirrors. We verify the proposal by recovering known quantum differential equations of Grassmannians and Picard-Fuchs equations of Calabi-Yau complete intersections in Grassmannians. Our algorithm applies to a broad class of nonabelian GLSMs and yields new examples of quantum differential equations for several Fano varieties. The associated cohomology-valued generating functions can be extracted directly from these equations. Using them, we compute instanton numbers of both complete-intersection and non-complete-intersection Calabi-Yau manifolds, including the Pfaffian and Gulliksen--Negård Calabi-Yau threefolds. The resulting instanton numbers agree with all previously known computations, while the generating functions obtained for the non-complete-intersection examples are new.

papers.title: Quadratic Models for Engineered Control of Open Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: We introduce a framework to model the evolution of a class of open quantum systems whose environments periodically undergo an instantaneous non-unitary evolution stage. For the special case of quadratic models, we show how this approach can generalise the formalism of repeated interactions to allow for the preservation of system-environment correlations. Furthermore, its continuous zero-period limit provides a natural description of the evolution of small systems coupled to large environments in negligibly perturbed steady states. We explore the advantages and limitations of this approach in illustrative applications to thermalisation in a simple hopping ring and to the problem of initialising a qubit chain via environmental engineering.

papers.title: Firm Entry and Exit with Unbounded Productivity
papers.abstract: In Hopenhayn's (1992) entry-exit model productivity is bounded, implying that the predicted firm size distribution cannot match the power law tail observable in the data. In this paper we remove the boundedness assumption and, in this more general setting, provide an exact characterization of existence of stationary equilibria, as well as a novel sufficient condition for existence based on treating production as a Lyapunov function. We also provide new representations of the rate of entry and aggregate supply. Market clearing rules out stationary competitive equilibria at or below Zipf's law. Under monopolistic competition where the demand for each firm's variety bounds its sales, a stationary equilibrium exists for every tail index of productivity. In an example with additive preferences, unbounded markups inherit the Pareto tail of productivity.

papers.title: On Herman's Positive Entropy Conjecture
papers.abstract: We show that any area-preserving $C^r$-diffeomorphism of a two-dimensional surface displaying an elliptic fixed point can be $C^r$-perturbed to one exhibiting a chaotic island whose metric entropy is positive, for every $1\le r\le \infty$. This proves a conjecture of Herman stating that the identity map of the disk can be $C^\infty$-perturbed to a conservative diffeomorphism with positive metric entropy. This implies also that the Chirikov standard map for large and small parameter values can be $C^\infty$-approximated by a conservative diffeomorphisms displaying a positive metric entropy (a weak version of Sinai's positive metric entropy conjecture). Finally, this sheds light onto a Herman's question on the density of $C^r$-conservative diffeomorphisms displaying a positive metric entropy: we show the existence of a dense set formed by conservative diffeomorphism which either are weakly stable (so, conjecturally, uniformly hyperbolic) or display a chaotic island of positive metric entropy.

papers.title: Residue Automata Modulo $3^k$, Syracuse Random Variables, and Terminal-Branch Bias in Collatz Trajectories
papers.abstract: We study the residues modulo $3^k$ visited by trajectories of the accelerated Collatz map $T(n)=n/2$ ($n$ even), $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ ($n$ odd), starting from the six ``recurrent forms'' $9n+r$, $r\in\{1,2,4,5,7,8\}$. (i)~We give the exact transition automaton on these forms and its extension to every modulus $3^k$, and prove that for integers drawn from a complete residue system modulo $2^j3^k$ the first $j$ residues modulo $3^k$ form \emph{exactly} a Markov chain; its stationary law is Tao's Syracuse random variable, so the form $9n+8$ receives the fraction $22/63$ of all visits. (ii)~We determine the spectrum of this chain completely: its characteristic polynomial is $(x-1)\prod_{i=0}^{k-1}\bigl(x^{2\cdot 3^i}-4^{-3^i}\bigr)$, so every non-trivial eigenvalue has modulus exactly $\tfrac12$ for every $k$. We prove that the mixing time lies between $k\log_2\frac32$ and $2k+O(\sqrt{k})$, show that the stationary mass of the class $-1 \bmod 3^k$ is at least $\tfrac43 2^{-k}$, and present numerical evidence for a cutoff at $k\log_2 3$. (iii)~We explain the strong bias observed in the residue class of the first power of~$2$ met by a trajectory: this class is determined by the last odd term $q_k=(4^k-1)/3$ through $k \bmod 3$; three of the six classes contain only powers of~$2$, a fourth has $O(\log^2N)$ elements up to $N$, and the remaining two are unions of predecessor sets of the $q_k$. Computations for $n\le 4\times10^{9}$ give the frequencies $0.9761$ and $0.0239$. (iv)~We formulate an \emph{octave law}---the expected number of orbit points in $[y,2y)$ lying in a class $r \bmod 3^k$ tends to $\frac{2\log 2}{\log(4/3)}$ times the Syracuse probability of $r$---and support it by exhaustive and Monte Carlo computation.

papers.title: Light propagation in dielectric materials: a microscopic derivation of the refractive index and of the extinction theorem
papers.abstract: We present a compact, self-contained derivation of the field established inside a dielectric by an incident light wave, starting from the picture of the material as a collection of polarizable atoms (or molecules) in vacuum, each driven by the incident field and by the fields re-radiated by all the others. Following the integral-equation route of Goldberger and Watson, the same few lines of calculation yield the Lorentz local field, the Lorentz-Lorenz relation between the refractive index and the atomic polarizability, and the Ewald-Oseen extinction theorem: the incident wave is cancelled inside the medium by a field radiated by the induced dipoles and replaced by a wave travelling at $c/n$. The dilute limit is connected to the forward-scattering amplitude, the optical theorem and Rayleigh scattering. We then discuss, for a planar interface, in what sense reflection and refraction are a bulk effect for s-polarized light and a combination of bulk and surface (bound-charge) effects for p-polarized light, and why that surface term must not be confused with the local-field correction, although both stem from the same depolarization mathematics. Finally, a small coupled-dipole simulation of a random, finite collection of point dipoles checks the self-consistent local-field relation numerically. SI units are used throughout. The material is intended for an advanced undergraduate course on electromagnetism and optics.

papers.title: ThinkWAM: Rethinking Latent Futures for Action Refinement
papers.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) couple action generation with predictions of future states. An initial action chunk may be flawed. A future prediction that is not conditioned on the chunk is identical for every proposal and thus carries no proposal-specific signal, limiting its usefulness for refinement before execution. We introduce ThinkWAM, a latent WAM that establishes bidirectional feedback before execution through a proposal-rethink-refine loop: the policy first proposes a complete action chunk, the proposal corrects multi-horizon future latents through a learned residual, and the corrected latents are injected into a second pass of the same action head, which generates the executable chunk. An affordance-guided observation-action memory and a near-fine, far-coarse multi-horizon prediction scheme, both motivated by predictive coding, support this loop, and all prediction stays in latent space. ThinkWAM achieves 98.70% success on LIBERO, 84.76% on LIBERO-Plus without OOD fine-tuning, 85.75%/65.85% on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean/Random, and 65.17% on RoboCasa24. ThinkWAM achieves 64.4% mean success across three real-world OOD conditions. The mean two-pass inference latency per action chunk is 153.48 ms on LIBERO, 164.61 ms on RoboTwin, and 101.2 ms on the Galaxea A1Z. Ablations show complementary gains from rethinking and affordance guidance. Diagnostics indicate that proposal-conditioned corrections change both predicted futures and action trajectories, showing that the corrected future representations improve the final action.

papers.title: Unified Law for Visual Tasks (The Four Laws of Computer Vision)
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a Unified Law for Visual Tasks, which could be further divided into Four Laws of Computer Vision, with the goal of enabling a single framework or method to uniformly train on and perform nearly all visual tasks. Our starting point is an inspiration and hypothesis: if the world information is encoded into image, which we call World Snapshots, then image processing is world processing, and image generation is World Snapshot generation. Furthermore, if all visual and visualization tasks can be reformulated as generation tasks, then a unified method, World Snapshot Models (WSMs), can perform the vast majority of visual tasks, much as large language models have largely unified natural language processing. This paper validates these laws across more than 1,000 trained and evaluated visual tasks (defined by distinct input-output mappings) and presents a unified training framework for future visual-task research and applications.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Selector Advice and Oblivious Equilibrium Search
papers.abstract: Ko's tournament argument recognizes a P-selective language with quadratic advice. We determine the leading coefficient in the selector-query model. On $n$-bit inputs, $n^2/4+O(n)$ ordinary advice bits and $n$ nonadaptive comparisons suffice. Some cuts require $n^2/4-O(n\log n)$ bits even for randomized decoders with adaptive access to individual-degree-two extensions. At degree one the exact fixed advice width is $n+1$. Assuming exponential hardness in $\mathrm E$ against SAT-gate circuits, the quarter bound holds in deterministic polynomial time for every P-selective language. The same fixed point determines the cost of searching for an approximate equilibrium before seeing the payoffs. In an $N$-action symmetric constant-sum game with payoffs in $[0,1]$, let $P$ be the best worst-case probability that one game-independent proposal is an additive $ε$-Nash equilibrium. For each fixed $0<ε<1/2$, \[ -\log_2 P=(1+o(1))\, \frac{(\log_2 N)^2}{4[1-H_2(1/2+ε)]}. \] The algorithm draws uniform actions and proposes their empirical distribution for both players. The lower bound allows arbitrary mixed profiles and $N^{o(1)}$ adaptive payoff inspections before the proposal. For all symmetric two-player games, including general-sum games, the sharp exponent is $(\ln 2/8+o(1))(\log_2 N)^2/ε^2$ when $ε\to0$ and $\log(1/ε)=o(\log N)$. For security strategies in arbitrary zero-sum games the exponent is four times larger, and sampling an optimal strategy attains it. The common mechanism counts successful tuples. A fixed point makes them capture constant sampling probability while controlling a power moment of their distribution.

papers.title: Cameron--Martin theorem for SLE welding measures
papers.abstract: For $κ\in(0,4]$, we prove a Cameron--Martin theorem for the welding law induced by SLE$_κ$ loop measure. Under simultaneous left and right composition $h\mapsto\varphi\circ h\circψ^{-1}$, the transformed law is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to the original law exactly when both maps belong to the Weil--Petersson group, and is mutually singular otherwise. Thus the Weil--Petersson group is the quasi-invariance group of the welding law under composition on either side. We also prove that it is its own normalizer in the group of orientation-preserving circle homeomorphisms. For Weil--Petersson pairs, we derive an explicit Radon--Nikodym derivative in terms of a relative action well defined for SLE weldings and prove that it belongs to $L^{1+\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$ depending on the pair.

papers.title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
papers.abstract: Rules govern how player actions change interactive worlds. Different rules create distinct gameplay experiences within similar scenes and action spaces. For customizable gameplay, generative world models must follow user-defined rules beyond real-world behaviors. However, realizing user-defined rules presents two challenges: Rule-State Persistence and Rule-to-Visual Realization. The former requires preserving rule definitions, dependencies, and world states across saving and loading, so that restored worlds follow the established rules. The latter requires accurately realizing rule-induced changes on designated objects and attributes, particularly when affected objects are unseen. In this paper, we propose WorldRuler, which organizes rule definitions, dependencies, and object states in an executable 3D rule graph and connects rule execution, video generation, and perceptual feedback in a closed loop.
